Sports.title: Wigan pine for FA Cup glory as not even victory can lift them off foot of League One
Sports.content:
If the 2013 FA Cup final represented a blip for the Sheikh Mansour-era Manchester City in their quest for total domination of English football, it was a historic moment for their conquerors, Wigan Athletic. Memories of that famous day at Wembley still endure for Latics’ supporters despite the relegation from the Premier League that followed. Yet watching the modern-day Wigan, who remain bottom of League One despite a 1-0 win over Reading on Saturday, makes the toppling of City in a Cup final seem an epoch ago.

The club, perhaps understandably, continue to hark back to their halcyon days. Last season they brought back Gary Caldwell – club captain in 2013 – for his second stint as manager, having led the club to promotion from this division in 2015-16. Choosing to swap Exeter for a return to the Latics last season was seen as a risky move by Caldwell, considering the shoestring budget imposed upon him by Mike Danson, the owner who is keen to sell.

Finances are ultra-tight at the Greater Manchester club amid dwindling crowds and losses on the pitch and on the balance sheet. The local businessman Danson and his family saved Wigan from liquidation in June 2023 after mismanagement from previous owners brought a points deduction and relegation from the Championship. Three successive mid-table finishes in League One under their stewardship have brought a semblance of stability, but this season they have plummeted.

The problem is the Dansons have been unable to find an ambitious buyer to take the club to the next level. Now the prospect of a first season in the fourth tier since 1996-97 is a distinct possibility, although victory against Reading – the Latics’ second league win of the campaign, sealed by Scott Hogan’s 71st-minute strike – made the picture a little rosier.

View image in fullscreen Wigan fans cheer on their team during their win over Manchester City in the 2013 FA Cup final. Photograph: Shaun Botterill/Getty Images

“Some of our play was tremendous,” said Caldwell. “Our spirit, our character, our determination not to let the ball go in the net was fantastic. It was pretty stressful towards the end. We need to try and build on this. You have to keep the players believing and committing. There’s still so many aspects of our game that need to be better, but a result makes you feel better about yourself psychologically.”

The presence of Leam Richardson in the opposition dugout at the Brick Community Stadium gave fans more reason to reminisce about better days. Richardson, who claimed the League One title as Wigan manager in April 2022, was sacked in November of the same year just 16 days after signing a new three-year contract.

Caldwell has also found himself under pressure. The former centre-back has been criticised by fans for his team’s uninspiring style of play, which has produced just six goals in nine games, the fewest in League One. They went 447 minutes without a league goal until Hogan, the veteran forward, converted after the substitute Christian Saydee’s cross was parried out by the Reading goalkeeper, Joel Pereira.

And while Wigan’s keeper, Joe Whitworth, was regularly called into action to see out the win, the home side were still good value for three points, allowing Caldwell and his squad to breathe. The manager’s backers will rightly point to the lack of spending by the club in the summer, with the £1.5m generated by the sale of Sam Tickle to Bristol City not yet reinvested on players and an overreliance on young loanees to prop up the squad.

View image in fullscreen Wigan’s Christian Saydee applauds the fans after the 1-0 win over Reading. Photograph: Harry McGuire/CameraSport

Danson and the club’s hierarchy have issued rallying cries to supporters to return to the Brick Community Stadium in an effort to generate more revenue, thus making the club more appealing to new owners, but why should fans part with hard-earned cash to watch such insipid football?

Before the game, Caldwell had said: “We also recognise the need for points is big, for our supporters to have that feelgood factor, and be able to leave the stadium in a much better frame of mind than they have been.”

The Scot got what he needed against Reading, yet the sense of chaos above Caldwell was evidenced by the abrupt departure of Sarah Guilfoyle from her role as managing director on the eve of the new season, after a 10-year stay at the club. And there are plenty who feel the owners ought to bear the brunt of criticism. The Wigan Athletic Supporters Action Group is demanding answers from Danson on why selling the club has been such a struggle and the lack of investment. Other fans are more resigned to the idea that some short-term pain may be necessary for long-term gain; most agree a sale would be transformative.

For now, despite a rare victory over a hitherto in-form Reading, the short-term struggles look likely to continue. The hope is that a hero of 2013 can perform miracles on the pitch, despite the constraints off it.

Sports.title: Haaland helps Maresca achieve record start as Manchester City defeat Ipswich
Sports.content:
There have been few winners in Manchester City’s guilty verdict, except highly paid lawyers and the inflatable fruit industry. The fans have suffered, being forced to question everything they have been told, while being labelled “cheats”, but they were able to forget the cacophony of noise around the club as Enzo Maresca became the first Premier League manager to win his first seven games.

Ipswich were the latest victims, but they put up a fight in City’s first home Premier League game since being found to have breached financial rules. Defiance has fortified most of the City fanbase, who were able to see local boy Phil Foden instigate the triumph with a kiss of the badge, before an emblem of their wealth, Erling Haaland, secured the points to move six clear, albeit with a few scares between, courtesy of Daizen Maeda and Zian Flemming.

“I didn’t expect to win seven out of seven, but we are working well,” Maresca said. “This is the most important thing.”

Victory came at a cost as Haaland and Antoine Semenyo limped off at full-time, in addition to Mateo Kovacic, Matheus Nunes and Nico O’Reilly suffering injuries, although Maresca was left unsure of the severity as City prepare to host AEK Athens on Tuesday.

If City have felt like it has been their backs against the wall for the past few weeks, it was Ipswich’s turn. Gary O’Neil put 11 men behind the ball whenever the hosts ventured over the halfway line as City enjoyed 90% possession in the opening quarter-hour, but without truly threatening as they struggled to find space in the lowest of blocks, expertly organised and fully disciplined.

Maresca had made six changes to refresh the side and it took time to understand one another’s rhythm, with Ayyoub Bouaddi creating it from defensive midfield in another mature performance from the teenager making his first Premier League start.

View image in fullscreen Enzo Maresca has guided Manchester City a record seven-match winning start in the Premier League. Photograph: Michael Steele/Getty Images

It was inevitable what was coming as there was irrefutable evidence that City were dominant. As at Anfield, Jérémy Doku was a key instigator, showing mesmeric skill on the left of the area before finding Foden to sweep home for his first goal since mid-December.

“I know him from years ago, for me he’s one of the best Premier League players,” Maresca said. “Since day one, it’s my duty to help him to be again one of the best players. I’m very happy for his goal and hopefully it can be just the beginning of many goals and many good performances.”

There was an element of pantomime around the ground from the booing of the Premier League anthem, the singalongs and inflatables. It was fitting Marc Guéhi did not know Maeda was behind him, allowing the Ipswich man to latch on to a sublime curved through ball from Abdoul Ouattara and equalise two minutes after the opener.

Quick Guide Manchester City 3-2 Ipswich key facts Show • With Manchester City maintaining their 100% record, Enzo Maresca is the first manager to win his first seven Premier League games in charge of a team. • Manchester City are the third team to win their opening seven games of a Premier League season, after Liverpool in 2019-20 (first 8) and Chelsea in 2005-06 (first 9). • Erling Haaland (pictured) has now scored 100 non-penalty goals in the Premier League, reaching this milestone in fewer appearances than any other player (139). The previous fewest was 150 appearances, by Alan Shearer in 1996. Opta Photograph: Martin Rickett/PA Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

After a missed chance, Haaland showed it is possible to get a better result second time around, making the most of Kovacic becoming an auxiliary winger. The header lacked power, but Christian Walton could not keep it out, palming the ball from one hand to the other and into the net before Haaland was serenaded with the clap of bananas.

City found themselves stuck in a lull, unable to prise open Ipswich, instead having to bide their time. It was a test of patience and a sweeping move upfield concluded with a precision pass from Iliman Ndiaye and an aggressive finish from Haaland, who was later denied a hat-trick by the video assistant referee.

View image in fullscreen Manchester City fans have gone back to more innocent times with their inflatable bananas. Photograph: Simon Stacpoole/Offside/Getty Images

Farai Hallam reviewed footage of Guéhi taking out Abdul Fatawu in the area and Flemming did the rest in the 90th minute, as reward for an impressive team performance, leaving O’Neil upset Ipswich departed with nothing.

“They’re an incredible group,” he said. “Players giving everything. It’s a privilege to stand there and represent them because they’re an incredible group.”

City were left to complain about a Premier League official’s decision when 12 minutes was added on, with few knowing why, but this result will not be questioned.

Maresca called on his team to make their own noise while a cacophony swirls around them, but on-pitch success will not speak louder while what is happening off it is unresolved. The fans sang about relegation and trips to Stockport, embracing a dark situation with humour to match.

Sports.title: Championship roundup: West Ham go second; Norwich beaten again
Sports.content:
Nuno Espírito Santo was delighted West Ham finished a “demanding week” by toppling Championship leaders Swansea.

Divine Mukasa’s first-half strike in front of a record Swansea.com Stadium crowd of 20,973 gave the Hammers a 1-0 win and took them into second place and within a point of the league leaders. It was their second success in four days after a 6-0 romp at Lincoln, and ended a week that began with a 1-1 home draw against QPR following Jarrod Bowen’s last-gasp penalty miss.

“We wanted not only to keep the momentum, but to build on it,” said Nuno. “It was a very demanding week in terms of the opponents we had to face, but it finished really well due to the hard work of the boys. The commitment, the unity and the way they played was really good against a very good Swansea side. It was a very intense.”

Kim Hellberg defended his decision to rest Will Lankshear against Cardiff after the division’s top scorer came off the bench to rescue a point for Middlesbrough. Lankshear, who took his tally to 10 for the season in all competitions midweek, was rested him for the visit of the Bluebirds. That selection backfired as Cardiff stunned Boro with two first-half goals from Jack Moylan and Ollie Tanner. Lankshear was then introduced at half-time and inspired a fightback, levelling for Boro with his 11th goal of the campaign after Tommy Conway had halved the deficit.

View image in fullscreen Will Lankshear’s goal saved a point for Middlesbrough. Photograph: Richard Sellers/PA

“You need to manage your players in this league and look into numbers,” said Hellberg. “We have a lot of players that have no pre-season. Will is one of those who came late and has been doing a lot of good things. He’s been absolutely brilliant and sometimes you need to also protect him.”

Liam Millar scored twice as Birmingham beat QPR 3-0 at St Andrew’s. Millar swung the game Birmingham’s way in the 27th minute and then doubled their advantage just after the break. On both occasions he was assisted by Tomoki Iwata while Demarai Gray added the gloss in the first minute of stoppage time by hammering a pull-back by fellow substitute Luis Vázquez into the top corner.

Quick Guide League One roundup: Bradford go top; Plymouth lose Show Bradford moved top of League One with their first home win under Michael Duff, as Plymouth slipped up against Huddersfield. The Bantams, who appointed Duff as manager earlier this month following the departure of Graham Alexander, claimed a 2-0 home win over Stevenage thanks to goals inside the last 11 minutes from Antoni Sarcevic and substitute Will Swan. That proved enough to put them a point clear at the top, with previous front-runners Plymouth going down 2-0 at home to Huddersfield and dropping to fourth in the process. The Terriers climbed above their opponents into third after strikes from Derensili Sanches Fernandez and Bojan Radulovic. Stockport climbed to second, edging out Bromley 1-0 with Kyle Wootton on target, while Robbie Savage’s first home league game in charge of Peterborough ended in a 2-2 draw with Burton. It looked as if Gbemi Arubi’s 89th-minute wonderstrike had earned Albion their first win in three, but Matt Garbett responded with a 96th minute leveller to snatch his side a point. Savage started his time at London Road with a 3-1 win at Leicester last Saturday. Aaron Collins scored the winner as MK Dons beat Luton 2-1 to claim a first league victory of the season. Alex Gilbey fired the Dons ahead with a fine strike before Jordan Clark equalised for the visitors. But Collins’s penalty won the match to condemn Luton to a third defeat in their past four games. Under-pressure Leicester manager Russell Martin celebrated a badly needed win, seeing off visiting Doncaster 2-1 – with Warren O’Hara’s 84th-minute own-goal causing some late tension. Cambridge kept pace with the promotion hopefuls after Shayne Lavery grabbed the winner in added time to leave Barnsley with a 2-1 win, while Sheffield Wednesday eased to a 5-0 win over AFC Wimbledon – Davis Keillor-Dunn with a double. Bottom club Wigan registered a first league win since 2 September, Scott Hogan with the only goal against Reading. Notts County lost 2-0 at Wycombe and Leyton Orient beat Blackpool 2-0. Press Association Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Luke Graham scored his first goal for Stoke as they won 1-0 at Pride Park to pile more pressure on struggling Derby. The Scotland defender headed in a free-kick early in the second half and that was enough to settle a scrappy contest. Derby, who are missing a number of key players, battled away and nearly snatched a point when David Ozoh’s shot was superbly saved by goalkeeper Viktor Johansson.

West Brom completed a stunning comeback after conceding two early goals as they beat Blackburn 3-2. Andri Gudjohnsen had Rovers two up before the break, before Barney Stewart pulled a goal back for Albion. Isaac Price’s penalty levelled it up before the substitute Felix Horn Myhre netted a dramatic winner for the home side a minute from time.

James Bree, Lewis Dobbin and Léo Scienza all squandered chances as Southampton dropped points at home for the first time this season with a 0-0 draw against Bolton. The trio all wasted tap-ins, while Saints were also left bereft by a penalty not being given for a Rúben Rodrigues handball.

View image in fullscreen Luca Kjerrumgaard enjoys his crucial opener for Watford against Charlton. Photograph: Ben Peters/Focus Images Ltd/Shutterstock

Watford lifted the pressure on Alessio Dionisi and quelled their supporters’ rebellion against the owner, Gino Pozzo, with a deserved 2-0 win against a sluggish Charlton. After shipping nine goals in defeats by Burnley and Cardiff, Watford had slumped into the bottom three and the fans had turned their anger on Pozzo. But goals from Luca Kjerrumgaard and the substitute Jordan Zemura extended Charlton’s worrying run to eight games without a win as they were booed off at Vicarage Road.

Dionisi said later his team was “not yet strong enough for the Championship but it’s possible to improve. I’ve been a coach for 14 years and I know when my team stays near my idea. This result is important and tonight I will drink a glass of red wine.”

Portsmouth piled on the misery for struggling Norwich as they made it back-to-back Championships victories with a 1-0 win at Carrow Road. Pompey followed up their midweek victory against Sheffield United with a hard-fought success in East Anglia, with a 51st-minute penalty from striker Marezi settling the issue.

It was a sixth successive league defeat for the hosts and there were calls for the sporting director Ben Knapper to go from frustrated supporters at the final whistle.

Norwich’s head coach, Philippe Clement, had no complaints with his side’s effort – but felt they sometimes failed to see the bigger picture on the pitch.

“I am very disappointed, very frustrated,” he said. “I saw a lot of passion out there, a lot of effort, but not enough overview. It’s about getting the balance right between their hearts and their brains. I understand the frustration of our fans and all I can say is that I will work even harder than I did last season to turn it around.”

View image in fullscreen Portsmouth’s Marezi celebrates on another bleak day for Norwich. Photograph: Stephen Pond/Getty Images

Jake Cooper’s scrambled equaliser rescued a point for Millwall as they came from two goals down to draw 2-2 with Lincoln. The visitors looked on course to put Wednesday’s 6-0 home thrashing against West Ham behind them in style when goals from Andrei Coubiș and Rob Street put them in a strong position after 33 minutes at the Den. But Millwall were able to prevent back-to-back home defeats with a much-improved second-half performance, and the visitors were hanging on for a share of the spoils after having Deji Elerewe sent off soon after Cooper’s leveller. Kyrell Lisbie had scored Millwall’s first.

Quick Guide League Two roundup: Salford make it five in a row Show League Two pacesetters Salford made it five wins in a row in the fourth tier as Macaulay Langstaff scored twice in a 2-1 success over bottom side Crawley. Barnet and Crewe remain close by just a point further back. Barnet came from behind to beat Tranmere 2-1, Kabongo Tshimanga scoring both, and Crewe defeated Rochdale 3-2. York were held to a 1-1 draw at Newport after going down to 10 men but Shrewsbury held on 1-0 against Bristol Rovers despite two red cards in the last 10 minutes. Ian Holloway’s Swindon are now eight games without a win in all competitions after a 1-1 draw with Walsall, Oldham eased to a 4-1 result against Cheltenham and Port Vale edged Chesterfield 1-0. Ten-man Grimsby went down 2-0 to Northampton, Accrington took a 3-1 win over Gillingham, strugglers Rotherham lost 2-0 at Fleetwood and there was a goalless draw between Colchester and Exeter. Press Association Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Oliver Arblaster’s early strike and a strong defensive display saw Sheffield United take all three points from a 1-0 victory over Bristol City at Ashton Gate. The visitors took a fifth-minute lead when a headed clearance fell to Arblaster, who connected with a sweet right-footed volley from just outside the box which gave the City goalkeeper Sam Tickle no chance. It proved enough to settle a contest high on endeavour but low on entertainment from which the Blades emerged worthy winners.

Wrexham eased the pressure on Phil Parkinson with a 4-1 win over rock-bottom Preston. Joe Worrall scored his first goal in more than two years and, after Alfie Devine briefly brought Preston level, the former Lilywhites midfielder Ben Whiteman struck next to score his first goal in Wrexham colours. Sam Smith gave the hosts breathing space just before the hour and Kieffer Moore killed it off moments later.

In a week that had seen former Liverpool captain Steven Gerrard linked with the manager’s job, Wrexham’s third league win of the season was a vital one as they moved up to 14th. But Preston remain stuck on four points from 11 games, with Graham Alexander having lost his first three games in charge.

Sports.title: Former heavyweight world title contender boxer dies 'suddenly' aged 40: Denis Boytsov, once set to fight Tyson Fury, was unable to speak for 11 years after mysterious 'attack'
Sports.content:
A former world No 2 heavyweight boxer once primed to fight Tyson Fury has died aged just 40, after 11 years of care following an 'attack' in which the perpetrators were never found.

Russian Denis Boytsov pulled out of a fight with Fury in December 2012 and was considered the world's second-best heavyweight behind Wladimir Klitschko. He had a 36-1 record when his career was cut short in 2015.

Boytsov suffered serious head injuries in a Berlin subway tunnel and had to be placed into a medically induced coma because of swelling on the brain.

A statement on the boxer's website suggested he was the victim of an attack linked to his boxing career. 'It is possible that this attack was linked to the boxer's sporting activity,' the statement said. 'Around two years ago, Boytsov was receiving threats constantly.'

His wife Olga Litvinova was left deeply upset and suggested Boytsov may have been the victim of an attempted 'assassination' after that series of threats.

Now, 11 years on, Boytsov's family have revealed he died 'suddenly' this week after many years in care. His father says the cause of death was a detached blood clot.

Russian boxer Denis Boytsov died this week from a detached blood clot at home

Boystov is pictured in his boxing gear in hospital after the 'attack' on him in 2015

'A blood clot broke off,' Nikolai Boytsov told Russian news agency TASS. 'There was nothing they could do; it was instant death. Three minutes and that was it.

'This happened at home. His wife fed him and started turning him to the side. He suddenly broke down, started shaking, turned blue. And his whole life was over.'

Brother Maxim Boytsov revealed Denis had been unable to speak in the 11 years following the Berlin incident. Boytsov underwent extensive treatment in Germany and then back in his homeland.

'No, we didn't communicate. He just nodded yes and no. But he understood everything. I courted him for ten years. But it didn't work out,' said Maxim.

Boytsov's funeral is set for today in the Russian region of Oryol.

British former heavyweight boxer David Price - who once beat Fury in 2005 - revealed Boytsov's punching power was much stronger than that of Anthony Joshua, having trained with both.

Boytsov's wife Olga was by his side as he died in Russia this week

Boytsov was due to fight Tyson Fury in 2012 and was considered a top heavyweight fighter

'I sparred a Russian called Denis Boytsov in Germany once. He only hit the top of my head, but he was a powerful puncher,' Price told the Daily Star.

'I think he got his career cut short, he got absolutely battered and left for dead, he couldn't fight again. But I remember him being a really powerful puncher.'

Sports.title: Britain's only female boxing referee faces backlash as she REFUSES to accept fighter's towel being thrown in twice - moments before technical knockout by a brutal headshot at the O2 Arena
Sports.content:
It is the best-known sign of submission in sport - but a boxing referee at the O2 Arena on Saturday night twice refused to accept a heavyweight fighter 'throwing in the towel' before he was brutally beaten.

Heavyweights Adam Olaniyan and Dan Garber were fighting in London on the undercard of Daniel Dubois' victory over Fabio Wardley - with Bradford fighter Garber, 41, beaten by technical knockout (TKO) in the second round.

But focus after the fight has instead been on referee Amy Pu, after she allowed Garber to undergo more punishing headshots even after his team had tried to stop the fight. Pu, the UK's first and only female professional boxing referee, kicked a towel thrown by Garber's team out of the ring to allow the fight to continue.

Garber had been dismayed by his team's attempts to submit and Pu elected to continue on with the fight. Seconds later, Olaniyan, 20, unleashed a flurry of further punches which sent Garber to the canvas to end the contest. Garber's team had thrown in another towel but that was also ignored before Pu stopped the punishment.

Garber could be seen receiving oxygen ringside after the fight.

It is rare for referees to overrule the decision of the boxer's corner to end a bout but is allowed within the sport's rules. British Boxing Board of Control (BBBofC) regulations state that the towel does not automatically end a fight and referees are left with the authority on when to do so.

Referee Amy Pu finally steps in to end Adam Olaniyan's fight against Dan Garber on Saturday

Garber's team twice tried to throw in the towel to stop the fight but Pu refused the submission

But fans were unimpressed by Pu's decision-making, with footage of her kicking the white towel out of the ring going viral after being posted by broadcasters DAZN.

'Ref nearly got dan garber killed. Kicking the towel out idiot,' one viewer wrote on X.

Another fan said: 'Dan Garber receiving oxygen after referee Amy Pu inexplicably refuses the corner's towel and allows Olaniyan to pile more damage in. Rules should be changed to make the towel coming in an automatic fight ended. Refs don't know what's been happening in the gym.'

And another picked apart Pu's record, writing: 'Bbbofc referee Amy Pu has been mostly terrible all night, two stoppages called earlier than they needed to be, kicking the towel out to let Dan Garber take more punishment, this is not new for her.'

Originally from Taiwan, Pu took up boxing in her 30s in London and later became a professional referee in 2024. She has spoken about isolated issues of suffering from racism and sexism in the male-dominated world of boxing.

'On the professional side, I have to say the reaction has mostly been really positive,' Pu told the BBC earlier this year. 'During the amateur days, there were some odd comments and stuff. I think one of the hesitations I had before turning professional was also for that reason.

'People have just been so supportive, knock on wood, I haven't really had any criticism directed at me because of my sex or because of my race.

'I'm really grateful and I hope that it continues, that people should see me as a referee. They can give me stick as a referee, not as a female Asian referee.'

Rising star Olaniyan's record now stands at 5-0 in his short professional career, while Garber has 14 victories to 10 defeats.

Garber, for his part, did not appear disappointed with Pu's decision-making. Writing after the fight on Facebook - instead focusing on the money he had made and being able to 'buy a third house'.

He said: 'What an experience, took the fight last week and we knew what we was up against but no excuses.

'Maybe this is the end now for me, time waits for no-one. Bought 2 houses out of boxing and tonight gets me a 3rd, it’s been a massive part of my life. If it is the end then what a way to go out in front of 20,000.'

Sports.title: Revealed: The day Roy Keane squared up to poppy protest footballer James McClean in half-time f-word rant about his photo with an Irish boxer
Sports.content:
Revealed: The day Roy Keane squared up to poppy protest footballer James McClean in half-time f-word rant about his photo with an Irish boxer

Poppy protest footballer James McClean has opened up on an explosive clash he had with Roy Keane during his international career with the Republic of Ireland.

McClean, 37, won 103 caps for his country between 2012 and 2023, and came across Keane while the former Man United hardman was assistant manager to Martin O'Neill from 2013 to 2018.

And, writing in his autobiography The Walls, as serialised in the Irish Independent, McClean reflected on what it was like to work with Keane.

Noting that there were a few 'outbursts' and 'flare-ups', the winger revealed how they had a bust-up at half-time of a post-season friendly against Mexico in New Jersey in June 2017.

It was a game that Ireland lost 3-1 after an under-strength team struggled to cope with their opponents as several players, including McClean - who was captain and at left-wing back - were playing out of position.

'Martin had just finished his bit when Roy came over, got right in my face and started f***ing me out of it,' recalled McClean.

James McClean opened up on a brutal bust-up he had with Roy Keane on international duty

Keane was incensed after McClean posed on the pitch with Irish boxer Michael Conlan

‘"Look at you, the f***ing captain, f***ing giving off, yeah? You were taking pictures before the game with f***ing Mick Conlan. Your head isn’t f***ing on it".'

McClean explained that following the pre-match warm-up he had posed for a photo on the side of the pitch with Michael Conlan, an Irish professional boxer who was a friend of his, after which he 'saw Roy staring over'.

McClean, who had given away a penalty in the first half, didn't hit back at Keane at the time, but inside he was 'spewing over it for the entire flight home' and tried to nip the issue in the bud.

Keane initially 'brushed it off' before he visited McClean in his room while he was doing a gym session.

McClean added: 'I sat on the bed as he leaned on the desk table and went off on another one. He accused me of having a big ego.

'He said he’d never been critical of me in the press or around the group, and now, the first time he’d said anything, I’d pulled him up over it. Then he started going off about the Lamborghini at Sunderland, which was f***ing six years earlier. I was thinking he must have been seething for the afternoon, gathering information.'

The Lamborghini reference was in relation to McClean's time at Sunderland when O'Neill, then managing the Black Cats, had allegedly dropped the winger after he found out about him buying a 'f***ing three-hundred-grand' supercar.

The clash came at half-time of Ireland's 3-1 defeat by Mexico in a summer friendly in June 2017

In their conversation, Keane also admitted he often went 'home and screamed into the pillow' because the 'standard was so poor' in training during his time with Ireland.

After defending his attitude in a tete-a-tete with Keane, McClean outlined his respect for the assistant boss and how much he cared about playing for his country.

McClean continued: 'He said the photos didn’t look like good preparation. I disagreed, and it went around in circles a bit until we just said we’d leave it.

'Roy was sound with me after that; I knew he couldn’t have any complaints with my performances. I scored in our next match, a friendly with Uruguay, and did a selfie celebration afterwards to make my point.'

Sports.title: Richarlison backs criticism of Roberto De Zerbi in another pointed social media post before Tottenham boss responds - as rift deepens amid star's exile
Sports.content:
Exiled Tottenham star Richarlison has shared a pointed social media post where he backed criticism of Roberto De Zerbi. Richarlison, 29, was set to depart north London this summer after appearing to fall out with the Spurs boss, who claimed the forward 'said too many times he wants to leave'. A move never materialised, however, and the Brazilian has been kept out of the first-team squad since. His omission comes at a time where Spurs are struggling at the bottom of the Premier League after scoring just three goals in six games, and Richarlison shared a post on his Instagram story of quotes from former Everton striker Duncan Ferguson. Speaking on The Overlap Daily about the Brazilian, Ferguson had said: 'You don’t leave a player like that out unless there’s been a real murder: he’s chinned him or there’s been a proper scrap on the training ground.' Sharing the quotes, Richarlison added: 'Thanks Duncan Ferguson, you are right.' Richarlison shared a pointed social media post where he backed criticism of Roberto De Zerbi Richarlison has been exiled from Tottenham's squad after appearing to fall out with De Zerbi Ferguson was a coach and two-time interim boss at Everton during Richarlison's four-year spell at the club, yet De Zerbi was unmoved when pressed on the 29-year-old's latest actions at his pre-match conference ahead of Monday's game against Coventry. 'It's not my problem anymore,' he said. 'You have to ask Vinai (Venkatesham, CEO) or Johan (Lange, technical director). It's not my problem. 'I know as a coach I have to support and take responsibility even when it's not my responsibility. 'I have not decided anything in this situation. If he wants to speak to me he can find me in my office until 8.30pm in the evening. 'But I don't want to speak any more because my focus is on the Coventry game.' Richarlison's latest post comes after he also took to social media within hours of Tottenham's 3-2 defeat by Aston Villa last month to post videos of himself training in what was interpreted as a pointed move at the time. He captioned the video of him undertaking drills: 'The focus remains'. His second post was another clip of him undergoing sprint training, accompanied by the caption: '35.4km/h - I broke my record'. Meanwhile, Richarlison made his first appearance since his exile on Tuesday for Tottenham's Under-21 side in the EFL Trophy against Cheltenham Town. The Brazilian scored Spurs' equaliser against the League Two outfit, and also notched in the subsequent penalty shoot-out as they lost 7-6 on spot kicks after a 2-2 draw in normal time in the group stage clash. 'Happy to do what I love most in life. I was missing it!', Richarlison shared on social media following the match. Richarlison made his on-pitch return for Spurs' Under-21 side against Cheltenham on Tuesday Richarlison, who will be without first-team football until January given he is not in Spurs' Premier League squad and they have also been knocked out of the Carabao Cup, was praised post-match by Cheltenham manager Steve Cotterill. Cotterill told reporters that he felt the Brazilian's attitude was 'absolutely first class' when featuring against the League Two side. ‘I thought his attitude tonight was immaculate,' Cotterill said. 'He could have easily come down here and thought I ain’t too bothered about tonight, he could have done that. 'He’s used to playing in front of 60,000 every week, his attitude tonight was absolutely first class and it was great for our lads to play against someone of his stature.’

Sports.title: Emiliano Martinez update: Chelsea's goalkeeper undergoes surgery and set to be out for weeks - but wife says it's 'nothing serious' after sickening collision at Everton
Sports.content:
Emiliano Martinez underwent successful minor surgery after his sickening collision with Everton's Jarrad Branthwaite with Chelsea's goalkeeper set for weeks on the sidelines.

Xabi Alonso's men secured their first clean sheet of the Premier League season with the help of Martinez, who was injured while bravely coming to clear a 67th-minute set-piece. He was then replaced by 21-year-old Mike Penders for the remainder of Chelsea's 2-0 victory.

The operation was believed to be for a jaw injury after Martinez had been carried away on a stretcher and taken to hospital. He was conscious as he left the Hill Dickinson Stadium.

The 34-year-old Argentinian later released a statement from his hospital bed in which he wrote: 'Thanks to everyone for the messages, the operation went well. The most important thing is that we won and with a bow at 0 (goals). We'll be back in a few weeks.'

His wife, Mandinha, added it is 'nothing serious' and that he will 'soon be back to normal'.

Between now and the November international break, Chelsea have to face Tottenham Hotspur at home (Premier League), Liverpool away (Carabao Cup), Manchester United at home (Premier League), and Sunderland away (Premier League).

Chelsea star Emiliano Martinez's wife says his sickening head injury is 'nothing serious'

The Argentine goalkeeper's agent posted a positive update in a photo from hospital

Penders, the Belgian who arrived this summer after a season on loan with Strasbourg, will fill in as Chelsea's No 1 in the meantime. His potential is high, though this will see him promoted earlier than expected as Alonso had been keen for his goalkeeper to carry experience.

A Chelsea statement released on Sunday morning read: 'Goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez has undergone successful surgery on a fractured jaw.

'Martinez was injured following a collision midway through the second half of our 2-0 victory over Everton at the Hill Dickinson Stadium on Saturday.

'Martinez was taken to hospital for further assessment, which confirmed a fractured jaw that required surgery.

'Everyone at Chelsea wishes Emi a speedy recovery and will support him throughout.'

Penders had gone into this season hoping to become Chelsea's first-choice goalkeeper when he thought he would be competing with Robert Sanchez.

Martinez was struck in a sickening collision during Chelsea's win away at Everton

However, mistakes made in Chelsea's opening game of the season away at Fulham led to Sanchez hastily being loaned to Como, the Italian side managed by Cesc Fabregas.

Martinez was signed for £7.5million from Aston Villa as Sanchez's replacement on a three-year contract, which, in Penders' mind per sources, pushed him further away from the starting line-up.

Circumstances will now see the 6ft 7in youngster get his chance to show Alonso and everyone else how ready he is as Chelsea goalkeeping coach Ben Roberts prepares him for playing rivals Tottenham at Stamford Bridge this Saturday.

Penders did well in handling being thrown in at Everton, coming to clear one cross towards the back of his box which the away end appreciated and navigating the extra 13 minutes added on to the end of the game. Teddy Sharman-Lowe, 23, will act as Penders' back-up.

Sports.title: Stunned inside 17 SECONDS and over in two rounds: Brutal Daniel Dubois was explosive in deciding his Fabio Wardley rematch and is now the undisputed champion-elect, writes JEFF POWELL MBE
Sports.content:
To hell with the romance. Stuff the slow starts. Never mind most of the O2 shouting against him.

Daniel Dynamite Dubois exploded into the ring with such power and brutality that he might have sent a tsunami along the Thames.

What he did beyond doubt last night, and what cannot be contested by Fabio Wardley or the three other world heavyweight belt wearers, was announce himself as the undisputed champion-elect.

White-collar Wardley was disabused of any notion he might regain the WBO title he lost to Dubois five months ago.

He was stunned in 17 seconds by Dubois's first booming right-hander of a red-hot night. And so the pain continued unabated.

'Fabio is a great boy, coming in for the second time, but it was my time, and my era,' said Dubois. 'I had my intentions, bad intentions, from the beginning.'

Daniel Dubois brutalised Fabio Wardley in their rematch as he wrapped things up in two rounds

This time there was no delay in Wardley's corner throwing in the towel. No point in the referee delaying the inevitable.

Dubois's sledgehammer blows rained down like missiles, with none travelling in the opposite direction.

One of the rival world champions was here to see the ferocity in person. Filip Hrgovic, who had disposed of Moses Itauma recently, sounded somewhat shell-shocked.

Agit Kabayel may be in no rush to meet Dubois. Nor, perhaps, will the winner of December's WBA clash between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua.

This was an enormous statement by a man whose courage had been questioned but who will now be favourite to hunt them all down in his quest for the succession to Oleksandr Usyk as the undisputed champion.

'I'm the champion now, and I want to get some big fights in,' said Dubois. 'At this stage in my career, big money, big fights.'

The next generation of heavyweights has arrived.

So the irresistible force and the immovable object came to blows again at the O2. Dubois had risen from the canvas twice in the spring to claim his second world heavyweight title. Wardley, who neglected to finish him off, paid such a bloodied price that he left us wondering how he had stayed on his feet.

After being dropped in the opening seconds in their first fight, Dubois delivered revenge this time around

Their mutual hammering in Manchester had left us greedily wanting more at the O2.

Both pledged to put the savagery on after-burner second time around. Forget the concerns for their health.

In the parlance of the first promotion, Don't Blink was the warning to all those in attendance. These two had spent their careers knocking people out for fun or sometimes being stopped themselves.

No one expected this fight to go the distance. Not the fighters themselves. 'Me early,' predicted Dubois. 'Me earlier,' said Wardley.

'Twelve rounds?' opined promoter Frank Warren. 'No chance.'

The majority of the crowd were with the underdog, roaring Wardley into the ring. Partly from their feeling for romance, with a white-collar boxer breaking into the highest echelons of the heavyweights.

Dynamite Daniel's reception was more subdued. Even a hint hostile. Wardley hoped for a first-round knockdown, but that went to Dubois.

The first right of the night had Fabio reeling on the ropes for an eight count. More hell followed.

Dubois may have found greatness and is the undisputed champion-elect in the next generation of heavyweights

It was all over in round two. Wardley was brave as always, but his corner could not let him keep taking sledgehammer blows without reply.

'I just came in and I didn't execute the game plan properly,' Wardley admitted. 'I hold my hands up to that; that is entirely down to me.'

'A little white-collar boy like me could never have dreamed like this,' he added, reflecting on a sold-out O2 despite defeat.

Dubois may have found greatness with this mammoth performance.

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola is using his own weapons to win games and Liverpool's £400m attack is finally heading in the right direction as Alexander Isak emerges as the Reds' most important player, writes LEWIS STEELE
Sports.content:
The calculators were out at the Gtech Community Stadium. A quick maths lesson in the media room before kick-off deduced that Liverpool’s front four cost a whopping £399.5million. The quartet of Alexander Isak (£125m), Bradley Barcola (£123m), Florian Wirtz (£116m) and Victor Munoz (£35.5m) had started just one game together before and that, a home match against Fulham, ended in a goalless draw. So the knives would have been out if those had blanked and the Reds had left a bitterly cold west London armed with anything but three points. This is a tricky place to go and many big teams falter on this turf but, given they started the weekend nine points behind the league leaders, this was must-win for Andoni Iraola. In the end, Wirtz threaded in Munoz for a splendid goal to equalise, then Barcola picked out Isak to finish for 2-1. Any narratives about Liverpool’s big-money flops were put on hold – for now at least – and, instead, the away fans could toast to their awesome foursome. Liverpool's clash with Brentford was a must-win for Andoni Iraola - and his side delivered The prolific and ruthless forward line does not tell the full story of this game. Far from it. For large parts, Liverpool were stodgy and, had Brentford not gone down to 10 men late in the first half, this could have easily ended up a completely different outcome. These things even themselves out over the course of the season, we are often told, and after being left aggrieved at Ryan Gravenberch’s red card that ruined their chances last week, this time they were left thankful for Yehor Yarmolyuk’s bizarre headbutt and subsequent sending off. Until then, the Reds were looking vulnerable and at risk of falling to the same fate they suffered on this ground last year, when Brentford bullied Arne Slot’s side and exploited many weaknesses. Some of those issues are still clear but Iraola is now using his own weapons to help win games. Last year, Liverpool could not hurt teams and then were too flimsy at the other end. The chief reason for this is Isak, all £125m of him. His goal was his fifth of the season which sees him surpass last term’s tally already. Without his goals, Liverpool would be six points worse off and in the bottom half. That might be a stretch but his brace in a 2-0 win at Ipswich, strike in a 1-0 victory at Bournemouth and now the match-winning goal in this 2-1 triumph has helped three tricky away trips turn from draws to wins. With him fit last Sunday against Manchester City, who knows whether the Reds would have taken one of their early chances at 0-0 and made the game an alternative spectre. Alexander Isak scored the winner at Brentford. He is not Liverpool's best player - but he is their most important Bradley Barcola may have been wasteful at time but he dazzled again after his Champions League hat-trick Isak is the sort of player who can drift in and out of games. But that is what the best strikers do — just think of the amount of time Sky Sports have highlighted Erling Haaland’s lack of touches only for the Norwegian to make them look silly by winning the game with his next shot. The Swede, then, may not be Liverpool’s best player but he is certainly their most important. Three match-winners already this term, one can only wonder how different last season might have been if this instinctive poacher was fit all year. His fitness is still questionable and it would not be a surprise to see him rested for Tuesday’s Champions League match against Villarreal for that reason. Isak scored the winner but the supporting cast in attack also caught the eye. Munoz, the lesser-heralded of the star forwards, scored a fine goal from the right-hand side at a time when it felt Brentford were starting to settle into playing with 10 men. Rio Ngumoha, a substitute, is also worthy of praise and he was a contender for man of the match. Against stubborn defences like this opposition, the 18-year-old’s unorthodox style is devastating and a real tool. Barcola was wasteful but still dazzled at times. The Frenchman had clearly left his shooting boots in Austria and looked shaky in front of goal after his midweek hat-trick at LASK, but this was another notable performance, including an assist. He was at the heart of everything, as was Wirtz. The German has been criticised this week — some of it harsh, most of it fair enough — but this was a metronomic display, creating nine chances which is more than any Liverpool player on record in a Premier League fixture. More of this from the attackers and Iraola knows the possibilities are endless, though he would have boarded the flight home knowing his team remains a work in progress. With a full contingent of players, Brentford would have been a good bet to get at least a point, and Iraola might worry at how many times the Bees got in behind his defence in the first half. There are also battle scars with Dominik Szoboszlai and Jeremie Frimpong set for ‘some time’ on the sidelines with muscular injuries. It is unclear how serious either are with the duo set for scans in the next 24 hours. But despite the fitness worries and minor teething problems that still need solving, the Liverpool boss can raise a glass knowing his £400m attack is heading in the right direction. With Isak et al on form and remaining fit, the Reds can prosper this year.

Sports.title: Man City charges LIVE: Points deduction timeframe as appeal 'decision date' predicted
Sports.content:
Football finance expert Kieran Maguire has claimed Manchester City must be deduced "multiple double figures of points" after breaching Premier League financial rules.

Maguire said: "The redacted report sets out year by year how much the sham contracts contributed to the artificial commercial revenue. Over the rolling three-year period, in some years we could be talking about a £350million difference. That would shatter all records for PSR compliance.

"Everton and Nottingham Forest's deductions covered a single breach in a single year, an overspend of no more than £20million. So is there a ceiling on what can be deducted? And the sanctions hearing could already have taken place. Because City are appealing and everyone has NDAs, we might not know the sanction until the appeal result. But it has to be multiple double figures of points, before you start the calculations.

"I worked out that if you add up nine years of Champions League non-participation for individual clubs at an average of £50million a time, around £20million for the Europa League, plus potential claims from players who missed bonuses, the Premier League's legal fees and a fine, we're talking in excess of a billion pounds regardless of the points deduction.

When asked about the possibility of City being kicked out of the Premier League, Maguire responded: "I think it would be a very unusual vote. We did see Bury get expelled from League Two some time ago but I think that the other clubs would have to bear in mind that Manchester City would probably take legal redress and that could prove to be very expensive if they are expelled without the verdict being held and without the appeal. So it's a risky path to tread, but the strength of feeling does vary from club to club.

"Certainly some of the other elite clubs are very unhappy with the delay in the situation because they feel it has an impact upon their ability to qualify for the Champions League. I think some of the more mid-tier clubs who don't see Manchester City as a threat, their main concern is, is this going to further increase the already sky-high legal costs that have been incurred by the Premier League and they don't want any part of it.

"So, they want a quick resolution and then they can get on with the rest of their season and focus on their own clubs."

Wardley was badly beaten by his heavyweight rival in their rematch on Saturday night as Dubois retained his world title. Wardley was knocked down inside the opening seconds before being stopped in the next round. The Ipswich man had risen from white-collar fighter to world champion but now faces an uncertain future.

And world champion Filip Hrgovic reckons he should hang up his gloves. "I think [Wardley] should retire," he said. "He didn't look good. I’m the future undisputed champion. I will smash Dubois in a rematch and I’m coming for the belts.”

Sports.title: Fabio Wardley landed just 4 punches in brutal Daniel Dubois KO
Sports.content:
Fabio Wardley landed just 4 punches in brutal Daniel Dubois KO

Dubois retained his WBO world heavyweight title with a brutal second-round stoppage of Wardley in London on Saturday night

View 2 Images Daniel Dubois was devastating (Image: Nick Potts/the Press Association)

Fabio Wardley landed just FOUR shots on Daniel Dubois as he was blasted out inside two rounds.

‌



‌



Dubois retained his WBO world heavyweight title with a brutal second-round stoppage of Wardley as their fight of the year rematch ended in a furious assault from the champion. There were 39 seconds of the round left when referee Steve Gray waved the off the contest at the same time as the towel was thrown into the ring by Wardley’s trainer Ben Davison.

‌



Resuming hostilities just five months after their first encounter, Dubois launched an all-out assault from the first bell and was rewarded with a destructive victory that issued a statement to his rivals in the division. The Londoner’s first defence of the title he seized from Wardley in May positions him for unification fights as well as the possibility of facing the winner of Tyson Fury ’s bout against Anthony Joshua on December 11.

‌



Daniel Dubois DESTROYS Fabio Wardley in two rounds in rematch READ MORE :

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

And on this evidence he will be favourite to unify the heavyweight belts following a display of ferocious punching power that left Wardley in survival mode right from the start. Wardley had vowed to make the adjustments needed to avenge the only defeat of his career, but instead the former white-collar boxer was outclassed as his lack of experience caught up with him.

‌



Dubois had oozed confidence all week and he wasted no time marching into the ring, dispensing with the stage theatrics to get the fight started as soon as possible. And in a dramatic reversal of the first fight, he floored Wardley just seconds into the contest following a barrage of shots that saw a savage right hand do the telling damage.

A one-sided opening round continued with Wardley coming under ferocious attack and it ended with him under pressure against the ropes while Davison hovered in the corner ready to throw in the towel. Images of the battering Wardley took in the later rounds in May came flooding back as he took more punishment in the second and with hardly any shots coming back in response, Gray and Davison intervened.

View 2 Images Fabio Wardley is knocked down

Article continues below

The punch stats show Wardley landed four of the 27 shots he threw compared to Dubois' 60 out of 119. The champion landed 51 of his power shots in a scary showing. Despite taking a fearful battering in the first meeting including extensive damage to his blood-soaked nose, Wardley immediately activated the rematch clause.

He felt that by flooring Dubois during the first and third rounds in Manchester even though he had not connected cleanly, he could force victory by mixing his power with a more nuanced approach.By rising from the canvas twice, meanwhile, Dubois had silenced questions over his mental resilience that first emerged when he was accused of “quitting” against Joe Joyce in 2020.

He entered the rematch as odds-on favourite to claim a 27th professional win and the stage was set for another slugfest between two of the division’s most explosive punchers, but it never materialised as the champion ended his rivalry with Wardley in chilling fashion.

"I actually really enjoy that because that's part of what drives you to have success, and that's part of the end of it. And if you're not ready for that and you can't do anything that's difficult, then you're never going to be great. So we've got to work our way through it and I'm enjoying it as we go."

United are understood to have taken a dim view of Butt's decision to go public with their conversation, especially at a time when results aren't going Carrick's way. The 45-year-old has only won two of his nine games in his first season as the club's permanent manager, a stark contrast to the form which the Red Devils enjoyed earlier this year after he was appointed initially on an interim basis.

‌



Is Michael Carrick the right man for Manchester United? Have your say in the comments section.

View 3 Images Nicky Butt said that Michael Carrick was reluctant to return to management (Image: The Good, The Ball & The Football)

But Carrick, who was dismissed by Middlesbrough in the summer of 2025, denied the notion that he needs a positive result against Leeds to keep his job. "I don't think it's the last game I need right now, for sure," he said.

‌



"I'm really looking forward to the game. I generally feel the drive for myself to want to push this club forward more than anything. There's always negativity if you want to look for it or you want to feel it, but I don't go looking for it. I don't want to feel it.

"I understand the reality and I've said it enough in terms of feeling like I'm saying the same things, but accepting where we are, but I don't feel that. I'm totally focused on what's best for this place and this football club and what it's going to take to win games, you know, and get the boys playing what we know we're capable of, which we still don't think we're that far away.

View 3 Images Michael Carrick is determined to get Manchester United back on track (Image: Cesar Cebolla/Pressinphoto/Icon Sport)

Article continues below

"You know, we can turn a few things in our favour and we'll be in good shape again and we can move forward pretty quickly. So, like I said earlier, I really don't think about me.

"I don't think 'how am I going to get through this, how am I going to survive this and what do I need to do to look after myself'. It's not important. It's about this football club and winning football matches."

Sports.title: 'There's one Arsenal team-mate I really disliked - it was a bad vibe from the moment we met'
Sports.content:
'There's one Arsenal team-mate I really disliked - it was a bad vibe from the moment we met'

A former Arsenal star reflected on his tense relationship with one of his team-mates at the Gunners

View 2 Images An ex-Arsenal star discussed his feelings towards one of his former team-mates (Image: IAN KINGTON / AFP via Getty Images)

Former Arsenal star Nicklas Bendtner named Emmanuel Adebayor as the only team-mate he could never get along with. The strikers played together for three years, but their mutual dislike memorably spilt onto the pitch, despite being on the same side.

‌



‌



Bedntner rose through the academy to make his debut in 2005, with Adebayor later arriving from Monaco. After the former returned from a Birmingham City loan spell, the pair became two of Arsene Wenger ’s striking options for the 2007/08 season but soon found they had little chemistry.

‌



The Denmark international spent nine years in Arsenal’s first team, later returning to England with Nottingham Forest, who host the Gunners on Sunday. The 38-year-old also had spells in Italy, Germany and Norway before retiring in his home country with Copenhagen, yet Bendtner has admitted that Adebayor was the one player he could not build a relationship with.

‌



Their uneasy dynamic notably came to the fore during a nightmare 5-1 League Cup semi-final defeat to rivals Tottenham Hotspur, with Spurs ultimately going on to lift the trophy. The scoreline saw tensions rise as the strikers got into a heated exchange and squared up to each other during the game.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss the best Arsenal coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources

‌



"There is only one guy I've fallen out with and that's Adebayor. We never liked each other. Apart from that I got on with most people," Bendtner told talkSPORT in 2021.

"We sat next to each other in the changing room. He was 25, I was 26, from the first moment we saw each other it was just a bad vibe. That never changed."

Focusing on their clash against Spurs, he continued: "We had some small bust-ups in the changing room and that quite big one in Tottenham where it sort of blew out of proportion. We got hammered 5-1, we were so bad and the disappointment of letting the fans and team down just got out of hand between us.

‌



"We had that sting on the pitch then we had a little bit in the dressing room and then the next day we were in [Arsene] Wenger's office getting fined. It got explained how we had to learn how to deal with each other on a professional level and on a personal level.

"It was actually quite a good way of learning how to work with someone that you really disliked."

View 2 Images Nicklas Bendtner and Emmanuel Adebayor clashed against Spurs in January 2008 (Image: CARL DE SOUZA / AFP via Getty Images)

‌



Adebayor starred for Arsenal throughout the 2007/08 campaign, scoring 30 goals in all competitions, but was unable to fire Wenger’s side to silverware. He was sold to Manchester City in 2009, which led to the striker’s infamous celebration against his old club, and he later rubbed further salt in Arsenal’s wounds by joining Spurs.

Bendtner notched 47 goals in 171 appearances for the Gunners before leaving for Wolfsburg at the end of his contract in 2014. The forward clinched the DFB-Pokal in his debut season but struggled for regular minutes. He headed back to England to sign for Forest, scoring twice in 17 appearances in his sole season at the City Ground.

A late-career renaissance with Rosenborg followed, as his goals steered the side to two league titles and the Norwegian Cup. The striker opted to retire in 2020 after a brief swansong with hometown club Copenhagen.

Article continues below

Bedtner may keep a close eye on Arsenal’s next match as the Gunners look to continue their Premier League title challenge against another of his old clubs. Mikel Artet'as side will aim to trim the gap to league leaders Manchester City back to three points with a win over Forest.

Sports.title: Harry Redknapp's brutal Michael Carrick manager verdict is a warning Man Utd must heed
Sports.content:
Harry Redknapp's brutal Michael Carrick manager verdict is a warning Man Utd must heed

Harry Redknapp has delivered a brutal assessment of Michael Carrick's managerial qualities at Manchester United

View Image Michael Carrick is under pressure at Man Utd

Harry Redknapp has branded Manchester United boss Michael Carrick as 'too laid back' and admitted he never envisioned him going into management. The 45-year-old, who was handed his senior debut by Redknapp, impressed during a brief caretaker stint at Old Trafford earlier this year but has found wins hard to come by since taking the reins permanently.

‌



Tuesday's 2-0 Champions League defeat to Atletico Madrid extended United's winless run to five matches. Carrick's only victories this season have come against Ipswich Town and Azerbaijani side Sabah.

Sunday's trip to Elland Road to take on local rivals Leeds United is therefore crucial, with tricky fixtures against Como, Bournemouth and Chelsea to follow. Carrick's first managerial role at Middlesbrough began promisingly before unravelling, with the former midfielder dismissed after two-and-a-half years at the helm.

‌



Will Lisandro Martinez play for Man Utd vs Leeds? Everything we know after bombshell comments READ MORE :

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Whether he can navigate his way through this difficult patch remains to be seen, with Redknapp's candid assessment of his personality and approach raising further questions about his prospects. He wrote in his column for The Sun: "I've known Michael since he was 12-years-old at West Ham.

"I can't say I always saw a manager in him. Michael's always been a lovely guy from a lovely family, a really intelligent footballer who knew the game, read it, controlled matches. But he's always been a quiet lad, too, laid-back. It's what he is.

‌



"When United scored against Tottenham the other day, he wasn't running up and down the touchline - the complete opposite to Roberto De Zerbi, kissing the ball and all that when they equalised. Results haven't been great but I hope he turns it around and keeps the job because I love him.

"You can change Michael tomorrow and they are still not going to finish any higher than fifth or sixth this season. That's how I see their team. They're nowhere near good enough to challenge for a title.

"That's what Michael is dealing with. And it would be the same for anyone else, whoever they bring in."

‌
