World.title: Why have settler pogroms surged during olive harvest season in West Bank?
World.content:
France and Belgium condemn settler attack on diplomats, but critics say the EU needs to act beyond words of condemnation.

Share Critics say hold Israel to account amid surge in olive harvest attacks on social media

The European Union has condemned Israeli settler attacks on EU diplomats and Palestinians in the occupied West Bank, amid unprecedented settler pogroms during the Palestinian olive harvest.

“We expect full accountability as well as effective measures to prevent continued acts of violence and violent harassment against Palestinians, including during the ongoing olive harvest season, as well as against journalists,” the EU said in a statement on Sunday.

“We urge Israel to fully abide by International Humanitarian and Human Rights Law, and to cease the expansion of settlements.”

Israeli settler attacks during this year’s olive harvest season have already surpassed 2025 totals, with critics pointing out that mere condemnations by the EU and member states without holding Israel to account will not deter settler pogroms, which are granted impunity by the Israeli authorities.

Saturday’s incident is the latest in weeks of intensifying pogroms against local communities in the occupied West Bank by Israelis from illegal settlements who are largely protected – or at least unrestricted – by Israeli forces.

On Friday, Israeli settlers also attacked Palestinian olive pickers and a veteran photojournalist.

Why have settler pogroms surged during olive harvest season in the occupied West Bank?

Here’s what we know:

What has been the response?

Belgium’s Foreign Minister Maxime Prevot said the country’s consul general to the Palestinians, as well as French and Polish diplomats and Catholic representatives, were also among those attacked.



French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot called on the Israeli government to arrest the settlers who assaulted Bernard Baudoux, the mayor of Aulnoye-Aymeries, and said on X it must “urgently put an end to this criminal violence and ensure the safety of the civilian population”.

The assault has prompted an Israeli police investigation, as settler pogroms disrupt the Palestinian harvest across the occupied territory.

United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the Trump administration is “very disturbed” by the images of the settler attack on American photojournalist Heidi Levine, 64, who works as a freelance photojournalist for The Washington Post, in the occupied West Bank on Friday.

Speaking to reporters at the Joint Base Andrews in Maryland, Rubio said he was yet to receive an official briefing on Friday’s incident, but what he saw “didn’t look good”.

He urged Israel to “crack down” on the violence and said President Donald Trump does not want to see “friction” or “a crisis” in the West Bank.

Ahmed Najar, a Palestinian political analyst and playwright, told Al Jazeera that condemnation without consequences is not accountability.

“Western governments continue to arm, fund and diplomatically protect Israel while treating settler attacks as isolated acts by a few extremists. But this violence flourishes within a wider system of occupation, settlement expansion and impunity,” he said.

“The West cannot claim to oppose settler violence while continuing to support the state and policies that enable it,” he added.

Sven Kuhn von Burgsdorff, former EU representative to the occupied West Bank and Gaza, had a similar view.

“⁠The lame protests issued by the European chancelleries in response to these terrorist acts of Israeli settlers are pathetic since they are not followed up by concrete punitive measures,” he said.

“This is especially disgraceful considering that this settler terrorism has been going on for years with full impunity. At the last Foreign Affairs Council meeting in Brussels on October 12, the EU ministers were still unable to decide on sanctioning the violent settlers and/or its enablers, the annexationist apartheid government of PM Netanyahu,” he added.

What happened on Saturday?

On Saturday, Israeli settlers attacked vehicles belonging to diplomats from France, Belgium and Poland near the Palestinian Christian village of Taybeh in the occupied West Bank.

At least seven masked settlers surrounded the vehicles, demanded identification documents, smashed the window of a vehicle belonging to the Belgian consulate and assaulted the French mayor, according to witnesses and media reports.



The 78-year-old told the Reuters news agency that he was “a bit shaken” by the event.

“I had my mayor’s sash on, with the blue, white and red colours, which clearly represent the symbol of France, in an attempt to protect the people around me. Well, that was not enough, and I was attacked, violently attacked, protected by the people who were there to try and limit things,” Baudoux said.

He said the settlers threw him to the ground, after which his group rushed back into their vehicles to leave.

“I didn’t think something like this could happen to me coming here as a pacifist to celebrate a ‘twinning’ — friendship between two cities,” he added.

However, refusing to be terrified by the attack, Baudoux said, “I think we need to go back to the olive plantations because they have great significance for the Palestinian people.”

Former EU diplomat Burgsdorff told Al Jazeera these attacks are not new, saying he witnessed “thugs attacking peaceful Palestinian farmers and citizens” during his visits to the occupied Palestinian territory between January 2020 and July 2023.

“Once a settler mob even threw stones at us – but we were already in our vehicles. Since we couldn’t count on protection by Israeli police or military, we left the scene of confrontation as soon as possible,” he added.

Where else have settlers attacked olive pickers?

In recent weeks, Israeli settlers have intensified pogroms against Palestinians picking olives in the region.

Earlier on Saturday, settlers injured six Palestinians as Israeli forces arrested farmers during pogroms across the occupied West Bank.

Four women and a child were among the injured when Israeli settlers attacked residents in Ma’in village in the Masafer Yatta area, south of Hebron, according to the Palestine Red Crescent Society (PRCS).

In Deir Ammar town, west of Ramallah, Israeli forces opened fire on farmers picking olives, forcing them to leave their land, according to the Palestinian news agency Wafa. Israeli settlers also injured two Palestinians as they opened fire in the area.

In the village of Kafr Malek, northeast of Ramallah, settlers raided a farm at dawn and killed about 20 sheep, Mayor Najeh Rustum told Al Jazeera.

Reporting from Ramallah, Al Jazeera’s Nour Odeh said settlers destroyed olive trees across the Beit Furik plain, east of Nablus, in the northern West Bank, while Israeli forces arrested landowners and olive pickers.

In Deir Jarir village, east of Ramallah, she said, settlers under army protection fired live ammunition at farmers in the al-Hariq area to prevent them from harvesting, forcing them off their land.

Settlers also smashed the vehicle of international activist Jonathan Budlak in the village and threw stones at a farmer’s vehicle.

On Friday, dozens of masked settlers attacked Palestinian farmers harvesting olives, throwing stones, using slingshots and setting trees on fire.



Friday’s and Saturday’s attacks follow the killing of Ali Hassan Yasser al-Bazzari, 44, during an assault on Palestinians picking olives near Burqa, northwest of Nablus, on October 7. Witnesses reported that settlers and Israeli soldiers attacked the harvesters.

Journalists documenting the violence have also been targeted.

Veteran freelance journalist Levine was attacked near Abu Falah on Friday. She fell to the ground during the attack before she was set upon, witnesses said.

Levine, who was taken to a hospital northeast of Ramallah after the attack, later told reporters that her attackers “just kept kicking me and kicking me, like probably 50 times”.

Levine was wearing a protective vest marked “PRESS” on the front and back. Her cameras and phone were taken from her during the assault, The Washington Post reported.

On October 6, armed settlers beat Palestinian photographer for the AFP news agency Jaafar Ashtiyeh, 58, with rifle butts near Aqraba, south of Nablus. He was taken to hospital with injuries to his head and torso, according to witnesses, relatives and colleagues.

Why have settler pogroms surged during olive harvest season?

The Israeli settler pogroms have been going on for many weeks and have increased during the ongoing olive harvest season.

Israeli rights group Yesh Din has documented 377 incidents of violence involving occupiers and soldiers in two weeks through October 10.

According to the Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA), “So far this year, nearly 200 settler attacks linked to the olive harvest have caused casualties or property damage. That is already more than the 185 incidents recorded during the entire 2025 season.”

But the attacks are not new. Every year, Israeli settlers and hardline groups use the olive harvest period to assert control over valuable agricultural lands, often blocking Palestinians from reaching their groves, stealing crops, or building illegal settlement outposts and roads on private Palestinian property.

The olive harvest is also a critical economic lifeline for roughly 80,000 to 100,000 Palestinian families in the occupied West Bank. Intimidating, injuring, or barring farmers from picking their olives, as well as uprooting or burning thousands of olive trees, inflict serious financial damage and force families off their land.

“The olive harvest is not simply an agricultural season for Palestinians; it is a vital source of income and a powerful expression of their connection to the land. Settlers target this period because Palestinian families are gathered in exposed groves, often close to settlements and outposts,” Najar told Al Jazeera.

“By assaulting farmers, burning or uprooting trees and stealing crops, they are not merely disrupting a harvest – they are making it increasingly dangerous for Palestinians to reach and remain on their own land,” he said.

“The violence is also intended to deter international campaigners from accompanying Palestinian farmers, standing with them against settler violence and documenting the atrocities being committed … The objective is not only to dispossess Palestinians, but to ensure that their dispossession happens without witnesses,” he added.

According to Al Jazeera’s Odeh, this year, due to the upcoming elections, which are crucial for right-wing parties, Israeli settlers are more emboldened.

“In fact, they have received even a religious edict telling them that stealing the olive harvest was not just permissible; it was the right thing to do,” she said.



What has Israel said about the attacks?

The Israeli military has condemned Saturday’s attack on the EU diplomats and said it has opened an investigation into the incident. It said its soldiers were not present during the attack.

Settler attacks over the years have also occurred under the protection or passive stance of the Israeli army, which often declares Palestinian farming areas “closed military zones” or coordinates with settlers to restrict landowner access.

Meanwhile, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s office has appeared to question the reports of the attack on the Europeans, saying on X that they are “alleged” and require “compelling evidence”, despite acknowledging that published footage of the incident exists.

Al Jazeera’s Odeh noted that while the prime minister downplays violence, Israeli opposition figures are attacking Netanyahu, saying it undermines the standing of Israel.

“They vow to protect the illegal settlements while trying to curb settler violence,” she added.

World.title: Who is Mehrdad Akhlaghi, Iran’s new tech-focused defence minister?
World.content:
Tehran, Iran – Mehrdad Akhlaghi Ketabchi has been appointed Iran’s defence minister at a time when the war with the United States is expected to escalate.

The 68-year-old was approved on Sunday by parliament, which has convened online since the start of the US-Israel war on Iran on February 28, to assume leadership of the Ministry of Defence and Armed Forces Logistics. In total, 237 lawmakers voted in favour of Akhlaghi’s appointment and 15 against.

Former Defence Minister Aziz Nasirzadeh was killed along with a large number of other senior figures, including Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei, on the opening day of the war.

The position was filled temporarily by Majid Ebn-e Reza, who will now become Akhlaghi’s deputy.

Akhlaghi will be responsible for rebuilding and expanding Iran’s military-industrial infrastructure, which has been heavily targeted by the US and Israel.

The new minister’s defence plans were approved earlier by senior military authorities, President Masoud Pezeshkian and parliament’s Commission on National Security and Foreign Policy.

“The Islamic Republic of Iran will not be the instigator of aggression against any country but will defend the territorial integrity of the country strongly and to the death against any aggression,” Pezeshkian said.

The president said Akhlaghi has more than 42 years of experience in the Defence Ministry and related organisations.



His principal expertise is in ballistic missiles, solid-fuel propulsion, aerospace technology and military-industrial production, according to state media.

Previously, he served as the head of the Shahid Bagheri Industrial Group, the Aerospace Industries Organization and the Defence Industries Organization. Akhlaghi and these entities are all subject to sanctions by the US. He is also under United Nations sanctions.

He has been associated with developing several missile types and related weapons-development projects over the past decades, according to Tasnim, a newspaper linked with the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC),

Akhlaghi reportedly played a role in expanding the major Sejjil and Zolfaghar family of Iranian ballistic missiles as well as precision-guided weapons, such as the Almas missiles and Yasin guided bombs.

He is also said to have expertise in space launchers, research rockets and infrastructure associated with the Imam Khomeini Space Center in Semnan. These have all been critical elements in Iran’s wars against Israel and the US.

This month, Iran’s Defence Ministry spokesman, Brigadier General Reza Talaei-Nik, told reporters that Akhlaghi’s nomination reflected Iran’s need to increase the quantity and quality of strategic weapons, particularly missiles and drones.

“Offensive arms are being actively improved,” the spokesman said.

The US has repeatedly claimed that it has destroyed most of Iran’s military-industrial capacities, but Tehran has maintained it continues to have considerable offensive and defensive capabilities outside the reach of US and Israeli bombs. These weapons have been upgraded based on Iran’s new war experience, it has insisted.

Akhlaghi told members of parliament this month that he had met with senior military commanders, including the commander-in-chief of the IRGC, Brigadier General Ahmad Vahidi, to develop a better understanding of their requirements during and after the war.

His priorities as defence minister would be faster military-industrial development, air defences, incorporation of emerging technologies using government and private sector firms, improvements in armed-forces welfare and development of international military cooperation, according to reports.

In his first comments as defence minister on Sunday, Akhlaghi taunted the administration of US President Donald Trump, which this month threatened to use the “mother of all bombs” on Iran’s nuclear and energy infrastructure.

“We have made preparations and continue our work with ease of mind,” he told reporters. “The US president must think of getting his forces out of our region in one piece. If he drops one bomb, he must see how many of his troops he will have to evacuate horizontally.”

World.title: Funeral held for 75 Palestinians after remains recovered from Gaza ruins
World.content:
Most of the victims were from the Daraj neighbourhood in Gaza City, the Health Ministry says.

Share Funeral held for 75 Palestinians after remains recovered from Gaza ruins on social media

A mass funeral has been held for 75 Palestinians whose remains were found recently under the rubble of homes and buildings destroyed in the months since Israel launched its genocidal war on Gaza in October 2023, the Ministry of Health announced.

Hundreds of Palestinians attended the funeral procession before the remains were buried at the Sheikh Radwan Cemetery on Sunday morning.

Most of the victims were from the Daraj neighbourhood in the northeastern part of Gaza City.

Al Jazeera correspondent Nour Khaled said the majority of the remains belonged to women and children “who were inside their homes when they were targeted”.

The remains consisted of some body parts and personal belongings and were wrapped in Palestinian flags before the burial, she said.

Abdullah al-Majdalawi, director of public relations and media for Gaza’s Civil Defence, told the Turkish state news agency Anadolu that the remains had been recovered over recent weeks from several destroyed homes in Daraj.

He said the buildings were bombed while residents were inside during the early months of the war and that the victims belonged to about 20 Palestinian families, including people who had been displaced to the homes.

Efforts to recover bodies from beneath the rubble continue to face severe difficulties due to a lack of equipment and heavy machinery, he added.

The Civil Defence launched the second phase of its recovery operations in July. It recovered 333 bodies and remains of 559 people during its first operation in November 2025.



The Civil Defence says it believes the remains of another 8,000 Palestinians are still trapped beneath the rubble across Gaza. There are about 200,000 damaged and destroyed buildings in Gaza, according to the UN agency for Palestinian refugees, UNRWA.

At least 74,475 Palestinians have been killed since Israel launched the genocidal war three years ago.

World.title: What help can Egypt offer Saudi Arabia in the war against the Houthis?
World.content:
Analysts say that any move from Egypt will remain ‘strictly defensive’, as the conflict in Yemen intensifies.

Share What help can Egypt offer Saudi Arabia in the war against the Houthis? on social media

Egypt’s parliament is convening on Sunday after President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi requested an emergency session to approve defensive military aid to Saudi Arabia, if Riyadh asks for support in its war with Yemen’s Houthis.

The request comes as the Iran-backed armed group continues attacks on Saudi Arabia, including the capital, Riyadh, and its airports and oil facilities.

El-Sisi declared that Egypt will “carry out any measure to protect” Saudi Arabia, in a speech on Saturday, but said that he “hopes” the parliament will give him authorisation to proceed.

On Sunday, Egypt said it would provide “all necessary and possible support to Saudi Arabia to defend its safety and stability”. The National Defence Council, chaired by President el-Sisi, said it “stands fully with” Saudi Arabia to defend its resources, territorial integrity and Islamic holy sites.

But what would Egyptian assistance look like? And what capacity does it have to “protect” Saudi Arabia in its war with the Houthis?

Here is what we know.

What’s behind el-Sisi’s decision to offer help to Saudi Arabia?

Saudi Arabia has long been a strategic and economic partner of Egypt, and el-Sisi said in a statement last month that Saudi security is “integral” to Egypt’s security.

Political analyst and Gulf studies expert Thomas Bonnie James told Al Jazeera that the Houthi security threat to the kingdom is one of the “converging” pressures that have led to this decision. The other one, is economics.

“Houthi pressure on [Bab] al-Mandeb threatens the Suez Canal, which Egypt’s foreign minister says has lost about $11bn since the attacks began in 2023,” he said, referring to Houthi attacks on Israeli-linked ships passing through the narrow strait, carried out in solidarity with Gaza.



James suggested that the decision is also important to Cairo, because “millions of Egyptians live and work in Saudi Arabia, which is Egypt’s largest single source of remittances. An Egyptian resident was killed, and others were injured in the attacks on Riyadh’s airport.”

He also said that Egypt does not want to be seen as the regional ally that “stood aside while others defended the kingdom,” as Turkiye and Pakistan have made their own pledges after activating the Mecca defence pact signed in August amid the deteriorating security situation in the Middle East.

What’s the latest on the Yemen war?

Hostilities in Yemen continue to escalate. Two air raids by the Saudi-led coalition hit Hodeidah in the southwest on Sunday.

Saudi forces also intercepted drones near Riyadh and Eastern provinces. The capital’s King Khalid international airport has come under attack at least 20 times since fighting flared between the internationally recognised government and the Houthis, also known as Ansar Allah – Arabic for Supporters of God.

The Saudi-backed forces are fighting the Houthis on several fronts, including Taiz and Marib, and some analysts argue the Houthis are stretched thin after their summer gains.

But James told Al Jazeera “that defeating them outright is a tall order”.

“Ground forces backed by air power can retake the coastline; stopping missiles launched from the mountains is much harder,” he said.

When will the Egyptian parliament convene?

They will be convening on Sunday at 1pm local time (10am GMT).

Under the Egyptian law, the President cannot declare war or send the military on foreign missions without the approval from the parliament.

For the authorisation to be granted, at least two-thirds of the politicians in the House of Representatives must vote in favour of the proposal.

Does Egypt have security cooperation with Saudi Arabia?

Not exactly. Egypt and Saudi Arabia have not signed a formal bilateral or multilateral pact on defence cooperation. But Cairo has a long history of cooperation with Riyadh.

Egypt is a founding member of the Multinational Maritime Defense Coalition, which Saudi Arabia launched in July. It aims to protect shipping in the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandeb – territories on Yemen’s coastline. Houthis captured towns and cities near Bab al-Mandeb last month, but the internationally recognised government has since wrested control of some of the areas from the Iran-backed group.

Egypt also participated in joint military exercises with Saudi Arabia in 2024.



Cairo was also part of a 2015 coalition, cobled together after the Houthi group captured large areas of north and western Yemen, including the capital Sanaa in September 2024. Egypt contributed naval and air forces to help secure maritime corridors in the Red Sea against the Houthis.

But James, the Gulf studies expert, told Al Jazeera that what el-Sisi is proposing is different from the maritime defence coalition Egypt recently joined.

“He is hoping for authorisation to deploy Egyptian forces to help defend Saudi territory itself,” he said. “It would move Egypt from a multilateral maritime framework to a bilateral military commitment.”

What will be the nature of Egyptian assistance to Saudi Arabia?

El-Sisi explicitly said that he is only proposing “defence” and that he isn’t “speaking in order for us to fight anyone or attack anyone”.

Military Defence Analyst Alexandru Hudisteanu said that the use of counter-drones and anti-missile support is a high probability if the decision is authorised.

“It would be the most urgent need at this point to make sure that the defence of Saudi Arabia is backed up and reinforced,” he told Al Jazeera.

Simultaneously, he added that the request itself is also a strategic move of deterrence.

“We know Saudi Arabia has one of the most prolific militaries out there in terms of capacities and capabilities. It’s a matter of the territory which Saudi Arabia needs to cover at any given moment,” Hudisteanu said.

James said that any contribution by Egypt would focus on the protection of Saudi territory, using “air and missile defence around critical infrastructure, intercepting drones, naval escort and intelligence sharing”.

James said that it is unlikely Egypt will deploy troops to Yemen’s front lines.

In the 1960s, former Egyptian President Gamal Abdel Nasser deployed tens of thousands of troops in the Yemen Civil War. Saudi Arabia backed the rival side. Egypt suffered heavy casualties and Saudi-Egyptian ties were strained.

“What Egypt will not want is to send troops into Yemen. Nasser’s intervention there in the 1960s sends a clear message: defend the kingdom, don’t take ownership of Yemen,” he told Al Jazeera.

World.title: Burnt out cars and shattered glass on Paris streets after protests turn to riots and looting
World.content:
France awoke to scenes of widespread damage on Sunday after a day of riots and demonstrations, with shopfronts shattered, burnt out cars, charred bikes, and piles of glass and debris on the pavements of Paris.

Police arrested about 1,800 people on Saturday as some 550,000 demonstrators took to the streets for protests that were largely peaceful.

They were demonstrating against rising fuel prices, the cost of living and deteriorating public services, including schools.

Groups of rioters, some dressed in black and wearing masks and balaclavas, also came out in Paris, Marseille and other towns and cities, with some setting fire to cars and buildings.

Widespread looting took place across the cities of Paris, Marseille and Lille, as well as other areas.

In Paris, protesters clashed with riot police, who turned tear gas and water cannon on the crowds. During the day, some groups lit fires in the street and torched vehicles. At least one restaurant was gutted by fire, and the BBC saw fighting breaking out among some of the groups.

Riot police were seen charging at one crowd in central Paris and hitting several people with batons.

"It's like we had a war," Paris resident Mehmet Ozeden told news agency AFP.

Another resident, Anita GrasIt, said it was "terrifying" to see groups of young people "smashing everything, with total impunity".

The looters were "proudly carrying supermarket baskets filled with goods and laughing about their thefts", Maryse, a woman living nearby who gave only her first name, told the BBC.

Further south in Marseille, protesters broke into the city hall by using a metal fence as a battering ram. In Lille, a McDonalds was set on fire, police said, and an Apple store in the city was broken into and looted.

World.title: Oil facilities hit in deadly overnight attack on St Petersburg
World.content:
At least one person has been killed in an overnight attack on St Petersburg that successfully targeted two of the city's oil facilities.

The region's Governor Alexander Beglov said fires were being extinguished at the St Petersburg Oil Terminal and the Ruchyi oil depot following the attack, which also injured at least five.

A logistics centre belonging to Ozon - known as Russia's Amazon - and a data centre belonging to Facebook equivalent VKontakte were also hit.

Kyiv has not yet commented on the strikes. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Saturday morning that Russia had targeted his country's energy sector 76 times since Donald Trump declared an "energy ceasefire" last week.

Ukraine had paused its strikes on Russian oil facilities - which it says are to limit the main revenue stream for Moscow's war effort - for three days after the announcement, while accusing Russia of continuing.

It then resumed strikes earlier this week, drawing the ire of Trump, who called for a truce to facilitate a deal he struck with his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin to supply diesel.

Ukraine has struck St Petersburg before, though regions closer to Ukraine are threatened more often. The city's oil terminal was last hit in July.

Russia's defence ministry said it had shot down more than 1,000 Ukrainian drones over Russian territory overnight into Sunday.

St Petersburg's governor said 12 apartment buildings and two homes were damaged in the attacks on the city, while Pulkovo Airport was temporarily closed.

He also said mobile internet service disruption was possible.

Social network VK confirmed a drone had targeted its regional data centre, but stressed its services were available "as usual" after users reported outages in the early hours of the morning.

Ozon also confirmed its local logistics centre had been targeted by a drone, sparking a fire.

It said staff were evacuated and no one was injured, and that it was not accepting shipments from sellers at the location "as it is currently serving other operational purposes".

As well as numerous oil facilities across Russia, Ukraine has also mounted strikes aimed at disrupting the Russian economy more broadly. Earlier this month, it launched a series of attacks on Yandex, Russia's largest search engine, that led to service disruptions.

Relations between Washington and Kyiv have frayed since the US struck a controversial deal to import Russian diesel in the hope of bringing down US energy prices, which have skyrocketed during the Iran war, ahead of the midterm elections.

Zelensky suggested the deal was tantamount to the US investing in Russia's war effort.

Trump's decision to temporarily suspend a raft of sanctions against Russia has brought fresh criticism, including from some US Republicans.

Both Russia and Ukraine have been striking one another's energy infrastructure with increasing intensity ahead of the winter, as Moscow's full-scale invasion drags on in its fifth year.

Russia says it hits targets used by Ukraine's military, though the UN noted on Friday that the first two weeks of October had been the deadliest for Ukrainian civilians in years.

Russian strikes on energy facilities have left hundreds of thousands without power, raising concerns about civilians enduring another freezing winter.

Zelensky said on Saturday that tens of thousands of people were still without power. Russia launched nearly 2,700 drones, 1,700 aerial bombs and 66 missiles in the past week, most of which were aimed at energy facilities, he said.

World.title: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis
World.content:
Warning: This story contains descriptions of drug-taking from the start and discusses suicide

The few grains of fentanyl sit in the silver foil as a straw, held between Mike's lips, hovers above, with a cigarette lighter below. The 48-year-old army veteran is crouched low in an alleyway in Columbus, Ohio's Linden neighbourhood.

"This drug will damn near make you do anything, unfortunately," he says.

The hit he's smoking cost three or four dollars.

"You can snort too much and you can't take it back. Kind of like a gunshot. Can't call the bullet back," he says.

He burns the foil and inhales. As the opioid takes hold, he grips the fence behind him. He sways as a low moan comes from deep in his throat - he could be humming a tune.

We've spent a few days with Mike - he's been our guide through the neighbourhood's back streets. Everyone seems to know him and he's regarded fondly. He helps out at a local pawn shop and gas station, and that's how he feeds his 20-year-old opioid addiction.

Synthetic opioids are more powerful and in plentiful supply, and they have transformed the drugs landscape.

Fentanyl, which is entirely man-made, is 50 to 100 times more powerful than heroin, which is cultivated from poppies. It is now often cut with synthetic tranquillisers, which make reviving overdose victims more difficult. These are homemade threats, where cocktails of synthetics can be made in American basements and bathtubs.

World.title: European diplomats attacked by Israeli settlers in West Bank
World.content:
A delegation of European diplomats has been attacked by masked Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank.

Belgium condemned the assault on its consul general and the other envoys, while France decried the attack as "appalling". Both called for Israel to bring those responsible to justice.

The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) also condemned what they called "the severe act of violence" and said they were investigating.

But the office of the Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu cast doubt on what happened, suggesting it was part of a "co-ordinated campaign to smear Israel".

The attack came only a day after a number of Palestinians and Heidi Levine, a Washington Post photographer, were injured in a separate assault by settlers in another village in the West Bank.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the attack on Levine was "disturbing" and "not a good look".

It was also condemned by the US ambassador to Israel, Mike Huckabee, who called it a "despicable act of terror carried out by masked cowards". A staunch ally of Israel, Huckabee said the assailants must face "prosecution to the fullest extent of the law".

World.title: Several dead or injured in major fire at Canada military base
World.content:
Several people have been killed or injured as a result of a large fire near a Canadian military base in Alberta, the nation's military has said.

The Canadian Armed Forces (CAF) said the full extent of the incident's impact was being assessed and that details of casualties and injuries would not be made public until that was complete.

Canadian Forces Base Wainwright, where the fire broke out around 16:00 local time (22:00 GMT) on Saturday, is one of the country's busiest military training bases.

Canadian TV network Global News reported that at least seven were killed and dozens more injured when a gas line or gas well was hit during a live-fire training exercise, citing unnamed military sources.

Defence Minister David McGuinty said the CAF and local authorities were managing the fire, describing the situation as "very, very active and delicate".

Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney said his "thoughts are with all the brave women and men affected".

The Canadian Broadcasting Corporation (CBC) said Royal Alexandra Hospital in Edmonton had declared a code orange, a disaster response protocol for responding to a high-casualty incident.

Warren Thirsk, an emergency department doctor there, told the broadcaster that the number of patients would otherwise "overwhelm" Edmonton's healthcare facilities.

"It is more patients than any of us want to count right now. It's a disaster. It's a one in every 15 to 25-year disaster."

After the fire erupted on Saturday, it "spread rapidly due to high winds" and tore through the fences of the base, the Municipal District of Wainwright said.

The region experienced gusts of up to 100km/h (62mph), though local officials indicated fire crews had contained the blaze.

McGuinty told reporters he "cannot recall an incident like this in recent memory".

Local authorities have urged residents to avoid the area and give all emergency vehicles right of way.

The mayor of the nearby town of Wainwright, Bruce Pugh, said it was a "heavy day" for his community.

"We have neighbours who are either serving or former members of the Canadian Armed Forces. We're integrated, our kids play in the same hockey teams, attend the same schools," he told CBC.

While details on the impact of the fire remain unclear, Pugh said he believed this would come to be the area's largest-ever mass casualty event.

World.title: Trump waives several Russia sanctions as row with Zelensky intensifies
World.content:
Donald Trump has blocked numerous sanctions on Russia two days before they were due to take effect, as a row with his Ukrainian counterpart Volodymyr Zelensky deepens.

The sanctions were passed by the US Congress and signed into law by the US president in September.

But Trump issued an executive order on Friday night saying that suspending some was in the US national interest, prompting a backlash from US lawmakers. Zelensky said it was unfortunate the US has decided to "completely disregard" the sanctions.

Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev said Trump's order was "an important and truly historic moment", and that the sanctions would have inflicted "serious damage" on the US and global market.

Relations between Washington and Kyiv frayed after the US struck a controversial deal to import Russian diesel last week. Ukraine has accused the Trump administration of withdrawing key military support.

Since then, Ukraine's president declared it was nice to be among "real leaders" while addressing an EU summit, after Trump said Zelensky was "more difficult to deal with" than Russian President Vladimir Putin.

The sanctions suspension seemed to add further fuel to the fire.

Zelensky said on Saturday morning that the sanctions "could have helped enormously" and that the law was "supposed to impose truly effective pressure on Russia to bring this war to an end".

He pointed to Russian overnight attacks on 15 Ukrainian energy facilities that had caused power cuts in several regions and said: "Russia is trying to cause a blackout in Ukraine â right before winter."

Zelensky said it was "important that everyone in America also sees what is really happening" on the ground.

The new US sanctions law took aim at Russia's economy by giving Trump broad powers to levy tariffs of up to 100% on imports from the top five purchasers of Russian oil and gas â most significantly China and India.

It also included sanctions against senior Russian figures, including Putin, as well as Russian financial institutions and Moscow's so-called "shadow fleet" of vessels used to circumvent existing embargoes.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said that the suspension would consist of a 60-day pause to allow for the Trump administration to analyse the impact they might have on the US and global economy.

World.title: Anti-government protesters battle with police in Albania
World.content:
Demonstrators and riot police fought pitched battles in the centre of Tirana on Saturday for the fifth day in a row.

Masked protesters, many of them high school and university students, hurled rocks and petrol bombs at riot police trying to defend the education ministry, one of the focal points of the protests.

The police responded with water cannon and volleys of tear gas, sending the crowds scattering. There are also reports that rubber bullets were used for the first time.

Protests which began in the summer have grown into a wider anti-government movement, with calls for the prime minister to resign following corruption allegations linked to his administration.

Many of the protesters in central Tirana wore gas masks or face masks, while volunteers handed out syringes of saline eyewash to reduce the pain from the tear gas which billows down the street.

The constant boom of petrol bombs could be heard exploding on Saturday.

During the afternoon, the focus of the protests shifted to the office of Prime Minister Edi Rama on the city's main boulevard.

Here the crowds swelled to far larger numbers than on previous days.

Riot police faced a steady hail of cobble stones and fireworks, and responded with barrage after barrage of tear gas, some of the canisters landing far back in the crowds, causing panic.

Incensed by the gas, the crowds waited for it to clear, then renewed their attacks.

World.title: At least 17 dead in crush at Hindu festival event in India
World.content:
At least 17 people have been killed and many more injured in a crush at an event in the Indian city of Kolkata to mark the Hindu festival of Durga Puja, officials say.

The incident occurred during sudden rainfall, which witnesses say prompted a surge of people to try to seek shelter.

West Bengal's Chief Minister Suvendhu Adhikari said a seven-year-old girl was among the dead, and that 25 people were being treated for injuries.

Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi described it as a "tragic" incident and said the regional government was providing help to affected families.

Six of the dead have been identified, Adhikari said.

A senior police official told the AFP news agency that an announcement caused "commotion" after it started raining and the crowd started "pushing, pulling and rushing forward and fell on the ground, leading to the stampede.".

Deadly crowd incidents, including during religious festivals, are not uncommon in India due to poor management and lack of adequate safety precautions.

Two years ago, 121 people were killed in Uttar Pradesh during a Hindu religious gathering.

World.title: 2027 Polls: Katsina governor seeks forgiveness, urges APC unity – News Agency of Nigeria
World.content:
Governor Dikko Radda of Katsina State has appealed to anyone offended by his administration’s decisions to forgive him, urging unity among All Progressives Congress (APC) members ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Mr Radda made the appeal on Saturday in Katsina while inaugurating the APC campaign council for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu and himself.

“I have no grudge against anybody in the party, and I welcome everyone who wants to join the party,” he said.

The governor urged party members to close ranks, mobilise voters and intensify grassroots campaigns to secure victory for APC candidates.

He warned members against relying on the party’s popularity without actively campaigning for votes.

“The time to get into any seat of power by awuf has gone. Come out and campaign massively for votes,” he said.

Mr Radda said APC members must work collectively for Tinubu and all party candidates, from polling units and wards to local, state and federal levels.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He described every party member as an ambassador of Mr Tinubu and other APC candidates, urging them to demonstrate commitment to the party’s collective interests.

The governor expressed confidence in the APC’s electoral prospects in Katsina and across the country, urging members to remain focused on victory.

He thanked residents for their support and patience with his administration over the past three and a half years.

Mr Radda said his administration had recorded significant infrastructure development across the state’s 34 local government areas.

He also said the government consistently paid monthly allowances to APC officials at the state, local government, and ward levels.

According to him, the payments have helped sustain the party’s organisational structure.

Earlier, APC State Chairman, Bishir Gambo-Saulawa, commended Mr Radda for strengthening the party and supporting the construction of its newly completed state secretariat.

He described the secretariat, where the inauguration took place, as a distinctive facility.

Mr Gambo-Saulawa also said the party’s candidates in the state had been duly certified by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC).

He acknowledged former APC state chairman Sani Ali’s contributions to the secretariat, noting that Mr Ali initiated the project.

During the inauguration, Mr Radda appointed Mr Gambo-Saulawa as the deputy chairman of the campaign council.

Ahmed Dangiwa, an architect, was named Director-General, while Abdullahi Aliyu Turaji was appointed Secretary-General.

Alhaji Sani Aliyu was named the council’s organising secretary.

The Minister of Arts, Culture and the Creative Economy, Hannatu Musawa, also commended Mr Radda for the infrastructure development recorded in the state.

Ms Musawa said Mr Tinubu had directed her to work closely with the governor to promote the development of Katsina State.

(NAN)

World.title: Lagos water corporation serves only 1.03% of population — Official
World.content:
The Lagos Water Corporation (LWC) says its water network serves 34,424 registered households or an estimated 1.03 per cent of the state’s 20 million residents.

The corporation, through the Deputy Director, Corporate Affairs and Brand Management, Rasaq Anifowoshe, disclosed this in an exclusive interview with the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) in Lagos.

Mr Anifowoshe said this while responding to questions bordering on the LWC’s water coverage and expansion plans.

“Using an estimated average household size of six persons, the number of residents associated with these connections is 206,444, an equivalent to approximately 1.03 per cent of the state’s estimated population of 20 million,” he said.

Mr Anifowoshe disclosed that the corporation had an installed water production capacity of approximately 210 million gallons per day (MGD).

This, he said, was against an estimated state’s daily water demand of approximately 540 MGD, as stated in the Lagos State Water Supply Master Plan.

“A review of the corporation’s 2025 production records indicates an aggregate annual production of approximately 2,633.22 million gallons, equivalent to an average daily production of about 7.21 MGD.

“Based on these records, actual daily production is three per cent of the installed capacity,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

NAN reports that the above figures highlight a substantial gap between installed capacity, actual output and estimated water demand across Lagos State.

Mr Anifowoshe identified ageing distribution pipelines, increasing demand arising from population growth and rapid urbanisation as well as the need to rehabilitate and expand existing water infrastructure as the major constraints.

NAN reports that these challenges affect the corporation’s ability to extend public water supply, particularly to communities relying on boreholes and private vendors.

Across Lagos, residents spend thousands of naira on alternative water sources as irregular public supply and inaccessible connections increase household costs.

Some Lagos residents interviewed by the NAN across Iponri, Oworonshoki, Costain, Apapa Road and Ebute Metta revealed concerns about unreliable supply, failed facilities and inadequate water pressure.

At the Iponri Housing Estate, Adebayo Solomon, said his household spent about N1,500 daily on vendor-supplied water, amounting to N45,000 monthly.

Mr Solomon said the expenditure would total approximately N547,500 if sustained throughout the year.

He said electricity shortages sometimes disrupted water availability, forcing his household to manage stored supplies or pay higher rates.

Mr Solomon said he would welcome an LWC connection if it provided regular supply and reduced dependence on vendors.

Another Iponri resident, Abdulkareem Ibrahim, said he relied on public boreholes provided by philanthropists because his community received no LWC supply.

“I depend on public water, the one provided by philanthropists. I fetch it in the morning or when I return from work at night,” he said.

Mr Ibrahim said the boreholes helped him avoid direct water expenses, although power interruptions sometimes disrupt pumping, forcing him to buy from vendors.

“I am just happy that we have water at all, all thanks to our magnanimous neighbours,” he said.

In Oworonshoki, Amanda Ogbodo, said she spent between N2,200 and N3,600 weekly on vendor-delivered borehole water.

Mrs Ogbodo said the expenditure amounts to between N8,800 and N14,400 over four weeks.

She said the LWC water had flowed more consistently in parts of her area over the preceding four months, mainly from Friday afternoons into Saturday.

However, she disclosed that homes on the higher ground remained underserved because of insufficient pressure, leaving residents on the lower ground better supplied.

She recalled that her business premises previously received LWC water, with eight or nine users contributing N10,000 monthly.

Mrs Ogbodo said supply stopped for about four years after a pipe broke and residents were told repairs were necessary.

She said water returned intermittently in 2025 but had only recently become more consistent.

“Electricity shortages over the preceding two weeks had also reduced availability and increased water costs.

“We plead with the government to help us run the pipe again and resume provision of constant water access,” she said.

At Costain, Eniola Adewale, said a truckload of water costs between N1,200 and N1,500, with vendors sometimes doubling prices during shortages.

She said her household relied on mobile vendors because the public facility was distant and supplied water irregularly.

Ms Adewale said she distrusted vendor-supplied water because its source was unknown, using sachet water for cooking instead.

Eunice David, a food vendor on Thomas Street, Costain, said she spent substantial amounts monthly pumping water for household use.

Mrs David said a public water facility previously serving her community had been non-functional for some time.

“We don’t know what to do again. We need help from the government,” she said, appealing for regular and affordable public water,” he said.

On Opeoluwa Street, Apapa Road, Garuba Alasan, said the public water facility had been non-functional for about 20 years.

“I have lived here for about 30 years, and in the past 20 years, I have used private water sources for my water needs,” he said.

At Vaughan Street in Costain, Anthony Olamide, a point-of-sale operator, said residents had an LWC connection, although supply depended largely on electricity.

Mr Olamide said residents contributed N1,000 monthly towards water supply, reducing alternative-water expenses when public water was available.

However, power outages stopped supply, sometimes forcing households to buy from vendors.

At Olaogun Street, Abule-Nla Junction Ebute Metta, Esther Emokpaire said her household spent between N1,000 and N1,500 per truckload of vendor-supplied water.

She said the household usually purchased water every two days, with prices varying according to availability.

Mrs Emokpaire said vendors claimed the water was clean and treated, although her household had not verified its quality.

“There was a time when members of my household developed skin rashes after bathing with water purchased from vendors,” she said.

She added that shortages made water harder to obtain and sometimes prompted vendors to increase prices.

Residents’ accounts show how irregular supply, failed facilities and inadequate pressure leave households paying for alternatives, including in communities with existing public connections.

Their experiences raise questions about the reach of public water infrastructure, supply reliability and whether announced interventions are translating into improved access.

However, the Lagos State Government’s second-quarter 2026 budget implementation report showed that 36.2 per cent of the approved annual budget for improving 15 existing mini and micro waterworks had been spent by June 30.

The report also recorded expenditure equivalent to four per cent of the approved annual budget for the Adiyan Phase II Waterworks project.

These expenditure figures do not establish the projects’ physical completion status or how much water they currently supply.

Speaking on the corporation’s plan for increasing public water coverage across the state, Mr Anifowoshe disclosed plans of rehabilitation and upgrade of micro/mini treatment plants.

“This will make water accessible to over 5,616,000 households upon full rehabilitation, thereby fulfilling the mandate of the corporation to provide potable water to Lagosians,” he said.

He also identified extension of distribution network to increase access to potable water for Lagosians as another plan.

Meanwhile, the corporation has announced plans to rehabilitate Ojokoro Mini Waterworks and construct Lagos Island Micro Waterworks to improve public water supply.

Mr Anifowoshe also listed the rehabilitation and upgrading of micro and mini water treatment plants among the corporation’s planned interventions.

He said the intervention would make water accessible to more than 5.6 million households upon full rehabilitation.

He listed digitisation of the distribution network as another planned intervention to enable digital monitoring and remote management of underground pipes and other assets.

According to Anifowoshe, the initiative will help reduce water losses and non-revenue water.

He also disclosed plans to construct the Igbonla 100 MGD water treatment plant to boost supply along the Lekki-Epe corridor.

“This will increase the production capacity of the corporation to meet the demand for water in the Lekki-Epe corridor,” he said.

For residents who continue spending thousands of naira on alternative water sources, the impact of these interventions will ultimately depend on reliable supply, functioning facilities and wider household connections across Lagos State.

(NAN)

World.title: 2027: Jigawa Fulani community endorses Tinubu, Namadi, commends livestock development initiatives
World.content:
The Fulani Community in Jigawa State has endorsed President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, Governor Umar Namadi, and all aspirants seeking elective positions under the platform of the All Progressives Congress (APC) ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The endorsement was announced during a community gathering organised under the leadership of Shehu Hadejia, at the Manpower Development Institute, Dutse, to appreciate the Jigawa State Government for its efforts to promote peaceful coexistence between farmers and herders and its interventions to improve livestock development across the state.

Speaking at the event, the community leader, Shehu Hadejia, said the gathering was organised to acknowledge the government’s role in sustaining peaceful relations between farming and herding communities, as well as the establishment of the Ministry of Livestock Development.

He particularly commended the government for initiatives introduced through the ministry, including the gazetting of grazing reserves, animal vaccination programmes and other interventions aimed at improving livestock production and addressing the needs of herders.

Governor Namadi, in his remarks, described the gathering as an important event, saying that members of the Fulani community had come from different parts of the state to express appreciation to the government and declare their support for the president, the governor, and APC candidates.

“Today is also another important day for us. Today, the entire Fulani community in Jigawa State is here,” he said.

He further said that the gathering demonstrated the community’s position on the political developments ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“You can see the number of people who came from all over the state. And they were here to endorse Mr President, the Governor, and all the APC candidates in Jigawa State.”

The governor reiterated his administration’s efforts to address challenges facing livestock owners through the provision of grazing areas, watering stations, and the cultivation of alfalfa to provide feed for animals.

“We have provided watering stations in every location. We are also working to grow alfalfa so that there will be sufficient food for the animals.

“We are ready to provide feed. We are ready to provide water, hospitals, schools, and everything else for them.

Governor Namadi also stated that the state had invested about ₦3.1 billion in artificial insemination over the last two to three years to improve cattle breeds and increase milk production, and has been undertaking regular animal vaccination for the protection of livestock health.

He emphasised that peaceful coexistence between farmers and herders remained essential to sustaining the peace and stability enjoyed in Jigawa State, urging communities to continue cooperating with government and security agencies to identify and report individuals whose activities could threaten public peace.

Also speaking, the Commissioner for Livestock Development, Professor Salim Mohammed, highlighted programmes and achievements recorded by the ministry within its relatively short period of establishment.

He listed the demarcation of additional grazing reserves, animal vaccination programmes and sensitisation campaigns promoting peaceful coexistence between farmers and herders among the ministry’s key interventions.

World.title: Abiodun mourns
World.content:
Ogun State Governor, Prince Dapo Abiodun, has expressed deep sorrow over the death of the Ogun State Sector Commander of the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC), Corps Commander Oludare Ogunjobi, describing his passing as a painful loss to the Corps, the road safety community and the nation.

Governor Abiodun commiserated with the Corps Marshal and the national leadership of the FRSC in Abuja, the management, officers and men of the Corps across the country, as well as the family, friends and professional associates of the deceased.

The governor noted that the late Ogunjobi’s commitment to road safety administration, public enlightenment and stakeholder engagement reflects the importance of dedicated service to the protection of lives and property.

He observed that the late Sector Commander played an important role in promoting responsible road use, improving compliance with traffic regulations and advancing efforts to make Ogun State’s roads safer for motorists and other road users.

Governor Abiodun described the death as a painful loss, particularly at a time when the collective efforts of road safety officials remain critical to reducing road traffic crashes and protecting the lives of citizens.

While praying for the peaceful repose of the deceased’s soul, he urged his family, colleagues and associates to take solace in the worthy service he rendered to the nation.

He prayed that God would grant the bereaved family, the FRSC national leadership, officers and men of the Corps, and all those affected by the loss the strength and fortitude to bear this irreparable loss.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times

World.title: Jigawa governor commissions ₦3.5bn asphalt and precast plant to boost indigenous constructions
World.content:
Jigawa State Governor, Umar Namadi has commissioned an industrial facility established by ALREN Construction Company comprising an asphalt plant, a concrete batching plant and a precast plant. The facility is located in Dutse, the Jigawa State capital.

The facility which represents an investment of approximately ₦3.5 billion, is expected to improve local access to construction materials, reduce sourcing challenges for contractors and stimulate economic activities across the state.

Speaking while opening the facility, the governor reaffirmed the Jigawa State Government’s commitment to strengthening indigenous contractors and expanding employment opportunities through private-sector investment.

Speaking at the commissioning ceremony, Governor Namadi said the investment aligned with his administration’s 12-Point Agenda, particularly its focus on private-sector partnership, employment generation and economic expansion.

“One of our 12-Point Agenda is in action today in this place. That is a partnership with the private sector to generate employment and increase economic activities in Jigawa State,” he said.

The Governor said that the facilities would provide indigenous contractors, particularly small-scale operators, with easier access to asphalt and other essential construction materials without having to travel outside the state to procure them.

According to Governor Namadi, the availability of these materials within Jigawa would reduce operational difficulties for local contractors, strengthen their capacity to execute projects and support the growth of indigenous businesses in the construction industry.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Our indigenous small contractors in Jigawa State will now have no reason to travel outside Jigawa State to get asphalt for the work they are doing.”

The governor described the investment as an example of how private-sector participation could complement government efforts to expand economic opportunities, strengthen local enterprises and create sustainable employment.

He said that the facilities had already employed 265 people, all of them indigenes of Jigawa State, adding that the company’s chairman had pledged to increase the workforce at the facilities to 500 by the first quarter of 2027.

Governor Namadi also stated that the employment generated by the investment would stimulate economic activities through workers’ earnings and contribute to government revenue.

He commended ALREN Construction Company for investing in Jigawa State and assured the company of the government’s continued cooperation and support.

“The Jigawa State Government will continue to work with you, because you are a very good partner to us.”

The governor further encouraged the company to explore investment opportunities in other sectors of the state’s economy, reiterating his administration’s commitment to maintaining an enabling environment for private businesses to thrive.

Speaking earlier, the Managing Director of ALREN Construction Company, Engr. Salim El Ters, said the investment was designed to strengthen the company’s operational capacity, support construction development and create employment opportunities.

“Our main concern today is to strengthen our capacity to support construction development and create valuable employment opportunities,” he said.

Engr. El Ters disclosed that the company planned to increase its overall workforce from 935 to approximately 1,170 employees, with about 30 per cent of the additional employees expected to be recruited from Jigawa State.

He expressed appreciation to the state government for its support and for creating an environment conducive to private-sector investment.

World.title: Governor donates ₦60m to Offa hospital project, awards scholarships to 50 students
World.content:
Kwara State Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq has donated ₦50 million to an ongoing hospital project in Offa and awarded scholarships worth ₦10 million to 50 students of an Arabic institution in the community.

The governor made the donations during the Annual Maolud Nabiy celebration organised by the Chief Imam of Offa, Muyideen Hussein, in Offa, Kwara State.

The donations comprise ₦50 million for the hospital project and ₦200,000 each for 50 students, bringing the total support to ₦60 million.

Speaking at the event, Mr Hussein commended the governor for his support for the Offa community, his institution and the Adabiyyah movement.

The cleric said Governor AbdulRazaq’s interventions and projects in the community had strengthened residents’ appreciation of his administration.

“I am welcoming Your Excellency to Offa, your second home. We are pleased to receive you today. We welcome you, because you are a true philanthropist and a blessing to the Offa community,” he said.

Mr Hussein also expressed gratitude for the governor’s support for the hospital project, which is currently under construction, as well as his contributions to the institution and its students.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The Olofa of Offa, Oba Mufutau Gbadamosi, also thanked Mr AbdulRazaq for the donations and other forms of support to the Chief Imam and the people of Offa.

ALSO READ: Kwara governor denies inflating hospital contracts

The monarch described the governor’s personal attendance at the celebration as a great honour to the community and prayed for his success in office and his political ambition.

The Maolud celebration brought together Islamic scholars, traditional rulers, political leaders and other stakeholders.

Among those present were the Khalifatul Adabiyyah, Sheikh Mustapha Al-Adabiy; the All Progressives Congress deputy governorship candidate, Seun Ogunniyi; the Chairman of Offa Local Government, Sulaiman Omituntun; Wahab Agbaje; and Hassan Oyeleke.

The event formed part of activities celebrating the birth of Prophet Muhammad and the religious institution’s contributions to Islamic learning.

World.title: PREMIUM TIMES’ journalists, others named finalists of African Investigative Journalism Awards
World.content:
Two PREMIUM TIMES’ journalists who worked on a collaborative investigation that unravelled lead poisoning linked to battery recycling in Nigeria have been named among the three finalists for the 2026 African Investigative Journalist of the Year Awards.

The investigation was led by the editor of the Business and Economy desk of PREMIUM TIMES, Oladeinde Olawoyin, and an award-winning investigative reporter, Folashade Ogunrinde.

The Wits Centre for Journalism, supported by Absa Africa, is organising the award in its fourth year to recognise outstanding investigative reporting across Africa that reveals untold stories, holds the powerful to account, questions those in public life, and serves the public interest.

The 2026 African Investigative Journalism Conference (AIJC), where the winner and runners-up will be announced at a gala ceremony on 11 November, is scheduled to be held from 10 to 12 November at the Edge Convention Centre in Nairobi, Kenya.

This year’s edition attracted over 200 entries across the continent, and the quality of investigative reporting made it challenging for the judges to select finalists.

“Judging these awards is never an easy process as there is so much valuable investigative journalism happening on our continent now,” said the convenor of judges, Gwen Lister.

He noted that judges had to assess the investigative work of shortlisted finalists against strict criteria, sparking vibrant debates and in-depth discussions on the merits and impact of the submissions.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“As judges, we all hope that striving for the prestigious title of African Investigative Journalist of the Year will spur on journalists across the continent to even greater heights,” Mr Lister added.

Dinesh Balliah, the director of the Wits Centre for Journalism, said the award reaffirmed journalism’s role in holding power to account in the context of a lack of resources, ongoing threats of violence and death and misinformation/disinformation.

“I wish we could recognise every one of the entrants through these awards, but it is impossible. The top three, though, represent all of these incredible journalists and their impactful work,” Mr Balliah said.

Daniel Munslow, managing executive of group communications at Absa Group, said the organisation recognises the critical role investigative journalism plays in strengthening transparency, accountability and public trust, which is why it celebrates some of the continent’s finest journalistic talent and the important work they do in bringing vital issues to light.

“The 2026 Absa African Investigative Journalist of the Year Award celebrates some of the continent’s finest journalistic talent and the important work they do in bringing vital issues to light.

“We are proud to support a platform that champions excellence in journalism and contributes to building more informed, resilient and prosperous societies across Africa,” Mr Munslow stated.

The entry

From a longlist of five, PREMIUM TIMES’ investigation, ‘Lead In Their Blood / Poor Oversight, Regulatory Failure Expose Nigerians to Slow Death from Battery Recycling’, by Mr Olawoyin and Ms Ogunrinde of PREMIUM TIMES with The Examination, Nigeria, was shortlisted alongside two other investigative reports.

They are ‘Your Eyes, Their Data’ by Naipanoi Lepapa, Kenya, in collaboration with Julia Lindblom of Göteborgs-Posten and Ahmed Abdigadir of Svenska Dagbladet, and ‘Nine Lives: King Cat and His Tender Empire’ by Jeff Wicks of News24, South Africa.

The investigation examined the health and environmental consequences of lead-acid battery recycling in parts of Africa, with PREMIUM TIMES reporting extensively from Ogijo, a community in Ogun State where several battery recycling factories operate.

The report found that residents and workers around the factories had been exposed to dangerous levels of lead pollution.

To provide scientific evidence for the investigation, the project commissioned independent blood lead testing for 70 residents, along with soil and air quality sampling around battery recycling plants in Ogun State.

Of the 70 people who volunteered for blood tests, seven out of every 10 recorded harmful levels of lead, according to the investigation. Every worker tested was also found to have been poisoned.

More than half of the children tested had lead levels high enough to cause lifelong brain damage, the investigation reported.

Soil and dust samples collected around the factories also showed extensive contamination, with some recording lead concentrations far above levels generally regarded as hazardous.

The investigation estimated that more than 20,000 people lived within a mile of the factories.

PREMIUM TIMES published its Nigerian investigation in two parts. The first report, “Lead In Their Blood: How Battery Recyclers Are Poisoning Nigerians,” documented the health risks faced by residents and workers in Ogijo.

The second, “Poor Oversight, Regulatory Failure Exposes Nigerians to Slow Death from Battery Recycling,” examined failures by regulatory authorities and the conditions that allowed the hazardous operations to continue.

The investigation also examined the international supply chain, tracing Nigeria’s recycled lead to overseas buyers and the global automotive industry.

The broader project found that recycled lead from Nigerian factories entered international supply chains used to produce car batteries.

It documented how one American battery manufacturer, East Penn Manufacturing, bought Nigerian lead through the global trading company Trafigura. Following the reporting, the company said it would stop importing the Nigerian lead and introduce additional scrutiny of its lead purchases.

Impact & Recognitions

Following the publication, the National Environmental Standards and Regulations Enforcement Agency shut down battery recycling facilities in Ogijo over environmental concerns.

The Ogun State Government also announced measures in response to the findings, including plans to test residents for lead exposure, while the House of Representatives called for an investigation into lead poisoning concerns in Ogijo and demanded an emergency response.

The state government and Lagos State Government also began a joint investigation into the pollution threat, while the Ogun government moved to suspend lead exports and shut affected battery recycling plants.

Nigerian authorities later moved to close factories linked to the US automotive industry amid the lead-poisoning investigation.

The reporting project has since been recognised for its depth and impact, winning PREMIUM TIMES’ standout report of 2025.

In September, it was named a finalist in two categories of the 2026 Online Journalism Awards in the United States.

The project has also received other international recognition, especially in the United States.

The project won the Selden Ring Award for Investigative Reporting from USC Annenberg and the John B. Oakes Award for environmental journalism.

It also won the Edward R. Murrow Awards for Investigative Reporting (Large Digital Organisation) and Best Video/Documentary about international affairs from the Overseas Press Club.

It won the Scripps Howard Journalism Awards, receiving both the Impact Award and the Excellence in Environmental Reporting Award.

In the Gerald Loeb Awards, it was named a finalist in the Video News category.

Mr Olawoyin, a multiple award-winning journalist, leads several projects at PREMIUM TIMES and mentors and supervises reporters.

Apart from his reporting of global economic issues across parts of Africa and the rest of the world, Mr Olawoyin’s reporting and research interests sit at the intersection of media framing and the impact of AI on the future of work, especially in the informal economy in Nigeria, sub-Saharan Africa, and the Global South.

Ms Ogunrinde is an award-winning investigative journalist recognised for her work in governance, accountability and inclusive development.

World.title: NDLEA intercepts N6.98bn tramadol shipment at Lagos port, arrests suspects across states
World.content:
The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) has intercepted 8,725 kilogrammes of powdered tramadol worth more than N6.98 billion at the Apapa port in Lagos, after discovering that a shipment from India, declared as maize starch, contained the controlled drug.

In a statement shared with PREMIUM TIMES on Sunday by the agency’s Director of Media and Advocacy, Femi Babafemi, the consignment comprised 349 bags, which laboratory analysis confirmed contained tramadol hydrochloride.

Mr Babafemi stated that at the Tincan port, officers also seized 55 kilogrammes of Canadian Loud, a strain of cannabis valued at N165 million. The substance was concealed in a Toyota Sienna inside a 40-foot container.

Arrests in Lagos

In Lagos, NDLEA operatives raided a store in Idumota and arrested Elizabeth Chidera Kalu. They recovered 10,600 ampoules of diazepam and 6,500 tablets of Molly, according to the agency.

Two men were arrested in separate operations in Mushin. Idowu Daudu, 35, was found with 59.95 kilogrammes of cannabis, while Ahmed Oniyinde, 35, had 61.23 kilogrammes.

Officers also intercepted a truck travelling from the Trade Fair market along the Iyana Oba axis. A search revealed 18,000 tablets of 250mg tramadol hidden in cartons labelled as Rambo insecticide.

The agency identified the suspects as Tajudeen Adeduntan, a loading manager, and his assistant, Azeez Sikiru.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

85-year-old woman among suspects arrested in Edo

In Edo State, six suspects were arrested during raids conducted between 15 and 16 October in Warake, Ivhiaro, Ewe and Irue communities in Owan East Local Government Area.

Grace Ehimeka, 85, was found with 179 kilogrammes of cannabis, while Ayo Aigberadion, 53, had 220.8 kilogrammes.

The other suspects were Ali Garba, 57, who was found with 5.852 kilogrammes of cannabis; Habib Braimoh, 45, with 100 grammes; Musa Mubid, 35, with two kilogrammes of cannabis, seeds, tramadol, Swinol and diazepam; and Hope Okoro, 35, with 237 grammes of Loud.

Ms Ehimeka’s arrest comes weeks after PREMIUM TIMES reported the rearrest of another elderly woman, Uloma Sunday, 83, in Abia State.

Ms Sunday was arrested on 7 October, months after she and her daughter, Chisom Uchechi, 32, were convicted in a drug-related case.

The pair were arrested in May 2025 after officers recovered 50 grammes of methamphetamine, 522 grammes of cannabis, 260 grammes of fresh cannabis leaves and 12 grammes of tramadol. They pleaded guilty and were sentenced to 12 months’ imprisonment or a fine of N200,000 each. Both paid their fines and were released.

During her latest arrest, Ms Sunday was allegedly found with methamphetamine and Colorado, a synthetic cannabinoid, concealed around her waist in a wrapper.

The NDLEA said intelligence reports indicated that she operated a drug joint where criminal suspects gathered and terrorised residents. The agency did not state whether she had been charged over the latest seizure.

The cases involving Ms Sunday and Ms Ehimeka are separate. The agency has not linked the two women.

NDLEA destroys cannabis farm in Ondo

In Ondo State, officers destroyed a cannabis farm covering three hectares in the Okemoro Isinbode camp forest on 17 October. The plants were estimated to weigh 7,500 kilogrammes.

Five suspects were arrested during the operation: Asikpo Ekpeyoung, 43; Solomon Okpani, 22; Ubong Friday, 35; Joseph Friday, 22; and Ekenimi Seth, 35.

Officers also recovered 92 bags of cannabis weighing 1,267 kilogrammes, 11 kilogrammes of cannabis seeds and three kilogrammes of fresh cannabis stems. The recovered exhibits weighed 1,281 kilogrammes, separate from the plants destroyed at the farm.

In another operation, officers arrested Okunebe Ndidi, 53, in the Ameyinti area of Owo on 16 October. They recovered 25 bags of cannabis weighing 375 kilogrammes.

Seizures in Bauchi and Kano

In Bauchi State, officers intercepted Shamsu Garba, 35, at Ragwam village in Katagum Local Government Area on 14 October. He was travelling in a Volkswagen Golf wagon carrying 894,800 pills, identified by the agency as tramadol capsules and Exol-5 tablets.

On the same day, officers recovered 291 blocks of cannabis weighing 265 kilogrammes from an abandoned vehicle at Tudun Natsira, along the Bauchi-Gombe road.

In Kano State, Ali Abdullahi, 38, and Ibrahim Adamu, 23, were arrested along the Zaria-Kano road on 13 October with 30,100 tablets of tramadol, 225mg.

A day later, officers arrested Murtala Dayyabu, 54, on Niger Street in the Malan Kato area with 100,000 tablets of Exol-5.

At the airport, a 16-year-old passenger, Fatimah Ahmad, was arrested on 16 October while preparing to board an Ethiopian Airlines flight to Jeddah via Addis Ababa.

The agency noted that she was carrying 511.75 grammes of cannabis concealed in a gallon of palm oil.

Ms Ahmad reportedly told officers that her cousin, Abubakar Yahaya, had given her the substance. He was subsequently arrested at the airport car park.

Further arrests in Kaduna and Abuja

In Kaduna State, officers arrested Mohammed Sani, 48; Zaharadeen Shafiu, 29; and Yakubu Abdullahi, 20, during a raid in Kayimi village. They recovered 496.5 kilogrammes of cannabis.

At Food Palace on Ali Akilu Road, officers arrested John Ayo David, 39, with 49,500 tablets of tramadol, 225mg.

In Abuja, Odo Jonas Ejike, 42, was arrested in Utako on 17 October with 29,500 tramadol capsules, the agency said.

NDLEA holds anti-drug awareness campaigns

The agency also held awareness programmes under its War Against Drug Abuse (WADA) campaign at schools and other institutions in several states.

The activities took place at Nawar-Ur-Deen High School in Ogboro, Oyo State; Elf Junior Secondary School in Bojude, Gombe State; Cherubim and Seraphim Primary School in Ikorodu, Lagos State; Harmony Secondary School in Lokoja, Kogi State; and Government Secondary School in Ikot Ansa, Calabar, Cross River State.

Other sessions were held at Rivers State College of Health Science and Management Technology in Port Harcourt, Mesh International School in Benin City, Edo State, and Abu Hanifa Academy in Kano Municipal.

NDLEA chairman Buba Marwa commended officers involved in the operations, including personnel at the Apapa and Tincan ports, the Murtala Muhammed International Airport, and the agency’s commands in Lagos, Edo, Bauchi, Ondo, Kano and the Federal Capital Territory.

He urged them to sustain efforts against drug trafficking and abuse.

World.title: Strike: SSANU suspends two-week ultimatum
World.content:
–Urges FG to reciprocate by releasing 2023 25%/35% salary award arrears, two months’ withheld salaries

By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

ABUJA — THE Senior Staff Association of Nigerian Universities (SSANU) has announced the suspension of the two-week ultimatum issued to the Federal Government to release funds for the implementation of the 2026 FGN/SSANU Agreement.

The suspension, according to a statement issued by the association’s National President, Comrade Mohamed Ibrahim, followed the approval and release of eight months’ arrears by the Federal Government on October 7, 2026.
