Recall that SSANU, at its 56th National Executive Council (NEC) meeting in the University of Uyo, resolved to issue a two-week ultimatum to the Federal Government to release funds for the implementation of the 2026 Agreement, failing which it would embark on a total and indefinite strike.

The Federal Government promptly responded, within two days of the issuance of the ultimatum, by releasing funds for the payment of eight months’ arrears (January to August 2026).

Consequently, arising from its National Administrative Committee (NAC) meeting, SSANU has withdrawn the ultimatum.

In a statement titled, “Notification of the Suspension of the Two-Week Ultimatum Issued to the Federal Government,” the association stated that the decision reflected its commitment to constructive engagement, peaceful dialogue and the maintenance of cordial relations with the government.

The statement read: “Following the two-week ultimatum issued to the Federal Government by the Senior Staff Association of Nigerian Universities (SSANU), which commenced on October 5, 2026, and the subsequent approval and release of eight months’ arrears by the Federal Government on October 7, 2026, the National Administrative Committee (NAC), acting on behalf of the National Executive Council (NEC), wishes to formally inform and notify members of SSANU and the general public of its decision to suspend the ultimatum.

“At its meeting, the NAC took cognisance of the Federal Government’s prompt release of funds for the payment of eight months’ arrears of CONTTA owed to SSANU members for the period of January to August 2026.

“In recognition of this positive development, mutual understanding and good faith, the NAC, on behalf of the NEC, has resolved to suspend the intended industrial action.

“This decision reflects the union’s commitment to constructive engagement, peaceful dialogue and the maintenance of cordial relations with the government, particularly in the interest of sustaining industrial harmony in our citadels of learning.

“While acknowledging this development, the union urges the Federal Government to reciprocate this gesture by fulfilling all other outstanding demands, which include the release and payment of the one-year arrears of the 25% and 35% salary award of 2023 and the two months’ 2022 withheld salaries.

“It also urges state governments that are yet to implement the 2026 signed agreement to pay other outstanding arrears to our members in state universities.

“The union remains committed to dialogue but expects the government to demonstrate the same level of goodwill by taking concrete steps towards resolving all outstanding issues affecting our members across federal and state universities.

“All NEC members are hereby notified of this decision and are encouraged to communicate the position of the NAC accordingly. We must continue to engage constructively with relevant stakeholders to preserve the peace in our citadels of learning, while remaining steadfast in the pursuit of the welfare and legitimate interests of our members.

“Thank you for your continued commitment and solidarity.”

World.title: Police arrest 95 suspected ‘Vikings’ cultists in Delta, recover five guns
World.content:
The Delta State Police Command has arrested 95 suspected cultists and recovered five firearms, 12 live cartridges and seven expended cartridges during coordinated operations across four local government areas of the state.

The operations, conducted on October 15, 2026, targeted suspected cultists in Asaba, Ika South, Ughelli South and Okpe local government areas, according to a statement issued by the Police Public Relations Officer, SP Bright Edafe, on Friday.

The recovered firearms comprised two pump-action guns, one locally fabricated cut-to-size gun and two locally made pistols.

The police said the operations involved operatives of the Department of Operations, Rapid Response Squad (RRS) and Command Anti-Cultism Unit (CACU), acting on intelligence about suspected cult activities.

In Asaba, operatives raided a hotel along Abraka Road following intelligence that suspected members of the Supreme Vikings Confraternity (SVC), also known as Aro Bagger, had gathered for an alleged cult anniversary celebration.

The operation led to the arrest of 67 suspects, comprising 55 males and 12 females.

Police said they recovered two pump-action guns, one locally fabricated cut-to-size gun, 10 live cartridges, five expended cartridges, 11 caps bearing suspected cult insignia and two jackets bearing suspected cult branding.

In a related operation in Agbor, Ika South Local Government Area, RRS operatives arrested 15 additional suspects, comprising 14 males and one female, over suspected links to the same confraternity.

The command also reported an operation at Jeremy Community in Ughelli South Local Government Area, where operatives of the Command Anti-Cultism Unit, Ovwian-Aladja Sector, working with a civilian anti-cult group, raided a suspected criminal hideout.

Three suspects, identified as John Pius, 32; Oghene Ochuko, 28; and Akinbule Godstime, 24, were arrested, while others reportedly fled.

The police said two locally made pistols, two live cartridges, two expended cartridges, two caps bearing suspected cult insignia and suspected charms were recovered during the operation.

In another operation at Jeddo Community in Okpe Local Government Area, 10 additional male suspects were arrested over suspected cult activities.

The command said all the suspects and recovered exhibits were in police custody, while investigations were ongoing.

The Commissioner of Police, Samuel Erale, commended the operatives and directed area commanders, divisional police officers and tactical commanders to intensify operations against cult groups across the state.

He warned that the command would not tolerate cult-related activities capable of threatening public peace and urged residents to provide credible information to assist the police in tackling crime.

World.title: SEHRB, Intersociety allege killings, torture in South-East
World.content:
By Chinedu Adonu

ENUGU — A coalition of human rights organisations has called for an independent investigation into alleged killings, torture, enforced disappearances, secret burials and deaths in custody linked to security operations in South-East Nigeria.

The coalition, comprising the South-East Human Rights Bureau (SEHRB), Oganihu Igbo Development Foundation and the International Society for Civil Liberties and Rule of Law (Intersociety), also demanded a probe into reports of unidentified bodies in mortuaries in Imo State.

Addressing a joint press conference in Enugu on Saturday, the organisations alleged that some detainees had been subjected to prolonged detention without access to their families and lawyers, as well as torture and other forms of inhuman treatment.

They expressed concern that persons reportedly arrested in the South-East had been transferred to detention facilities outside the region, including Wawa Barracks in Niger State and custodial centres in Kuje and Suleja, without their families being adequately informed of their whereabouts.

“Our position is clear: the State has a duty to protect citizens from violence, but security operations must themselves comply with the law. Fighting lawlessness cannot justify lawlessness by the State,” the coalition said.

The organisations presented accounts from families whose relatives allegedly disappeared after being arrested by security operatives, with some reportedly remaining unaccounted for years after their arrest.

One of the cases highlighted was that of Ozioma Elizabeth Onyeaka, a 35-year-old teacher from Anambra State, who reportedly disappeared for more than five years before her family learnt that she was alive and being detained at Wawa Barracks.

The coalition also raised concerns over the case of Sunday Ifedi and his wife, Calista, who were reportedly arrested by operatives of the Department of State Services (DSS) in Enugu in 2021 and transferred to Wawa Barracks.

According to the organisations, Sunday regained his freedom after more than four years in detention, while Calista allegedly died in custody.

The coalition said allegations attributed to Sunday and human rights activist Omoyele Sowore indicated that Calista was buried in a shallow grave at Wawa Barracks.

It demanded an independent investigation into the circumstances surrounding her reported death, the disclosure of relevant custody and medical records, and the identification of her burial location.

The organisations said that if the allegations were established, her remains should be recovered and released to her family for a dignified burial.

Another case cited was that of Esther Okwudili Egbom, who was reportedly arrested by DSS operatives during a night prayer programme in Aba, Abia State, in February 2025.

Her daughter, Chiamaka, alleged that the operatives were searching for another person who had fled before their arrival but arrested her mother because she owned the ministry where the operation took place.

The family reportedly had not seen Egbom since the incident. Chiamaka also alleged that her brother was beaten during the operation and subsequently died.

The coalition demanded that the DSS account for Egbom’s whereabouts and investigate the circumstances surrounding the alleged death of her son.

Other testimonies presented by the organisations included allegations of torture, prolonged detention and denial of family contact involving persons reportedly arrested in Owerri, Orlu and other parts of the South-East.

The coalition said the allegations, if substantiated, could amount to serious violations of constitutional rights, the Anti-Torture Act 2017 and Nigeria’s international human rights obligations.

Probe of unidentified bodies

On reports of unidentified bodies in Imo State, the organisations called for independent forensic investigations to establish the identities of the deceased and determine the circumstances surrounding their deaths.

They demanded the preservation of mortuary registers, police records, autopsy reports and other relevant evidence, as well as the use of DNA testing where necessary to identify the remains.

The coalition urged the Federal Government, the Inspector-General of Police, the DSS, military authorities, the Attorney-General of the Federation and the National Human Rights Commission to establish an independent investigative mechanism to examine the allegations of disappearances, torture and deaths in custody.

It also called for a comprehensive audit of detention facilities to establish the identities and legal status of detainees, their custody histories and whether they had access to judicial safeguards.

The organisations, however, condemned killings, abductions and other atrocities allegedly committed by armed separatist elements, criminal gangs and other non-state actors in the region.

“There must be no hierarchy of victims,” they said, adding that civilians killed by armed criminals, persons unlawfully killed by security personnel, detainees who disappear in state custody, torture survivors and unidentified dead all deserved truth, justice and accountability.

The coalition urged the National Assembly, the Nigerian Bar Association, civil society groups, religious and traditional leaders, and the media to support credible investigations into the allegations.

“The missing must be accounted for. The detained must have access to justice. The dead must be identified and treated with dignity,” the organisations said.

World.title: Jigawa Fulani community endorses Tinubu, Namadi, APC candidates
World.content:
By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse

The Fulani community in Jigawa State has endorsed President Bola Tinubu, Governor Umar Namadi and all candidates of the All Progressives Congress (APC) ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The endorsement was announced at a gathering held at the Manpower Development Institute, Dutse, where community members commended the state government for its efforts to promote peaceful coexistence between farmers and herders.

Speaking at the event, the community leader, Alhaji Shehu Hadejia, said the decision to support APC candidates was in recognition of the government’s efforts to address the challenges facing livestock farmers across the state.

He particularly commended Namadi for establishing the Ministry of Livestock Development and introducing programmes aimed at improving livestock production and reducing conflicts between farmers and herders.

According to him, the gazetting of grazing reserves, regular animal vaccination and other livestock development initiatives have helped improve the welfare of herders in the state.

Responding, Namadi described the endorsement as a demonstration of the community’s confidence in his administration and the APC-led government.

“Today is also another important day for us. Today, the entire Fulani community in Jigawa State is here,” the governor said.

“You can see the number of people who came from all over the state. And they were here to endorse Mr President, the governor, and all the APC candidates in Jigawa State.”

Namadi reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to improving livestock production through the provision of grazing reserves, watering stations and animal feed.

He said the government was also promoting alfalfa cultivation to ensure adequate feed for livestock.

“We are ready to provide feeds. We are ready to provide water, hospitals, schools, and everything else for them,” he said.

The governor disclosed that his administration had invested about ₦3.1 billion in artificial insemination programmes over the past two to three years to improve cattle breeds and boost milk production.

He added that the government had sustained regular animal vaccination programmes to protect livestock against diseases.

Namadi also stressed the need for peaceful coexistence between farmers and herders, urging residents to cooperate with security agencies by providing information on individuals threatening peace in their communities.

Earlier, the Commissioner for Livestock Development, Professor Salim Mohammed, said the ministry had recorded significant achievements since its establishment.

He listed the demarcation of additional grazing reserves, animal vaccination and public sensitisation on peaceful coexistence among measures introduced to strengthen livestock development in the state.

World.title: ‘Why airlines may not get cheaper jet fuel despite local production’
World.content:
By Dickson Omobola

Aviation fuel marketer, CITA Energies, has said jet fuel marketers may not be able to significantly reduce the price of Jet A1 supplied to the country’s airlines due to the single-source supply arrangement, pricing disparities and rising operational costs.

This comes amid recent complaints by the country’s airlines over the high cost of aviation fuel, which accounts for at least 40 per cent of their operational expenses.

The company said the reliance on a single supplier had limited competition among marketers, leaving little room for notable price differences despite efforts to offer airlines cheaper fuel.

CITA Energies’ representatives spoke to newsmen on the sidelines of the company’s 20th anniversary celebration in Lagos.

Chairman of CITA, Dr Thomas Ogungbagbe, said the pricing structure for locally supplied aviation fuel had created difficulties for marketers, particularly because of the mismatch between the global pricing formula and the pricing arrangement adopted by Dangote Refinery.

Ogungbagbe said marketers operating under the global pricing formula used the average benchmark price for the preceding month, while Dangote’s pricing arrangement followed a different formula.

He said: “We still have issues with pricing because we are priced on the global formula pricing, and the global formula pricing does not recognise individual countries. The contracts are signed, for example, on a month minus one basis, using the average of prices published daily during the preceding month.

“This means that in October, we use the September average as our benchmark for selling. Meanwhile, in Dangote, it is BL plus five. So, you have a lot of mismatches, which means that once you load, five days may pass before you know the price. You can even be selling in Lagos without knowing the price at which you bought the product. That is the major gap.

“Second, we have a premium that was introduced sometime around March by Dangote, which has not been removed. It is not in line with the global pricing formula. What that means is that we can only pass it on to customers, and that is why the airlines are making noise.”

CITA chairman said Dangote Refinery had helped address aviation fuel scarcity in Nigeria, but maintained that pricing remained a major challenge for marketers.

He said: “You can’t even get N1,900 per litre. Nigeria had never produced jet fuel. Even the refineries we had before never produced jet fuel. Basically, Dangote is the first one. Dangote, being the first, has also brought a lot of opportunities and challenges. The opportunity is that the problem of scarcity has been eradicate d. Availability is assured.

“But the challenge is also in the pricing because, as I told you earlier, there is a nebulous premium that you pay on top of the average, which should not be there. That is why some people prefer to import, where they can get the real formula. We are still pleading with Dangote to help us remove this.”

Also speaking, Acting Managing Director of CITA Energy, Titilayo Olaore, said marketers reviewed their costs weekly to determine how competitive they could be and how much relief they could offer airlines.

She, however, said the current supply arrangement meant marketers were working with the same price, leaving little room for significant differences in the prices charged to airlines.

Olaore said: “It is a dynamic industry, and we have a one-source justification hazard now, which has led us and every other stakeholder that supplies aviation fuel to the airlines to rely on one price.

“With that price, we then build up whatever other costs come up along the way before we get to the airside. Every week, we look at our numbers. We try to work on how competitive we can be and how beneficial we can be to the airlines in terms of pricing, but we are working with one price.

“The times when we could work with multiple options, maybe there would be a bit more flexibility. But the fact is that we all get from one source now, and our prices vary within a N5 differential between us and the next person. So, the flexibility is not there.”

Meanwhile, CITA’s National Operations Manager, Dr Jeffrey Egbadon, lamented the international conflicts that had disrupted global supply chains, saying these were some factors responsible for the pressure on aviation fuel prices.

Egbadon fingered tensions involving Iran, Israel and the United States, disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz and the Russia-Ukraine war as factors affecting the availability and movement of petroleum products.

He said: “It has been challenging with aviation fuel, especially in terms of pricing. The war currently happening between Iran and Israel, as well as the tensions involving Israel and the United States, have also been a challenge because of the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

“Recently, the war involving Yemen and Saudi Arabia has also shown that there have been a lot of blockages in the movement of products into Africa and through African waters. You can also see what is happening between Russia and Ukraine. That is another major factor. What we see today is that many of the countries that produce these products are engaged in one conflict or another.”

World.title: Rainbow Coalition will fail in Kwara — Accord Party
World.content:
By Demola Akinyemi, Ilorin

The Accord Party in Kwara State has predicted that the Rainbow Coalition will fail to make the expected electoral impact in the state ahead of the 2027 general elections, arguing that the alliance is driven more by elite political realignments than grassroots support.

The party’s state publicity secretary, Olamilekan Esinrogunjo, stated this in a statement on the emerging political alignment made available to Vanguard on Sunday.

He described the coalition as flawed, alleging that it lacked a clear governance agenda and was driven largely by personality clashes.

Esinrogunjo also described the Rainbow Coalition as a credibility challenge because of what he called contradictions in its political positioning.

He questioned the decision to oppose the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Kwara while supporting President Bola Tinubu at the federal level, saying the arrangement could confuse voters and serve the interests of political elites rather than ordinary citizens.

“ You cannot claim to be opposition in Kwara and, at the same time, ask the same people to support the APC at the presidential level. That contradiction is one of the fundamental problems of the Rainbow Coalition,” he said.

The Accord Party spokesman also dismissed the suggestion that the movement of prominent politicians across party lines would automatically translate into electoral support.

“They can make noise here and there. Politicians can move from one party to another, but votes do not move automatically with them. An alliance of politicians is not necessarily an alliance of voters,” he said.

He further argued that the coalition’s reliance on political heavyweights and former officeholders to revive support for the Saraki political dynasty amounted to more political noise than electoral substance.

According to him, the coalition had yet to establish a clear message capable of attracting ordinary voters across the state.

“What is the Rainbow Coalition offering Kwarans beyond political realignment? Is it an opposition platform, a vehicle for supporting the President, a return to the defeated dynasty or simply an arrangement among politicians seeking new political opportunities?” he queried.

Esinrogunjo said the 2027 elections would not be determined solely by defections, endorsements or alliances among political elites, but by the ability of parties to connect with voters and present credible programmes.

He maintained that the Accord Party was offering an alternative across all levels of the elections, from the presidency to the state House of Assembly.

“Kwara is not anybody’s political inheritance. The people own their votes, and they will decide who gets their mandate,” he said.

The party spokesman insisted that Accord would continue to present itself as an opposition platform focused on policy, grassroots engagement and what he described as a “new direction” for the state.

He urged voters to look beyond politicians’ movement between parties and assess political platforms based on their programmes, candidates, records and capacity to address the challenges facing the state.

World.title: Borno loses billions in infrastructure to metal scavenging — Zulum
World.content:
By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri

Borno State Governor, Babagana Umara Zulum, has said the state has lost infrastructure, electrical materials and metals worth billions of naira to metal scavengers, known in Hausa as Ajakuta.

Zulum said the losses, alongside other security concerns, informed the state government’s decision to ban scrap metal trading.

The governor spoke at the weekend while addressing scrap metal operators, urging them to submit proposals on how they could continue their businesses without contributing to insecurity or damaging public infrastructure.

He explained that the ban was imposed in the overall interest of the state and was not intended to deprive operators of their means of livelihood.

Zulum said the government had no personal interest in shutting down their businesses, stressing that the restriction was aimed at protecting public assets and strengthening security.

“It is deeply concerning to me if one person loses his livelihood for whatever reason in Borno. Believe me, there is nothing I stand to gain from banning scrap metal trade other than addressing the serious security concerns associated with your activities,” he said.

The governor disclosed that the state government spent more than ₦3 billion to connect an electricity distribution line from Damaturu to Maiduguri, but the wires were subsequently lost to metal scavenging.

“We spent more than ₦3 billion to connect an electricity distribution line from Damaturu to Maiduguri, but unfortunately, we lost all the wires to metal scavenging activities,” he said.

Zulum also said hundreds of scavengers had been killed while searching for metals in villages that were not yet safe for civilian activities.

He added that security intelligence available to the government indicated that insurgents were using scrap metal trading channels to sell looted metals.

“We have security intelligence that even the insurgents use your platforms to sell looted metals. So, no responsible government will ignore such intelligence just to be politically correct,” the governor said.

Despite the restriction, Zulum granted operators a waiver to evacuate stocks accumulated before the ban from designated locations.

The measure, he said, was intended to ease the impact of the restriction on genuine operators while the government addressed the security and infrastructure concerns associated with the trade.

World.title: Oyebanji targets industrialisation, SMEs to drive Ekiti growth
World.content:
Governor Biodun Oyebanji of Ekiti State

…Governor plans agro-processing, cheaper transport, 24-hour airport operations

By Rotimi Ojomoyela

ADO-EKITI — Ekiti State Governor, Biodun Oyebanji, has said his administration will prioritise industrialisation, small business development and productivity in his second term to transform infrastructure investments into jobs, local manufacturing and economic growth.

Oyebanji said the government would expand support for small-scale entrepreneurs, strengthen agricultural value chains, attract private investors and introduce alternative transportation systems powered by compressed natural gas (CNG) and electricity to reduce operating costs.

The governor, who spoke in an interview on his second-term agenda, said the next phase of his administration would focus on ensuring that infrastructure developed during his first term translated into tangible economic benefits for residents.

According to him, his administration invested substantially in roads, electricity, agricultural infrastructure and other critical facilities during its first term, providing a foundation for increased production and economic activities.

He said the state had constructed roads linking communities, improved township roads and developed farm roads, adding that nearly 400 kilometres of roads would have been completed by the end of 2026.

Oyebanji, however, stressed that infrastructure development would continue alongside efforts to promote industries, expand businesses and improve the state’s economic fortunes.

He identified welders, tailors, hairdressers, barbers and other small-scale entrepreneurs as key beneficiaries of the proposed economic expansion, saying access to affordable financing would help them grow their businesses and create employment.

The governor also emphasised the need to strengthen agricultural production and establish reliable markets for farmers, arguing that locally produced commodities must be processed within the state to generate greater economic value.

On attracting private investment, Oyebanji said his administration was improving the business environment through reforms in land administration, taxation and regulatory processes.

He said the government was establishing a one-stop shop to enable prospective investors to obtain relevant information, approvals and services without unnecessary bureaucratic delays.

Oyebanji maintained that the government’s primary responsibility was to create an enabling environment for private capital rather than assume responsibility for establishing and operating industries itself.

On transportation, the governor said his administration was testing a pilot mass transit scheme to determine its effectiveness before expanding government investment in the sector.

He explained that the initiative was not intended to displace existing commercial transport operators but to introduce fair competition and provide residents with more affordable alternatives.

Oyebanji identified CNG-powered and electric vehicles as important components of the state’s long-term strategy to reduce transportation costs, noting that petrol-dependent operations continued to impose significant financial burdens on drivers and passengers.

He said discussions were ongoing with a company expected to introduce the initiative, which would extend beyond cars to include tricycles and motorcycles.

On aviation, Oyebanji said his administration was working to enable the state’s airport to operate round the clock, rather than close at 6 p.m. or face restrictions during adverse weather conditions.

He disclosed that an Instrument Landing System (ILS) had been installed and was undergoing assessment by a certification team, while a contract had been awarded for airport lighting infrastructure required to support night operations.

The governor also announced plans to commission a privately developed fuel depot at the airport, explaining that the facility would allow aircraft to refuel in Ekiti and make flight operations more convenient.

He said improved aviation facilities, agricultural investments and better road connectivity would support the state’s broader economic development strategy.

Speaking on his priorities, Oyebanji said: “Our next major focus, therefore, is industrialisation and support for small businesses. That is the only way we can deepen our shared prosperity agenda.

“Our farmers must also be able to produce at scale and have reliable off-takers who can purchase their produce and supply it to companies that will add value through processing.

“The responsibility of government is to create an enabling environment for investors to come in, establish businesses and create jobs.

“If the pilot scheme succeeds, the government will invest in transportation by procuring more vehicles that can compete with existing operators. I do not want to drive transport operators out of business.

“I am not in government to inflict hardship on anybody. I understand the challenges these operators face, and I will not introduce policies merely to win applause from some people at the expense of others.”

World.title: Sani, CJN: Healthy Judicial Personnel Vital to Justice Delivery
World.content:
John Shiklam in Kaduna

Kaduna State Governor, Senator Uba Sani, has said the wellbeing of judicial officers and staff is vital to the effective administration of justice.

He stated this in Kaduna on Saturday at the opening ceremony of the 32nd Annual Judiciary Sports Competition organised by the National Sports Association of Judiciary (NASAJ).

Represented by the Attorney General and Commissioner for Justice, James Kanyip, Sani said sports provided judicial personnel an opportunity to stay fit, build professional relationships and promote teamwork.

“The strength of our courts rests not only on laws, procedures, precedents and facilities, but on the competence, integrity and well-being of the people who serve in the courts,” Sani said.

The governor said the values promoted through sports were equally important in the courtroom.

“This competition gives judicial personnel a valuable opportunity to promote physical fitness, build professional relationships and enjoy healthy recreation.

“It also reinforces values that matter in the courtroom as much as on the field. Fairness, respect for rules of law, discipline, teamwork and regards and respect for others,” he said.

Sani described the judiciary as central to Nigeria’s constitutional democracy, saying the courts play vital roles in interpreting the law, resolving disputes, protecting rights and upholding the constitutional order.

He commended the Chief Justice of Nigeria (CJN), Justice Kudirat Kekere Ekun, for her attention to the welfare of judicial personnel.

The governor said hosting the competition in Kaduna demonstrated the state’s commitment to cooperation among public institutions.

He urged participants to compete with determination, respect the rules and honour one another.

Speaking while declaring the event opened, the CJN, Justice Kekere-Ekun, described sports as vital to the wellbeing and effectiveness of judicial personnel.

Represented by the Kaduna State Chief Judge, Justice Mohammed Tukur Muazu, the CJN said sports could promote physical fitness, relieve stress and improve the balance required for effective performance.

She said: “The effectiveness of judicial institutions depends, in part, on the well-being of the men and women who serve within them.”

According to her, the demanding responsibilities of judicial officers and staff required concentration, diligence, patience and sustained commitment.

“Equally important, sporting activities encourage teamwork, discipline, perseverance and respect for rules.

“These values are as relevant on the field of play as they are in the discharge of our respective professional responsibilities,” the CJN said.

She commended NASAJ for sustaining the annual competition, saying it had created an opportunity for judicial officers and staff from across the country to interact, renew friendships and strengthen fellowship.

She also expressed appreciation to the Kaduna State Government for hosting the competition.

The CJN urged the participating teams to compete with commitment, fairness and respect for their opponents.

Ealier in his welcome address, President of NASAJ, Comrade Noah Sunday, commended the CJN for the unwavering support and encouragement of sporting activities within the Nigerian judiciary.

World.title: NAFDAC Begins Probe of NYSC Member’s Death At Enugu Orientation Camp
World.content:
Ayodeji Ake

The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) has commenced an investigation into the death of a National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) member at the orientation camp in Agwu, Enugu State, dismissing claims that the deceased died from the effects of substandard or falsified medicines.

The agency said preliminary findings suggested that the cause of death was acute kidney injury secondary to severe dehydration and shock, while samples of medicines administered to the deceased had been collected for laboratory analysis.

In a statement issued by its Director-General, Prof. Mojisola Christianah Adeyeye, NAFDAC said its officers had visited the camp clinic, interviewed doctors and other healthcare personnel, and taken samples of the medicines used in treating the deceased for further investigation.

According to the agency, the corps member was brought to the clinic at about 9 p.m. on Wednesday, October 7, 2026, by two fellow corps members, with symptoms suggestive of severe malaria. He was also known to have peptic ulcer disease.

NAFDAC said he was stabilised with intramuscular antimalarial medication and other supportive treatments administered intravenously before being placed on bed rest for observation.

He was discharged on Thursday morning with oral medications.

The agency, however, said the corps member returned to the clinic unaided on Saturday, October 10, complaining of pain in his right thigh. He was advised to see a physiotherapist.

His condition subsequently raised concern when the attending doctor noticed that he was sweating profusely and checked his blood pressure, which was found to be critically low at 80/40mmHg.

NAFDAC said he was stabilised with intravenous normal saline, but repeated monitoring revealed recurrent episodes of low blood pressure.

His poor urine output, despite adequate fluid resuscitation, prompted the medical team to refer him to the University of Nigeria Teaching Hospital (UNTH), Ituku-Ozalla, Enugu State, in an ambulance accompanied by another doctor.

The corps member reportedly slipped into a coma around the time he arrived at the teaching hospital, and efforts to resuscitate him were unsuccessful.

The agency further disclosed that a friend of the deceased later informed the camp clinic doctor that the corps member had been vomiting for two days following his initial admission. The doctor was reportedly unaware of the development before the information was provided.

NAFDAC said the same medications administered to the deceased had also been given to several other patients at the camp clinic, who recovered after treatment.

It added that the doctors, pharmacists and other healthcare workers at the clinic had not only prescribed the medicines but had also used them themselves at different times.

The agency, however, said its investigation was ongoing, with laboratory analysis of the collected samples expected to help establish the quality and safety of the medicines involved.

NAFDAC urged members of the public to remain calm while it undertakes the necessary investigations, reiterating its commitment to ensuring that medicines available in the country are safe, of good quality and effective.

The agency also expressed condolences to the family of the deceased corps member, praying for strength for them to bear the loss.

World.title: Otu @ 67: The Sweet Prince And The  Odyssey of Renewed Hope
World.content:
Linus Obogo

On October 18, 2026, Cross Riverians will pause in affectionate reflection to celebrate the 67th birthday of His Excellency, Senator Prince Bassey Edet Otu, the governor whose political identity has become inseparable from the evocative sobriquet, the Sweet Prince. Yet, beyond the poetry of that appellation lies a compelling human story: the odyssey of a man whose journey through business, legislative service and executive leadership has been shaped by an enduring encounter with the aspirations, anxieties and expectations of his people.

Born on October 18, 1959, Otu’s life has traversed different seasons of responsibility, each preparing him, in its own peculiar way, for the demands of leadership. Before assuming the governorship in May 2023, Otu had established himself in the banking and petroleum sectors, experiences that broadened his understanding of enterprise, economic opportunity and the intricate relationship between public policy and human welfare. His subsequent emergence in the House of Representatives in 2003 marked the beginning of a consequential political journey that would take him through two chambers of the National Assembly and ultimately to the highest political office in Cross River State.

Between 2003 and 2011, representing Calabar Municipality/Odukpani Federal Constituency, Otu served in the House of Representatives, including as Chairman of the House Committee on Petroleum Resources (Upstream). His legislative responsibilities exposed him to the strategic questions surrounding petroleum governance, local content development and the equitable management of national resources. In 2011, he advanced to the Senate, representing Cross River South Senatorial District, where he chaired the Senate Committee on Finance and subsequently the Committee on Banking and Other Financial Institutions. These assignments placed him at the intersection of fiscal policy, financial regulation and national economic administration. They also furnished him with institutional experience that would later inform his approach to governing a state confronting formidable developmental challenges.

But political biographies are not written by official positions alone. Sometimes, their most enduring chapters are composed in the unrecorded encounters between a public figure and ordinary citizens. It is in this realm of personal generosity, accessibility and humanitarian disposition that Otu’s admirers locate the origins of his endearing title, the Sweet Prince. The sobriquet evokes an image of a politician whose relationship with the people extends beyond the formalities of office to the intimate obligations of compassion. It speaks to the expectation that power should possess a human face, that prosperity should be shared, and that the vulnerable should not become invisible beneath the weight of public administration. For his supporters, the name captures not merely a political identity but a disposition they associate with kindness, humility and the instinct to give.

His assumption of office as governor on May 29, 2023, therefore represented more than a change of political leadership; it marked the transition from legislative representation to the demanding business of governing an entire state. Under the banner of the People First Agenda, Otu has sought to reposition Cross River through a development philosophy that places human welfare, economic renewal and social inclusion at the centre of public policy. His more than three years in office have been characterised by interventions spanning agriculture, infrastructure, education, healthcare, technology, tourism and human-capital development.

A defining feature of this approach has been his commitment to continuity in governance. Rather than abandoning projects initiated by his predecessors, the administration has pursued the completion, consolidation and repositioning of strategic investments whose value extends beyond political tenures. The deep seaport, the Obudu Cargo Airport and the Adiabo-Ikoneto road projects are notable examples. By sustaining attention on these initiatives, Otu has demonstrated that development should be guided by long-term public interest rather than the changing fortunes of administrations. When completed and properly integrated into the state’s economic architecture, they could strengthen trade, logistics, tourism and regional connectivity, while creating new opportunities for employment and investment.

In agriculture, the administration has pursued a Green Economy Revolution, seeking to restore farming to its historic place in Cross River’s economic life. Its initiatives have included the ambitious 50,000-hectare rice production programme in Ndok, Ogoja; the distribution of farming inputs and equipment; support for smallholder farmers; and investments in agricultural value chains. Through complementary programmes involving cassava, oil palm, aquaculture and other commodities, the administration has sought to connect agricultural productivity with food security, employment and rural prosperity.

The ultimate test will be the sustainability of these interventions, their effect on farmers’ incomes and their capacity to make food more accessible to households.

Road infrastructure has similarly featured prominently in the administration’s development agenda. From urban road rehabilitation and drainage improvements in Calabar to interventions on connecting routes across the three senatorial districts, the objective is to make communities more accessible and commerce less burdensome. Roads are not merely ribbons of asphalt; they are economic arteries through which farmers reach markets, children reach schools, patients reach hospitals and businesses connect with opportunity. Their enduring significance lies in the lives they improve and the economic activity they unlock.

In education, the administration has invested in classroom rehabilitation, instructional materials, teacher development and institutional reform. The facilitation of the federal takeover of the Institute of Technology and Management, Ugep, now Federal Polytechnic Ugep, represents an important effort to widen access to tertiary and technical education. Investments in school infrastructure, digital administration and teacher development likewise reflect an understanding that the future of Cross River depends substantially on the quality of education available to its children. A state’s greatest resource is ultimately the knowledge, creativity and capacity of its people. This explains why in his graciousness, he has reactivated the bursary scheme to cushion the pangs of tuition and other ancillary obligations on parent.

Healthcare has also received substantial attention. The governor has been intentional about expansion and rehabilitation of health facilities, recruitment of health professionals, establishment of a fistula treatment facility, installation of medical oxygen plants and deployment of technology-assisted medicine delivery. His Health Palliative Programme is intended to improve access to essential services for vulnerable groups, including pregnant women, children and senior citizens.

These interventions matter because healthcare is not an abstract budgetary category; it is the difference between anxiety and reassurance for families confronting illness, and between preventable suffering and the possibility of recovery.

Tourism, one of Cross River’s most distinctive economic assets, has likewise been repositioned as a central pillar of the state’s renewal. Building on the state’s natural attractions, cultural heritage and established tourism infrastructure, Governor Otu’s administration has sought to restore confidence in the sector, improve the visitor experience and reconnect tourism with enterprise, hospitality and employment. The reclaiming of Tinapa from the Asset Management Company of Nigeria (AMCON) is especially significant. Beyond recovering a major state asset, the move reflects a broader determination to return strategic properties to productive use, revive their commercial potential and ensure that Cross River’s investments serve the people for whom they were created.

Equally significant is the governor’s emphasis on ICT, entrepreneurship and human-capital development. Digital systems for public administration and revenue management, alongside vocational training, business support and youth empowerment programmes, seek to equip citizens for a changing economy. The task ahead is to ensure that these initiatives translate into measurable improvements in employability, productivity, household incomes and the capacity of young people to build independent futures.

Governor Otu’s people-centred outlook has also been reflected in his attention to workers, pensioners and other citizens whose welfare depends directly on the state’s financial commitments. The payment of gratuity has offered relief to beneficiaries who waited for their entitlements, while the further promise to pay another tranche before December signals an effort to sustain the process of clearing inherited obligations. Such payments are more than accounting entries; they restore dignity, ease household pressures and reaffirm the principle that years of public service should be honoured with fairness and responsibility.

Yet birthdays offer something beyond the accounting of achievements: an opportunity to acknowledge the human journey behind public responsibility. From the legislative chambers of Abuja to the Government House in Calabar, Otu has travelled a road marked by ambition, experience and the continuing challenge of translating promises into progress. His 67th birthday is therefore both a celebration of the man and a reminder of the trust invested in his office.

To Cross Riverians, the enduring significance of the Sweet Prince is being demonstrated by the extent to which compassion has been translated into policy, policy translated into performance, and performance becoming a better quality of life for the greatest number.

As you mark yet another milestone, Your Excellency. May the years ahead bring renewed wisdom, strength and an ever-deepening commitment to the service of Cross River State.

* Obogo is Special Adviser on Media and Publicity and Chief Press Secretary to Governor Bassey Otu

World.title: Oyedele: World Markets Have Written Off Opposition, Eyeing Tinubu’s 2nd Term
World.content:
•Rules out return to fuel subsidy, warns of risks to naira

•CBN seeks Chinese capital, deeper financial ties to boost investment in Nigeria

• World Bank report: ADC asks Tinubu to explain ‘missing’ $12.4bn

Nume Ekeghe in Bangkok, Thailand and Chuks Okocha in Abuja

The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, has said financial markets and the international community have largely written off Nigeria’s opposition political parties as unserious, with investors already pricing in the prospects of President Bola Tinubu securing a second term and expecting continuity in his economic reforms.

This is just as the Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), Olayemi Cardoso, also said policy consistency and transparency were essential to sustaining investor confidence, as improvements in economic and foreign exchange stability created better conditions for long-term investment.

Meanwhile, the African Democratic Congress (ADC) has called on President Tinubu to explain the $12.4 billion gap, an equivalent of about N16.5 trillion, in Nigeria’s external accounts identified in the World Bank’s October 2026 Nigeria Development Update.

Oyedele and Cardoso spoke at the closing press briefing of the IMF/World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok, Thailand, where the CBN governor said policy consistency would be critical to attracting long-term capital, sustaining economic stability and accelerating growth.

On his part, Oyedele argued that investors’ expectations of continuity under Tinubu had influenced their assessment of Nigeria’s economic outlook, including their response to opposition proposals to restore fuel subsidies.

“In all the meetings I have had, I came to a conclusion that the markets, including the domestic market, which you can read from the capital market, and the international market, have largely written off the opposition in Nigeria as being unserious. That is why they have not priced in the proposed return of subsidy,” he said.

He added that any indication that the president intended to restore the subsidy would immediately be reflected in market prices.

“So, maybe the international and domestic markets are aware about who is sincere about Nigeria and what direction they should travel,” he said.

“As I said, the markets and the international community have been pricing in the prospect of a second term for the President, and they expect continuity in the reforms.”

The minister’s comments followed repeated questions from investors about whether the government would sustain its policies as Nigeria approaches another election cycle.

He said concerns about possible policy reversals had featured prominently in his engagements with investors in Thailand and during two visits to London, particularly over whether electoral pressures could force the administration to abandon its reform agenda.

“Throughout the meetings we have had this week, as well as those I attended before now, including two visits to London to meet investors, one question has repeatedly come up: Are you going to reverse your reforms? Are you under pressure because of elections?” he said.

According to Oyedele, the government remained committed to the reforms, which he described as necessary to restore macroeconomic stability and lay the foundation for sustainable growth.

He said the next phase of the economic programme would focus on translating the gains in stability into stronger investment, lower financing costs, job creation and improved economic opportunities for Nigerians.

Oyedele said private investment had increased twentyfold since the reforms began, rising from about $300 million in 2023 to $6 billion in 2026.

He also highlighted improvements in Nigeria’s external position, saying net reserves had risen from barely $3 billion to more than $45 billion, representing a fifteen-fold increase.

Oyedele ruled out a return to fuel subsidies and multiple exchange rates, warning that reversing the reforms could undermine investor confidence, trigger capital flight and put renewed pressure on the naira.

“Let me be clear: there will be no return to fuel subsidies or multiple exchange rates,” he said.

“If, for any reason, Mr President were to say today that we were considering bringing back fuel subsidies, what happened in Indonesia would be child’s play in comparison,” he said.

“At the end of the day, capital would leave because investors understand what such a decision means.”

He argued that capital flight could intensify pressure on the foreign exchange market and weaken the naira, with the consequences ultimately borne by ordinary Nigerians.

“When capital leaves, the foreign-exchange market will come under pressure, and the naira will crash. The exchange rate could move to N3,000, N3,500 or N4,000 to the dollar,” he said.

Oyedele said such a development would worsen the economic pressures facing households.

The minister also defended the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited’s recent temporary reduction in petrol retail margins, insisting that it was a commercial decision rather than a subsidy financed with public funds.

“The recent temporary reduction in the retail margin on fuel was a time-bound commercial decision by the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited to reduce margins and support Nigerians,” he said.

“It is not a subsidy paid for with public funds.”

He explained that a company’s decision to reduce its profit margin to lower prices should not automatically be classified as a subsidy.

“If you offer a discount by reducing that profit margin, how does that become a subsidy?” he asked.

Cardoso: Policy Consistency, Transparency Critical to Investor Confidence

Meanwhile, Cardoso has stressed that policy consistency and transparency were essential to sustaining investor confidence, as improvements in economic and foreign exchange stability created better conditions for long-term investment.

Cardoso said Nigeria was seeking to deepen financial cooperation with China to attract more Asian investment into its markets and improve cross-border payments, settlement arrangements and trade finance.

He disclosed that discussions with the Governor of the People’s Bank of China, Pan Gongsheng, had focused on practical ways to strengthen cooperation among financial institutions in both countries.

Cardoso said China’s developed payments infrastructure offered lessons for Nigeria, while stronger financial links could facilitate trade and investment between the two economies.

He said the discussions would be followed by technical engagements during his forthcoming visit to Beijing, where officials would examine specific areas of cooperation and identify initiatives capable of delivering practical results.

The CBN governor said Nigeria was particularly interested in attracting Chinese capital into its financial markets, noting that investment in Nigerian financial instruments had remained limited despite the substantial liquidity available in China.

“Finally, bear in mind that, despite the considerable liquidity available in China, there has not been much investment in Nigerian financial instruments over time,” he said.

“This could be an opportunity to change that trajectory and generate greater interest from Asian markets in Nigerian instruments and African instruments generally.”

Cardoso said the initiative formed part of a broader effort to strengthen Nigeria’s financial relationships with Asian economies and expand the pool of capital available to domestic markets.

World Bank Report: ADC Asks Tinubu-led Govt to Explain ‘Missing’ $12.4bn

Meanwhile, the ADC has called on President Tinubu to explain the $12.4 billion gap, equivalent to about N16.5 trillion, in Nigeria’s external accounts identified in the World Bank’s October 2026 Nigeria Development Update.

In a statement issued yesterday by its National Publicity Secretary, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, the party said Tinubu owed Nigerians a clear account of the discrepancy, especially as families struggling with the cost-of-living crisis were forced to account for every naira.

Citing the report, the ADC said Nigeria recorded a $12 billion current-account surplus and $6.2 billion in net financial inflows in the first half of 2026.

The party said these inflows should have strengthened the country’s reserves, but the report instead identified a $12.4 billion gap.

Abdullahi said the World Bank attributed the gap, in part, to oil export earnings that were not repatriated. He added that the report noted that the repatriation of export proceeds remained limited, partly because Nigerian oil had been pledged against several long-term loans.

“The scale is staggering,” the ADC said.

“This unexplained gap is larger than the entire current-account surplus for the same period. It is about 5.6 times the $2.2 billion Nigeria attracted in foreign direct investment. In naira terms, it is almost a quarter of the N68.32 trillion 2026 federal budget.

“This cannot be dismissed as a minor accounting discrepancy. President Tinubu welcomed this report. He cannot celebrate one part of the report and stay silent on a gap bigger than the surplus that he and his government are celebrating.

“Due to President Tinubu’s failed policies, families across Nigeria are forced to skip meals and account for every naira just to survive. Meanwhile, money that could have eased their hardship is currently unaccounted for. Tinubu owes Nigerians an explanation.

“Sacrifice cannot be compulsory for everyday citizens while accountability remains optional for the government that is in charge of our collective resources.”

The ADC called on the federal government to publish a full public reconciliation of the $12.4 billion gap and disclose all oil-backed loans and pledged crude commitments.

It also demanded updated net reserve figures and clear evidence that higher revenues were improving essential services such as health, education and power.

“President Tinubu must open the books. Nigerians have sacrificed enough. We deserve answers,” the party said.

World.title: North Will Give Tinubu Over 70% of Votes in 2027, Says Yilwatda
World.content:
•Shettima: Region will re-elect president

•Makinde will defeat Tinubu in his 12 battleground states, others, says campaign council

Deji Elumoye, Chuks Okocha and Adedayo Akinwale in Abuja

The National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Professor Nentawe Yilwatda, has predicted that the North will give President Bola Tinubu more than 70 per cent of its votes in the 2027 presidential election.

Vice President Kashim Shettima has also said the North will re-elect Tinubu, stressing that the region had spoken with a resounding voice and unmistakable conviction for Tinubu’s re-election.

But the Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation (MDPCO) declared that its presidential candidate on the platform of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Governor Seyi Makinde of Oyo State, will defeat Tinubu in the 12 battleground states identified by the president, as well as in other states across the federation.

Speaking yesterday in Abuja when Shettima unveiled the Arewa for Asiwaju Campaign Head Office and formally inaugurated the campaign structure of the northern think tank, Yilwatda urged people in the North to support Tinubu’s re-election bid, citing infrastructure projects, appointments and other initiatives of the President’s administration.

The APC chairman listed road projects across northern states, the Ajaokuta-Kaduna-Kano gas pipeline, irrigation dams, railway projects, healthcare initiatives and the Nigerian Education Loan Fund among the interventions he said should encourage the North to support Tinubu for a second term.

“I can’t mention all of them, but President Bola Tinubu has done wonderfully. He has covered all the geopolitical zones in the North in terms of road projects,” he added.

He moved a motion for the northern region to support the re-election of the Tinubu/Shettima ticket, outlining reasons why the region should mobilize massively for the president.

He noted that the region’s strong backing stems from the Vice President’s inclusive leadership and progressive mindset over the past three years.

Shettima: Region Will Re-elect President in 2027

Also speaking, Shettima declared that the North will re-elect Tinubu, adding however, that the growing northern support for president’s re-election was not a blank check.

According to him, Tinubu’s administration will earn it through facts, radical transparency and measurable results.

He maintained that expanding loyalty in the region would demand greater accountability and an honest dialogue with citizens about ongoing reforms undertaken by the administration.

Shettima said the North had spoken with a resounding voice and unmistakable conviction in its support for the President.

According to him, renewed political confidence should never be taken for granted, adding that the government and its supporters must continue to engage Nigerians with facts and show how the ongoing reforms are improving security, livelihoods, and economic opportunity.

“By now, I believe the North has spoken. We have spoken with a resounding voice and unmistakable conviction. From Adamawa to Zamfara, from Borno to Niger, we have spoken. Such confidence places an obligation upon us that no officeholder should ever underestimate,” he stated.

The Vice President noted that President Tinubu’s bid for a renewed mandate must rest on the administration’s record and a clear account of how another term would advance Nigerians’ interests.

He restated that the North had nothing to fear in President Tinubu’s second term as Nigeria’s leader.

Shettima acknowledged that Nigerians had endured difficult economic adjustments, warning campaigners against dismissing genuine concerns or relying on political slogans to defend government policies.

“Our citizens have endured difficult adjustments. We cannot pretend otherwise. What we owe them is an honest account of the decisions taken, the gains achieved and the difficulties that persist. We lose our hearing when applause becomes our only source of information,” he added.

The Vice President said the concerns of traders facing higher costs, graduates searching for work and families struggling with daily expenses must remain central to government decision-making.

“A failed policy enters somebody’s home as a missed meal, an unpaid school fee or an opportunity lost,” he said.

He also defended criticism as essential to democratic governance, saying the administration must remain open to useful ideas irrespective of political affiliation, ethnicity, religion or region.

“There is no democracy without critics. Progress demands that our assumptions endure the examination of those who disagree with us,” Shettima said.

The Vice President said the administration’s priorities remain security, economic opportunity, poverty reduction, education and stronger public institutions.

“The farmer should be able to cultivate in safety. A child’s education should prepare that child for a productive life. Public institutions should give citizens confidence that effort can yield opportunity,” he said.

Earlier, Deputy Senate President Barau Jibrin said the inauguration of the A4A structure for the 2027 presidential elections came at a time when the region needed a strong, trusted platform to mobilise support for Tinubu.

Similarly, Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Senator George Akume, said history was beckoning the North to act with wisdom and evidence, not sentiment, in its decision to support the Tinubu administration in the 2027 elections.

On his part, Kano State Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf, speaking on behalf of all the governors of the North, said the northern region’s support for the President in the forthcoming elections would be based on its conviction to uphold fairness, equity, unity and the progress of the country.

In his welcome address, the Director General of A4A and former Jigawa State governor, Abubakar Mohammed Badaru, said the group’s emergence was not accidental, but born of the conviction that President Tinubu and his deputy have performed well and deserve re-election.

Makinde Will Defeat Tinubu in His 12 Battleground States, Others, Says Campaign Council

Meanwhile, the Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation (MDPCO) has declared that its presidential candidate on the platform of the APM, Governor Makinde will defeat Tinubu in the 12 battleground states identified by the president, as well as in other states across the federation.

Makinde also declared that Nigeria’s biggest problem is grinding poverty, not religion, urging Christians to stop shunning politics and take an active role in transforming the country.

The MDPCO, in a statement by its Director of Strategic Communications, Hon. Richard Nnanna Ihediwa, asserted that Makinde would decisively defeat Tinubu and his APC Presidential Campaign Council in Rivers State and the FCT, insisting that no amount of political manoeuvring, intimidation or abuse of incumbency by the President’s henchmen can reverse the growing tide of opposition to his re-election.

The organisation said the arrogance and political overreach of Tinubu’s inner circle had deepened public resentment and further weakened his electoral prospects.

It added that President Tinubu’s decision to personally visit and campaign in only 12 states — Oyo, Kaduna, Rivers, Plateau, Borno, Enugu, Bauchi, Sokoto, Delta, Kano, Adamawa and Lagos — further confirmed his apprehension over the mileage and foothold already achieved by Makinde with his RESET NIGERIA Agenda message in the aforementioned and other states of the federation.

“Mr President should know that his visit to these states, if he eventually does, will not in any way change the direction or the determination of the people to vote him out, given his unpardonable failures in office which have brought unprecedented hardship across the country,” the organisation said.

“President Tinubu has no meaningful achievement he can boast of in these and other states of the federation where Nigerians now refer to his government as ‘T-Pain’ following the suffering they have been subjected to by the policies of the Tinubu administration in the last three and a half years.”

The MDPCO challenged President Tinubu not to have a change of mind but to visit the states to face the people.

“We challenge President Tinubu to travel around the country by road and witness the decrepit state of federal highways, the squalor in which Nigerians live and the level of infrastructural decay across the country, while his government squanders trillions of Naira on white elephant projects and wasteful programmes.

“If President Tinubu believes he is popular as he claims, he should not stop at the rally ground or at the airport when he gets to any of the states. He should go beyond waving to a gathering of APC rented crowd and be bold enough to directly engage the people in the communities and towns to seek their votes, as the APM candidate, Makinde, has been doing since he started his campaign,” it said.

“Nigerians are gravitating towards the core campaign pillars and proposals in Makinde’s RESET NIGERIA Agenda, which include the establishment of an all-inclusive, four-year transitional government of national unity with four priority pillars of education, economy, security and socio-political policies.

“Unlike President Tinubu’s visionless, thoughtless and rudderless rule characterised by crass arbitrariness, Makinde’s RESET NIGERIA Agenda offers data-driven strategies that revolve around tackling poverty through massive production; a security plan that prioritises intelligence gathering, social reorientation and decisive kinetic and non-kinetic actions; an education plan that focuses on expanding access to quality functional education; and institutional reform that emphasises inclusive governance and sincere public leadership.”

The campaign urged Tinubu “not to waste the nation’s resources on his ‘Nebuchadnezzar’ Campaign Council of failed politicians who, like the president himself, cannot attract votes from Nigerians.”

In another development, Makinde has declared that Nigeria’s biggest problem was grinding poverty, not religion, urging Christians to stop shunning politics and take an active role in transforming the country.

He said Christians could not afford to stand aloof from politics because it was dirty or because they should not serve under leaders who did not share their faith, stressing that national transformation required their active participation.

Makinde spoke yesterday in Abuja after receiving a Christian Icon Award at the Christian Association of Nigeria’s (CAN) 50th anniversary celebration.

The governor said Christians should draw lessons from biblical figures who accepted difficult assignments in pursuit of a greater purpose.

Makinde cited David, who, despite having been anointed king, served in the palace of Saul, from whom God had departed.

World.title: Tinubu Mourns as Journalist, Ex-Nigerian Ambassador, Dele Cole, Dies in London at 86
World.content:
Deji Elumoye in Abuja



President Bola Tinubu last night expressed profound sadness at the news of the passing of a distinguished diplomat, journalist, politician, historian and elder statesman, Ambassador Patrick Dele Cole, who died in London at 86.

Cole’s death was confirmed yesterday by a family source, who disclosed that the former Nigerian ambassador died earlier in the morning following weeks of deteriorating health.



The source revealed that Cole had recently been discharged from the Intensive Care Unit (ICU), but his health had continued to decline.

“He left ICU a few days ago. He had been doing poorly in recent weeks leading to this end,” the family source said.

Born on August 4, 1940, Cole turned 86 in August, barely two months before his death.

He was widely known for his contributions to Nigeria’s diplomatic service, journalism, and historical scholarship, having held several prominent positions throughout his career.



Before entering diplomatic service, Cole established himself in Nigeria’s media industry, serving on the editorial board of The Guardian newspaper and subsequently as Managing Director of Daily Times, one of the country’s most influential newspapers.

He later represented Nigeria as Ambassador to Argentina and Brazil, extending his public service career into international diplomacy.

He served as Special Adviser on International Relations under President Obasanjo from 1999 to 2007. He was also appointed Nigeria’s ambassador to Brazil and Argentina.



He also ventured into politics and was associated with the Social Democratic Party (SDP) in the 1990s.

Beyond his diplomatic assignments, Cole was recognised for his involvement in national discourse, particularly on governance, politics, and Nigeria’s historical development.



His career spanned journalism, public administration, and diplomacy, placing him among a generation of Nigerian public figures who contributed to the country’s political and institutional development.

In a statement he personally signed, President Tinubu said Ambassador Cole devoted his life to national service, bringing distinction to his work in diplomacy, journalism and politics.



Tinubu noted that Cole’s career reflected the enduring value of dialogue, tact, mutual respect and the pursuit of shared interests in advancing national development and international cooperation.

“His contributions to Nigeria’s media landscape were particularly notable. As Managing Director of the Daily Times, he upheld the vital role of the press in holding public officials accountable, speaking truth to power, and strengthening democratic governance. His legacy in journalism and public life remains an enduring part of our national story,” Tinubu explained.



The president added that at 86, the deceased witnessed defining moments in Nigeria’s history and contributed to the nation’s development through his work in the media, diplomacy and public service.



According to Tinubu, his life stood as a testament to the value of experience, principled engagement and commitment to the public good.

“As we mourn his passing, I extend my heartfelt condolences to his family, friends, professional associates and all whose lives he touched. I pray that memories of his remarkable life will bring them comfort and strength at this difficult time. May Almighty God grant Ambassador Cole eternal rest and give his family and all who mourn him the fortitude to bear this profound loss,” the statement added.

World.title: Over 40 Companies Raise N2.45 Trillion from Stock Market in Nine Months
World.content:
Kayode Tokede

Over 40 companies raised N2.45 trillion from the Nigerian capital market between January and September 2026, as businesses positioned themselves for growth amid persistent economic pressures, according to data on corporate listings on the Nigerian Exchange Limited (NGX).



The capital-raising surge underscores the NGX’s growing importance as a source of long-term financing for businesses seeking alternatives to expensive bank loans.

Data on corporate listings on the NGX show total corporate capital raising hit about N2.45 trillion in nine months of 2026, covering public offers, private placements and supplementary listings.



The surge came as the Nigerian Exchange Limited All-Share Index gained 61.43 per cent year-to-date (YtD) as of September 2026 to 251,211.67 basis points, making Nigeria one of Africa’s best-performing exchanges.

Among the over 40 companies are: Dangote Sugar Refinery, which raised N485.88 billion through a rights issue; Abbey Bank raised N64.547 billion; Guinea Insurance listed 12.673 billion new shares; Regency Alliance Insurance raised N6.051 billion; Sunu Assurance raised N9.339 billion; Sovereign Trust Insurance raised N5.022 billion; Neimeth International Pharmaceuticals raised N2.442 billion; Critical Minerals Financing Corporation raised N1.807 billion and Eunisell Interlinked raised N200 million, among others.



Of the corporate listings, Fidelity Bank Plc, United Bank for Africa Plc (UBA), FCMB Group Plc, First HoldCo Plc, Access Holdings Plc, Sterling Financial Holdings Company Plc and Guaranty Trust Holding Company Plc led the listed firms, with listings of N883.8 billion in the period under review.



The N883.8 billion listing on the NGX by these four financial institutions came against the backdrop of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) policy mandating that firms raise fresh equity to meet paid-up capital thresholds.

As GTCO listed N10 billion after a successful private placement of 125,000,000 ordinary shares of 50 kobo each at N80.00 per share, NGX admitted UBA’s and First Holdco’s N157.8 billion and N128.7 billion rights issue and private placement in early January 2026, respectively. Access Holdings, N21.4 billion; FCMB Group, N231.83 billion; Sterling Financial Holding Company, N106.978 billion; and Fidelity Bank, N227.05 billion, were new listings on NGX.



The Managing Director of Globalview Capital Limited, Mr. Aruna Kebira, said the recent surge reflected rising investor confidence in the Nigerian Exchange, not apathy, and that confidence is key to capacity building.

Speaking on market participation, Kebira said innovations, improved transparency and the T+1 settlement cycle, where investors get proceeds a day after selling, have deepened retail participation and awareness.

Kebira cited the Dangote Refinery offer, where platforms like OPay and banks actively mobilised investors, as a driver of serious market awareness.



He said the market had evolved significantly since 2011 and was aligning with global standards, moving away from the speculative ‘kalokalo’ approach seen in 2004.

On funding options, Kebira said equity remained the cheapest way to run and expand a manufacturing organisation, as interest on bank loans must be paid regardless of profitability, while equity allowed profits to be ploughed back into the company to do more for shareholders.



He added that the funds had a multiplier effect on capacity expansion, technology adoption and job creation.

He said boards would be under pressure to deliver value, increase production, pay good dividends and put square pegs in square holes because reputation was at stake, adding that the recapitalisation in insurance was necessary to restore the ability to pay claims and rebuild public confidence in the sector.



On his part, the National Chairman of New Dimension Shareholders Association, Mr. Patrick Ajudua, however, stated that fresh capital raising did not automatically translate to higher dividends or immediate job creation.

“You need to know that investment has a risk element. Not all companies that raise fresh capital deliver better dividends,” Ajudua said.

He noted that, in fairness, many companies had delivered dividends, particularly since this administration came to power, which stabilised the economy, especially the foreign exchange market.

World.title: Kwara APC: Ex-VC Leads High-profile Group to Resolve Disputes, Reconcile Aggrieved Members
World.content:
Elder statesman and former Vice-Chancellor of the University of Ilorin, Prof. Oba AbdulRaheem, is leading a group of prominent Kwara indigenes to reconcile aggrieved members of the All Progressives Congress (APC) and mobilise support for the party ahead of the 2027 general election.

The group, which held its inaugural meeting at Abdulraheem’s Ilorin residence on September 17, said it is committed to resolving all disagreements that trailed the outcome of the APC’s primaries.

Abdulraheem, also a former Chairman of the Federal Character Commission (FCC), chairs the group, the Kwara APC Peace Committee.

Apart from Abdulraheem, eminent indigenes of Kwara in the group include Dr. Johnson Adewumi, a foremost educationist/ entrepreneur and founder of the Thomas Adewumi University, Oko; former Minister and former Speaker, Kwara State House of Assembly, Hon. Issa Bio Ibrahim; and former Secretary to Kwara State Government and former Member, Federal House of Representatives, Hon. AbdulGaniyu Cook Olododo.

Other members include Oloriewe Raheem Adedoyin, a veteran journalist and member representing Africa in the Executive Board of the International Press Institute; elder statesman and former Speaker, Kwara State House of Assembly, Hon. Benjamin Ezekiel Issa; elder statesman and Member of Tinubu Shettina PCC, Pastor John Dara; and former Commissioner, Federal Character Commission, Hon. James Jiya Kolo.

According to the statement, the committee intends to serve as a voice of conscience among APC leaders by addressing internal grievances and promoting the achievements of the administrations of President Bola Tinubu and Kwara State Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq.

It said the group had reached out to some aggrieved political leaders and influential stakeholders to encourage reconciliation and forge a common front ahead of the elections.

The committee is also canvassing support for the APC’s governorship candidate, Hon. Yakubu Danladi, and other party candidates in the state.

The statement said the initiative aimed to secure the backing of party stakeholders for the candidates and strengthen cohesion within the APC ahead of the general election.

World.title: Police arrest suspects after comedian murdered
World.content:
Limpopo police launched a successful manhunt following the murder of popular comedian and content creator Khadziyane Ndivhuwo. Image: Instagram
