Limpopo police launched a successful manhunt following the murder of popular comedian and content creator Khadziyane Ndivhuwo, known as Skeem Mafenya, in the Malamulele area.

The 20-year-old was found with multiple stab wounds to his upper body at Madonsi Boltman B in the Vhembe District in the early hours of Saturday.

Police said they received a report about a person lying motionless inside a yard. When officers arrived, they found Ndivhuwo lying on the ground.



Emergency Medical Services personnel were summoned to the scene but declared him dead.

What happened?

According to information provided by police, the incident occurred at approximately 03:35 on Saturday.

It is alleged that a community member heard a knock at their door. When they looked through a window, they noticed Ndivhuwo bleeding profusely.

Emergency services were called, but he could not be saved.

Ndivhuwo resided in Malamulele B2 Extension and was known locally for his comedy and online content.

Three suspects have been arrested in connection with the stabbing. Police say the suspects include a teenager, aged 17.



Police spokesperson Brigadier Hlulani Mashaba says the suspects are expected to appear in court soon.

“The suspects were arrested just hours later in an intelligence-driven operation. We welcome this arrest and we’re going to monitor the case closely to ensure that the suspects are held criminally liable. The suspects are expected to appear before the Malamulele Magistrate’s Court soon, facing a charge of murder,” explained Mashaba.

Police appeal for information

Limpopo police have urged anyone with information that could assist the investigation to come forward.

The investigating officer, Lieutenant Colonel Fhumulani Ragimana, can be contacted on 082 729 0229.

Police have not disclosed whether the victim knew his attackers or what may have led to the killing.

World.title: Plea not to share graphic CCTV footage of fatal Boxer shooting
World.content:
Employment and Labour Minister Nomakhosazana Meth has urged the public not to circulate graphic CCTV footage of the fatal shooting of three female managers at a Boxer Superstore in KwaZulu-Natal. Image: Boxer website

Employment and Labour Minister Nomakhosazana Meth has urged the public not to circulate graphic CCTV footage of the fatal shooting of three female managers at a Boxer Superstore in Eshowe, KwaZulu-Natal.

Meth condemned the shooting, which reportedly occurred following an internal disciplinary process at the store.

In a statement issued, the Minister appealed to members of the public to respect the privacy of the victims’ families and colleagues by refraining from sharing distressing images and videos of the incident.

The Department of Employment and Labour extended its condolences to the families and loved ones of the three women, as well as their colleagues.

Meth also called on law enforcement authorities to ensure that justice is served.

Call for safer workplaces

The minister said the tragedy highlighted the importance of ensuring that all employees can carry out their duties without fearing for their lives or personal safety.

The shooting at the Boxer Superstore occurred mere days after World Mental Health Day, observed on 10 October, prompting renewed calls for stronger workplace support and open communication.

Meth encouraged employers, employees and labour representatives to engage in open dialogue to address workplace challenges and prevent conflict from escalating.

She also emphasised the importance of strengthening Employee Wellness Programmes and ensuring workers have access to appropriate mental health support.

The department said workplaces should prioritise the safety and well-being of employees, while fostering environments where concerns can be raised and addressed constructively.

World.title: Here’s when Kaizer Chiefs will play CAF Confederation Cup second leg tie
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs will have to overturn a first-leg deficit after losing to Zambia’s Red Arrows in the second preliminary round of the CAF Confederation Cup. Image: Kaizer Chiefs website

Kaizer Chiefs will have to overturn a first-leg deficit after suffering a 1-0 defeat to Zambia’s Red Arrows in the second preliminary round of the CAF Confederation Cup.

Amakhosi went down at the Levy Mwanawasa Stadium in Ndola, where a late goal from Red Arrows captain Alassane Diarra gave the hosts the advantage heading into the decisive second leg.

The match was played in scorching conditions, with Kaizer Chiefs unable to find an equaliser after Diarra struck in the 77th minute.



The result leaves the Soweto giants needing a response on home soil if they are to keep their hopes of reaching the Confederation Cup group stage alive.

Diarra delivers late blow

With the tie finely balanced for much of the encounter, Diarra’s late intervention proved decisive for the Zambian side.

His 77th-minute goal gave Red Arrows a narrow lead to take into the return fixture, putting pressure on the Glamour Boys to deliver in front of their home supporters.

Kaizer Chiefs face decisive Durban showdown

The two teams will meet again on Friday, 23 October when Kaizer Chiefs host Red Arrows at Moses Mabhida Stadium in Durban.

Kick-off is scheduled for 18:00.

With a place in the CAF Confederation Cup group stage at stake, Kaizer Chiefs will need to overturn the deficit in the return fixture.



The home advantage could prove important for Amakhosi, but Red Arrows will arrive knowing that even a draw would be enough to secure their progression if the aggregate score remains in their favour.

For Kaizer Chiefs, the task is clear: respond in Durban and keep their continental campaign alive.

Will Kaizer Chiefs get the job done in the second leg in Durban?

World.title: Gayton McKenzie washes his hands with VAR – and the DA isn’t happy
World.content:
Sports Minister Gayton McKenzie is facing renewed criticism over delays in introducing Video Assistant Referee (VAR) technology to South African football, with the Democratic Alliance (DA) accusing him of failing to take responsibility for the project.

In a statement, DA spokesperson on Sport, Arts and Culture Leah Potgieter MP said McKenzie had failed to account for the delays and accused him of abandoning a promise to bring VAR to local football.

The criticism follows a media briefing where McKenzie reportedly said: “There are no more questions you can ask me about VAR.”



According to Potgieter, the minister’s remarks effectively leave the project almost entirely in the hands of the South African Football Association (SAFA).

R20 million at the centre of VAR controversy

The DA has raised concerns about the reported R20 million allocated to the project, claiming the money remains with SAFA while progress on implementing VAR has been limited.

Potgieter argued that Gayton McKenzie cannot distance himself from the project because a commitment was made and public funds were allocated.

“Unfortunately for Minister McKenzie, he can’t wash his hands of it. A commitment was made, and public money was allocated,” she said.

The party also criticised what it described as a lack of accountability from the minister, arguing that football supporters and players have been left waiting for a promised improvement to the game.

VAR technology allows match officials to review certain incidents, including goals, penalty decisions, direct red-card incidents and cases of mistaken identity.



Its potential introduction in South Africa has been a significant talking point among football supporters, particularly amid recurring debates over refereeing decisions in domestic competitions.

DA questions McKenzie’s accountability

Potgieter accused Gayton McKenzie of making public commitments without demonstrating sufficient progress towards delivering them.

She said South African football supporters deserved answers about the delays and the future of the project.

The DA’s statement places renewed pressure on both the Department of Sport, Arts and Culture and SAFA to clarify the status of the VAR rollout, how the allocated funds are being used and what remains to be done before the technology can be introduced.

The statement did not provide a revised implementation date.

The outstanding questions include when VAR will become operational in South African football and what accountability measures will apply to the project.

McKenzie’s reported comments and the DA’s criticism have renewed the debate over responsibility for delivering the technology and ensuring that public funds allocated to the initiative translate into tangible progress.

World.title: Kaizer Chiefs coach Fernando Da Cruz needs to be careful about this
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs coach Fernando Da Cruz chats to Inacio Miguel at the Levy Mwanawasa Stadium in Zambia during the CAF Confederation Cup game against Red Arrows. Image: Red Arrows media

With Kaizer Chiefs winless in four games, questions are being raised regarding Frenchman’s tactical approach and how he manages his troops.

Amakhosi have it all to play for in Friday’s second leg at the Moses Mabhida Stadium to qualify for the CAF Confederation Cup last 16 group stages.

And there’s a bit more. The Soweto giants may be unbeaten in the Betway Premiership, but three wins and five draws have piled pressure on Da Cruz.



FERNANDO DA CRUZ’S KAIZER CHIEFS TACTICS UNDER SCRUTINY

Da Cruz has seemingly set strong emphasis on tactical discipline and structure. The approach has restricted the individual quality and flair associated with Amakhosi and South African players.

Organisation takes local football to a different level but local players need room for improvisation to create opportunities and entertainment. Individual expression seems to be holding back Kaizer Chiefs’ attacking players.

The 1-0 defeat to Arrows highlighted some of those concerns. Da Cruz has strongly stuck to three central defenders and two wingbacks that drop into a back five when defending.



There’s a call for the former AS FAR coach to balance his tactical guidelines without limiting his team’s ability to attack. Their are growing concerns about players’ negative body language. At times they look weighed down by tactical responsibilities, and often seem too afraid to make mistakes.

A NEED FOR ADAPTATION

Man-management could prove decisive in determining whether Da Cruz succeeds at Naturena. He needs to understand the players’ strengths and give them enough freedom to make decisions during matches.

The French coach must also adapt to South African football. His experience in French and Moroccan football structures may have influenced his methods, but he needs to find an approach that suits this current environment and culture.



While his limited English is a factor, Da Cruz must remain open to different ways of communicating, motivating his squad and getting his message across. Tactical knowledge alone will not guarantee success if players struggle to understand or execute his ideas.

His recent coaching history is another factor worth considering. Da Cruz had not coached a team since 2023, having subsequently worked as a technical director and later as an instructor within the Moroccan Football Federation. Managing a team during competitive matches presents different challenges.

At Kaizer Chiefs, tactical discipline must deliver results without sacrificing creativity, individual quality and the confidence of the players.

World.title: Employed but struggling: South Africans face cost-of-living squeeze
World.content:
Having a job and earning a regular salary was once seen as a sign of financial stability, but for a growing number of South Africans, a monthly income is no longer enough to cover the rising cost of living. Image: Pickpik

Having a job and earning a regular salary was once seen as a sign of financial stability, but for a growing number of South Africans, a monthly income is no longer enough to cover the rising cost of living.

Despite annual consumer inflation reaching 4.4% in August 2026, essential expenses continue to put pressure on household budgets, leaving some employed consumers increasingly reliant on credit just to get through the month.

RELATED | Discovery reveals higher medical aid rates for 2027: Here’s how much



Rising costs leave households under pressure

Electricity and transport are among the expenses adding to the squeeze on household finances.

Eskom direct customers faced an electricity price increase of 8.76% in April, while municipal electricity customers have been paying 9.01% more since July.

Meanwhile, October’s fuel price increases pushed inland petrol prices above R30 a litre for the first time, adding further pressure to transport budgets.

These increases come on top of household commitments such as rent or home-loan repayments, groceries, school fees, insurance and existing credit repayments.

Even relatively small increases across several essential expenses can leave a household struggling to balance its budget.

The problem is compounded when consumers have little money left over at the end of the month to deal with unexpected costs.



Why more South Africans are turning to credit

As household budgets become increasingly stretched, some consumers are borrowing not to cover emergencies or major purchases, but simply to make it to payday.

The shortage of emergency savings makes the situation worse.

Recent surveys found that only 29% of adults had enough savings to cover three months of expenses.

Without an adequate financial buffer, an unexpected bill or temporary loss of income can force consumers to rely on credit, potentially making an already difficult situation worse.

When debt counselling could help

Debt counselling is a regulated process designed to help over-indebted consumers restructure their repayments into a more manageable arrangement.

The process aims to help consumers repay their debts while allowing for reasonable living expenses and, where applicable, protecting assets.

Payments are generally consolidated into a single monthly amount, which is distributed to creditors through a payment distribution agency.

For households finding that a regular salary no longer covers their essential expenses, the message is clear: financial difficulty does not automatically mean poor money management, and getting help early could prevent the situation from deteriorating further.

Financial reality

René Moonsamy, chairperson of the National Debt Counselling Association (NDCA), says headline inflation figures do not necessarily reflect the financial reality facing households.

“Although inflation seems to be heading in the right direction, it’s important to consider two things,” Moonsamy explains.

“Firstly, a lower headline inflation rate doesn’t mean that prices are coming down, just that they are increasing more slowly, or the costs of some of the goods and services in the inflation basket have decreased.

“Secondly, households must still pay for essentials that are increasing way beyond the average inflation rate, with salaries that have only gone up by 4.1% in the year to May 2026.”

She added that essential expenses are rising faster than the average inflation rate, while salaries have not necessarily kept pace.

World.title: One lucky South African hits R112 million PowerBall jackpot
World.content:
One lucky South African has become R112 million richer after winning the PowerBall jackpot in the Tuesday, 13 October 2026 draw. Image: Sizekhaya

One lucky South African has become R112 million richer after winning the PowerBall jackpot in the Tuesday, 13 October 2026 draw.

The winning ticket was purchased at OK Foods Meyerton, with the player emerging as the sole jackpot winner in PowerBall draw number 1763.

Meyerton is a small industrial and residential town located 18km north of Vereeniging in Gauteng.



Lucky numbers

The five numbers drawn were 3, 15, 24, 30, 31 while the PowerBall bonus ball – which is also required in winning the jackpot – was 7.

The National Lottery operator has congratulated the winner and urged them to come forward to claim the life-changing prize.

“We congratulate our latest PowerBall jackpot winner on this extraordinary win. Winning R112-million is a life-changing moment, and we look forward to welcoming the winner when they come forward to claim their prize,” said Kgothatso “KG” Mashile, Head of Marketing at Sizekhaya Holdings.

Advice for R112 million PowerBall winner

Mashile encouraged the winner to complete their personal details on the back of the physical ticket immediately and keep it in a safe place.

Taking these precautions is an important step in protecting the winning ticket while preparing to claim the jackpot.

Once the winner comes forward, they will have access to free and confidential professional counselling and financial guidance through Sizekhaya Holdings.



The support is intended to help the winner prepare for the significant changes that come with receiving such a large amount of money and make informed decisions about their financial future.

“An extraordinary win like this brings incredible possibilities, but it is important for the winner to approach this new chapter with care and make informed decisions that will help secure their future,” Mashile added.

A life-changing lottery win

The R112 million jackpot represents an extraordinary financial windfall for the unidentified winner.

However, the lottery operator has stressed the importance of approaching the prize responsibly, with professional guidance available to help the winner navigate their new circumstances.

For now, the identity of the Meyerton ticket holder remains unknown as the winner has yet to come forward to claim the prize.

World.title: Updated SASSA grant payment dates for November and December
World.content:
SASSA beneficiaries now confirmed the amended payment dates for the final two months of 2026, giving millions of South Africans the opportunity to plan ahead for the festive season. Image: Facebook @SASSANewsZA

SASSA has confirmed the amended payment dates for the final two months of 2026, giving millions of South Africans the opportunity to plan ahead for the festive season.

The changes were necessary in November as they clashed with the local government elections scheduled for Wednesday, 4 November.

WIN | Test your SASSA knowledge and win R250



In a statement, the agency said the revised schedule follows consultations with various stakeholders to ensure the efficient and secure administration of grant payments, with minimal disruption during the election period.

Approved

National Treasury has approved the revised payment dates, allowing the agency to implement the new schedule.

As always, the South African Social Security Agency (SASSA) pays Older Persons Grants first, followed by Disability Grants and then Children’s Grants.

In terms of the revised arrangements, social grants will now be paid as follows:

Older Persons Grant: Friday, 30 October

Disability Grant: Monday, 2 November



Children’s Grants: Tuesday, 3 November

The final two months of the 2026 payment calendar are now as follows:

Month Older Persons Disability Children’s November Friday, 30 October Monday, 2 November Tuesday, 3 November December Wednesday, 2 December Thursday, 3 December Friday, 4 December

The final major grant payment cycle of the year starts on Wednesday, 2 December, when Older Persons Grant beneficiaries are scheduled to be paid.

Disability Grant beneficiaries will receive their payments on Thursday, 3 December, while Children’s Grants are scheduled for Friday, 4 December.

Why SASSA payments are staggered

SASSA uses a staggered payment system to help manage demand and reduce congestion at payment points.

Beneficiaries should also remember that they do not have to withdraw their money on the day it is paid.

Once the grant has been deposited, the money remains available in the beneficiary’s account.

This means beneficiaries can choose when to access their funds rather than rushing to a payment point on the scheduled payment date.

How much will SASSA beneficiaries receive?

Following the grant increases introduced in April 2026, the main grant amounts are:

Older Persons Grant: R2 400

R2 400 Disability Grant: R2 400

R2 400 Care Dependency Grant: R2 400

R2 400 War Veterans Grant: R2 420

R2 420 Foster Child Grant: R1 290

R1 290 Child Support Grant: R580

The SRD grant remains separate from the permanent social grant payment schedule.

The R370 Social Relief of Distress (SRD) Grant has individual payment dates rather than following the three-day payment cycle.

Beneficiaries receiving the SRD grant should check their personal SASSA status for their specific payment date.

With the final three payment cycles of the year now confirmed, beneficiaries can plan their household budgets around their respective payment dates – particularly with the December festive season approaching.

World.title: TRC Inquiry postpones Zuma testimony pending recovery
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The TRC Cases Inquiry will wait until Jacob Zuma is well enough to testify.

The former president is taking time to rest after a hospital stay for what his party calls fatigue.

Meanwhile, it has said Thabo Mbeki is fully cooperating with the commission.

This is despite his multiple attempts to have Chair Sisi Khampepe removed.

The inquiry is looking into claims of political interference to block prosecutions of apartheid-era crimes.

Inquiry spokesperson, Lionel Adendorf, said Monday will be an important day of testimony.

" Tomorrow is an important day. I need to stress that it is, obviously the president because of the time period where the TRC cases inquiry our terms of reference start. It is important that we had to have the president on the stand. Unfortunately our work has been delayed by the review application to the Johannesburg High Court and then the Constitutional Court.

"But here we are. Finally, we will have former president on the stand and we have his cooperation. There was no subpoena issued. He generously and graciously offered to assist us as well as former president Zuma. Our evidence leaders have been in contact with his lawyers.

"We do have an arrangement to interview him at a time when he is much better and able to travel and take the stand. And we hope that we can agree on that urgently. The agreement between our evidence leaders and the legal representatives for former president Jacob Zuma has agreed that it would be done within our timeframe."

World.title: KuGompo City residents fight back
World.content:
KUGOMPO CITY - KuGompo City residents are taking the fight against cable theft into their own hands.

Resident Chris Botha said Cambridge is frequently plunged into darkness due to the theft of electricity infrastructure.

Cambridge West residents said criminals hide in thick bushes and often use them as hideouts while hacking away at copper wire cables.

One such resident is Anelisa Mbokomba.

"We're experiencing this every week, cable theft every single week, and it goes for the longest periods of two to three days without power.

"We find ourselves having our fridges go bad, unable to do the basic things that we have to do, get our kids ready for school, get ourselves ready for work, just because we have no power," she said.

The Cambridge Sector Four CPF patrols day and night.

They believe communities in the Buffalo City Metro are under siege as cable theft has become out of control.

Cambridge Sector Four's Chris Botha said: "The guys that target the cables or that dig them up, especially, they're not just targeting live cables; they're targeting the backup cables. So not only are your main lines affected, but the backup lines as well, from what we've seen."

The Hawks in the Eastern Cape say that while they acknowledge that cable theft is rife in the Buffalo City Metro, they deny claims made by the residents that law enforcement agencies are losing their fight against the crime.

"I wouldn't say we are not doing enough because we have made a lot of arrests regarding cable theft. Communities are equally responsible for reporting any suspicious activity in their communities. We are trying our best," said Hawks Eastern Cape spokesperson, Ndiphiwe Mhlakuvana.

World.title: Four new Mpox cases confirmed
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The Health Department has confirmed four new Mpox cases.

This has brought the total number of confirmed cases nationwide to 26.

Cases have been reported in Gauteng, the Western Cape, the Eastern Cape, the Free State and KwaZulu-Natal.

Two cases involve foreign nationals, while the rest are linked to local transmission.

Authorities are advising members of the public to seek medical attention if they develop symptoms such as a rash, fever, headache, muscle aches, swollen lymph nodes or fatigue.

Anyone who has been in contact with a confirmed case should monitor themselves for symptoms for 21 days.

World.title: eNCA MarkData Election Survey | Here's what the results mean
World.content:
The DA has opened a wide lead over the ANC in Johannesburg, but not nearly enough to avoid another five years of coalition government in the City of Gold, the eNCA MarkData poll has established.

And in Cape Town, the DA will have to ensure all its supporters cast their votes if its overall majority is to be maintained.

The relevant full results of the poll was announced and analysed in a live broadcast on eNCA this morning. It was conducted between 12 August and 10 September among a scientifically selected representative sample of a thousand registered voters per metro who intend to vote.

The margin of error for Johannesburg is 3,08%, and for Cape Town 3,09%. The modelled turn-out is 48.8%. For more on the methodology used in the poll, please click here.

The poll has found that the DA leads the ANC by 35% to 21,8% in Johannesburg. Other parties polling strongly include the MK Party on 12,5%, the EFF on 11.9% and Action SA on 10,3%, with the Patriotic Alliance much further back on 3,7% as the only other party favoured by more than 1% of respondents.

Helen Zille (DA) is the most popular of the mayoral candidates at 30,6%, followed by Action SA leader and former Johannesburg mayor Herman Mashaba on 23,4%. With the ANC thus far unable to announce a candidate, voters were given several options. Of the ANC hopefuls listed, current mayor Dada Morero came out tops on 15%, far behind Zille and Mashaba.

For the full relevant Johannesburg poll results, please click here.

In Cape Town, the poll measured DA support on 52.6%, followed by the ANC at 23,6%, and the EFF beating the Patriotic Alliance, who will hope to do much better in the Western Cape rural areas, because PA numbers in the City of Cape Town are surprisingly weak.

EFF support in Cape Town is 6,5%, with the PA on 3,9% and the MK Party on 1,5%. No other party polls above 1% in Cape Town.

Current Cape Town mayor Geordin Hill-Lewis (DA) is even more popular than his party, with 55,4% of Capetonians polled wanting to see him back in office. No candidate from another party is close to polling in the double digits.

The eNCA MarkData polls also measured voter preference on hot button local issues like rate increases and gangsterism in Cape Town, and water issues and xenophobia in Johannesburg.

The voter preference regarding the proposed wall along the N2 in Cape Town yielded an astounding result, with 69,6% of respondents in favour of it, and only 19,9% against. Fully 45.3% of respondents blamed the national government for Cape Town gangsterism, with 25,3% blaming the city government and 14,1% the provincial government. More than 10% blames no-one.

For the full relevant Cape Town poll results, click here.

Whereas 60,5% of Cape Town respondents believe their city is well run, the same is true for only 29,2% of Johannesburg respondents. About 36,2% of Cape Town respondents believe the Mother City is poorly run, versus 68,7% of the City of Gold respondents who believe their city to be poorly run.

About 88% of Johannesburgers believe foreigners and xenophobia to be a problem in their city, and roughly two thirds are angry at the current ANC-led coalition government about water provision and infrastructure maintenance.

Polling results for Durban’s eThekwini metro and Pretoria’s Tshwane metro will be announced next week. Last week, the polling results for Ekurhuleni (click here) and Nelson Mandela Bay (click here) were announced.

World.title: 'Over 80 vehicles recovered since April' - BMA
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The BMA's Vehicle Targeting System is already bearing fruit.

It's helped recover 83 vehicles valued at over R46 million rand since its implementation in April.

The system has also flagged thousands of cases involving vehicles with outstanding documentation.

BMA Commissioner Mike Masiapato said the initiative is helping authorities identify stolen vehicles, falsified ownership records and other fraud.

" Just to demonstrate that we are not launching something that is starting today, but we are launching something that is unfolding as we speak. This system has been running since 1 April.

"We say that we have been able to have around 83 vehicles that have recovered up to this point. In the past six months, 83 vehicles has been recovered. And in terms of our mathematics, they are all valued at around R46.6million. Seven of those were stolen vehicles that we had to recover. Eight were ownership records that has been falsified. Eight were cloned vehicles. Twenty-seven stopped on the basis of the false letters or fraudulent letters from the financers that were produced, and 33 financed vehicles were also recovered, settled, and they were returned to the institutions that own them.

"Separately, we can also indicate that around one thousand eight hundred and seventeen vehicles had been stopped because the person driving could not show the written consent of the bank or the financier through which the vehicle is then financed on. And we therefore also put the value of that to around 600 and 36 million."

World.title: Residents must stay in touch after elections
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The Joburg Crisis Alliance saw the build-up to 4 November as an opportune time to host their 10th Summit.

Sithembile Mbete from the Public Affairs Research Institute was one of the panellists at the gathering.

She said residents frustrated with poor service delivery have to keep engaging politicians long after the elections.

" What came out of the conversation today is that we really need to be engaged as residents throughout this period, not just the election, but really watching to see who's going to be on our ward committees and electing those ward committees, paying attention to who becomes the MMCs and holding those people accountable.

"Because those are the people that are responsible for each of the portfolios that are responsible for delivering water, for delivering, you know, for making pick-it-up function, etc. Then really paying attention to the budget processes so that it can be then easier for us to monitor those budgets once that they have been passed.

"And so, the sense that we must feel a sense of ownership of the city the entire time and not only respond to the politicians as they come and seek our votes before elections."

World.title: 84 HR officers linked to Sh6.2 billion payroll fraud sent on forced leave
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Some 84 human resource officers suspected of being involved in the Sh6.2 billion payroll fraud have been sent on forced 30-day leave with immediate effect.

Public Service Cabinet Secretary Geoffrey Ruku, in his order, said the HR officers are drawn from Medical Health, Public Health, Professional Standards, Kenya Police Service and Kenya Prisons Service departments.

The move comes after the Director of Criminal Investigation (DCI) on July 7 handed over a State payroll audit of February 2025, which showed a fraud that might have cost taxpayers Sh6.2 billion.

The Standard had carried an investigative report dubbed 'Prison Heist' that exposed a Sh41 million payroll heist at the State Department for Correctional Services, which falls under the Kenya Prisons Service.

The expose showed how a rogue accountant logged into the system on December 19, 2025, and initiated transfers of allowances for almost 1,000 officers in a single day.

The shocking scheme saw officers across all ranks receive unsolicited payments ranging from Sh30,000 to Sh140,000, with the total irregular payout amounting to Sh41,346,895.

Public Service Cabinet Secretary Geoffrey Ruku, in his order, said the HR officers are drawn from Medical Health, Public Health, Professional Standards, Kenya Police Service and Kenya Prisons Service departments.

The breach was so outrageous that senior officers who head prisons across the country and are either too senior or on the verge of retirement were included in the transfers, raising immediate red flags.

The State Department for Correctional Services oversees 135 penal institutions spread across 8 regions and 47 counties, with a daily average of 61,000 inmates in custody.

The CS, who was accompanied by Principal Secretary for Public Service and Human Development Jane Imbunya, also ordered the relevant PSs and accounting officers to ensure that payroll user rights of the suspected HR officers in the affected Departments are withdrawn with immediate effect.

According to the Ministry, in an effort to establish the modus operandi employed in the suspicious transactions, individuals whose particulars featured in the suspicious transaction data were sampled for interrogation and statement recording.

"The exercise is ongoing at various County Headquarters where the identified officers are deployed. Statements recorded so far indicate that some beneficiaries of the suspicious payments were recruited by their colleagues and, in certain instances, by Human Resource officers," said Ruku.

He added: "The recruited beneficiaries were subsequently used as conduits through whom irregular transactions were processed through the payroll system. It has further emerged from the statements recorded that, after receipt of the resulting payments, the beneficiaries allegedly remitted some of the proceeds to some recipient accounts."

These emerging accounts, the CS pointed to a coordinated arrangement in which beneficiaries were recruited to facilitate the processing and receipt of irregular payroll payments, with a portion of the proceeds subsequently being shared with the persons facilitating the transactions.

The CS said in the meantime, the Ministry, through the State Department of Public Service and Human Resource Development, will deploy Human Resource officers in the affected State Departments to continue administration of the payroll.

He also said there are expected arrests before the end of the 30 days, especially in the Kenya Prison Service.

World.title: Kenya confirms third Ebola case
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kenya has confirmed a third case of Ebola involving a 65-year-old woman who is a close relative of the first two patients.

The Ministry of Health, in a statement, said the woman developed a fever, sore throat and malaise while in quarantine, prompting her isolation and testing.

Her samples tested positive for Ebola at both the National Virology Reference Laboratory and the Kenya Medical Research Institute (KEMRI).

According to the Health Director-General Patrick Amoth, the patient has been transferred to an infectious disease unit, where she is receiving supportive care and being monitored.

“Having been in quarantine, she was diagnosed early and is currently receiving supportive care, improving her chances of recovery while limiting the risk of further spread of the disease,” the statement read.

The second patient, on the other hand, is in stable condition and responding well to supportive care.

The latest case brings the number of confirmed Ebola infections in Kenya to three.

According to the Ministry, of the 130 contacts identified so far, 127 had been traced and placed in quarantine, with efforts ongoing to trace the remaining three.

World.title: Motorists, households face fresh fuel price hikes
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

EPRA attributed the price increases to the escalating conflict in the Middle East. [FIle, Standard]

The Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority (EPRA) has increased fuel prices, raising the cost of super petrol by Sh12.93 per litre, diesel by Sh9.90, and kerosene by Sh28.49.

The new prices, effective from October 15 to November 14, 2026, will see motorists in Nairobi pay up to Sh226.96 per litre for super petrol, Sh227.76 for diesel, and Sh219.85 for kerosene.

EPRA Director-General Edward Mwirigi Kinyua attributed the price increases to the escalating conflict in the Middle East, which has disrupted petroleum supply chains and driven up the cost of importing fuel.

The rise in kerosene prices is likely to hit low-income households that rely on the fuel for cooking and lighting.

Meanwhile, higher diesel prices could raise the cost of transporting goods and operating public service vehicles, potentially driving up fares and commodity prices.

Diesel is a key fuel for the country's freight transport sector and a significant portion of public service vehicle operations, meaning the increase could have a ripple effect across the economy.

The latest review comes after EPRA maintained pump prices during the September 15 to October 14 pricing period, despite a decline in the cost of importing petrol.

World.title: Oburu Oginga to leave hospital soon - ODM
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

ODM SG Catherine Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician.

ODM Secretary General Catherine Omanyo has dismissed social media reports about the health of party leader Oburu Oginga, saying he is recovering well and is expected to be discharged from hospital either today or tomorrow.

Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician, accusing them of exploiting his health condition to attract online attention and increase engagement.

“It's unfortunate what I've been reading on social media. Those people who are seeking to have more likes or viewers, they will be disappointed because he's up, he's well, he's fine. In fact, he's headed home either today or tomorrow,” she said.

Omanyo insisted that the reports had exaggerated his situation, dismissing claims of his death and assuring the public that he was doing well.

She noted that health conditions could fluctuate, saying Oburu's position as ODM party leader had made his well-being a subject of heightened public interest.

“Everybody, everybody, including you and me, our health is not static. You can be under the weather any time. It's just that he's a party leader, and it makes breaking news,” Omanyo said.

She urged social media users to exercise restraint when discussing the health of public figures, warning against spreading unverified reports, particularly claims of death, before confirmation from credible sources.

Her remarks come amid growing speculation on social media about Oburu's health, with some users circulating unverified claims about his condition.

World.title: Kenya declares Ebola a formidable epidemic disease, sets new rules
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale, who declared Ebola caused by the Bundibugyo virus a formidable epidemic disease under the Public Health Act. [File,Standard]

Kenya has declared Ebola virus a formidable epidemic disease, introducing new rules governing screening, isolation, quarantine, contact tracing and the handling of bodies.

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale issued the declaration through a legal notice published in the Kenya Gazette on Monday, October 12, under Section 35 of the Public Health Act.

The declaration follows Kenya’s confirmation of its first imported case of Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease on October 6, after a Kenyan citizen who had been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo travelled through Uganda to Nairobi. The patient died despite receiving supportive treatment.

The case prompted health authorities to trace people who may have come into contact with the patient and strengthen screening at points of entry.

In an update on October 12, the World Health Organization (WHO) said Kenya had listed 127 contacts, with 94 in quarantine, and screened more than 665,000 travellers at points of entry.

WHO also supplied protective equipment and testing materials worth about US$70,000 to support the response.

The government published two legal notices on October 12. Legal Notice No. 203 declares the disease a formidable epidemic, while Legal Notice No. 204 establishes the Public Health (Ebola Disease) Rules, 2026.

The regulations provide for screening at points of entry, medical assessment, isolation, referral, quarantine and monitoring.

They also assign responsibilities to transport operators, health facilities, medical practitioners and laboratories.

Health authorities will conduct investigations and contact tracing, while designated health facilities will manage suspected and confirmed cases. The rules also provide for the inspection and decontamination of premises.

The regulations cover the safe and dignified disposal of bodies, burial procedures, record-keeping, transportation and repatriation. They also address public communication, media houses’ responsibilities in public sensitisation and assistance from enforcement agencies.

The rules provide for offences and penalties, although the Gazette extract does not specify the penalties for individual violations.

What the declaration means

Bundibugyo virus disease is a form of Ebola that spreads through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of an infected person or contaminated materials.

Contact with the body of someone who has died from the disease can also expose people to infection during unsafe burial practices.

Symptoms can include fever, fatigue, muscle pain, headache and sore throat, followed by vomiting and diarrhoea. The incubation period ranges from two to 21 days.

WHO says no approved vaccine or specific treatment currently exists for the Bundibugyo strain, making early detection, isolation, supportive care and contact tracing central to controlling its spread.

The health agency has advised against travel or trade restrictions on Kenya, Uganda and the Democratic Republic of Congo based on the information available.

The new rules establish a legal framework for managing the disease, from identifying suspected infections and monitoring contacts to caring for patients and preventing exposure during burials.

World.title: Ruto wades into growing ODM-UDA conflict
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto marks Mazingira Day by planting trees in Elgon downs, Trans-Nzoia County. [PCS]

President William Ruto delved into the growing tension among Orange Democratic Movement (ODM) and United Democratic Alliance (UDA) contenders in the Coast and asked them to tone it down during his recent tour of the region.

Speaking hours before he wound up his eight-day tour, Ruto appeared to notice the widening cracks and told politicians within the two parties to embrace a ceasefire and unite against the opposition.

The head of state, who is facing a formidable challenge from the united opposition, warned that divisions in the ODM and UDA could weaken their team, whose union gives it a chance to win the 2027 general election.

“ODM and UDA are one team, and you should accommodate each other under a broad-based government. We should not allow divisions in ODM and UDA to undermine our unity of purpose,” he stated.

His statement appeared to be directed at the growing tensions among contenders, particularly in Kwale, Mombasa and Kilifi counties where prominent politicians face challengers within the ODM and UDA political union.

President Ruto’s earlier attempt to zone the region in favour of sitting governors is also blamed for the cracks in the broad-based team at the Coast.

In Mombasa County, UDA secretary general Mr Hassan Omar has already rejected a plan by the so-called broad-based team to support governor Abdulswamd Nassir’s re-election.

Omar, who is also a member of the East African Legislative Assembly (EALA) insisted that he will challenge Mr Nassir.

Already, businessman and EALA member Mr Suleiman Shahbal has quit ODM after he left he could not get the party ticket as the president's allies favour Nassir, a deputy party leader.

Shhabal has since aligned himself to former Laikipia governor Mr Murithi Nderitu’s Kenya Reform Party even as he insisted that he will be on the ballot.

In Mombasa, Mining, Blue Economy and Maritime Affairs Cabinet Secretary Mr Hassan Joho and governor Nassir appeared to be handing over Coast which was the ODM leader late Raila Odinga’s political turf, to President Ruto.

“This region stands with Ruto because he has dignified us with title deeds and many other development projects. We however expect him to support us when we seek the presidential seat in 2032,” Joho said.

Joho’s elder brother Abubakar Joho, who is a prominent businessman, has also joined the campaign for President Ruto.

While touring Kwale, Ruto addressed the growing noise among the main contenders, Governor Fatuma Achani (UDA), Prof Hamadi Boga and Engineer Lung’anzi Chai (ODM) after the broad-based leaders appeared to settle for Ms Achani who has the backing of Sports CS and former Kwale governor Salim Mvurya.

After witnessing the rising political tension, Ruto changed tone and told the three contenders to directly seek support from the voters rather than relying on external political backing.

In a complete change of heart and political tact, Ruto emphasised that the power to choose leaders ultimately belongs to the electorate, who will evaluate candidates based on their track record and development agenda for the region.

“You should all seek votes from the people and not rely on external backing. What I need from all of you is your support,” he stated.

For long, Governor Achani has enjoyed unwavering backing of President Ruto, Mvurya and recently Joho, who had preferred Kwale to be zoned in favour of the governor and UDA.

But Prof Boga, who has been Mr Joho’s ally, described the broad-based government’s zoning arrangement as undemocratic and a coercion to the Kwale electorate who he said should be allowed to choose their leaders without external interference.

Boga has been critical about the attempt to stop some aspirants from contesting seats in the broad-based government, noting that it was possible to zone candidates and difficult to do so for the voters.

In a statement, Boga noted that former Gender CS and Kilifi governor aspirant Ms Aisha Jumwa’s recent departure from UDA to Wiper Patriotic Front (WPF) reflected a growing sense among a segment of coastal leaders that decisions about their political future are increasingly being made elsewhere, then handed down as settled outcomes rather than negotiated realities.

“Zoning at the Coast is a fantasy: You can zone candidates but you cannot zone the voters,” Boga had warned.

“And if UDA and ODM are not paying attention to that signal, they may be underestimating the political consequences of their emerging arrangements at the Coast. “There is a dangerous assumption taking root in the broad-based arrangement: that coastal politics can be settled around a table in Nairobi and then delivered to voters as a finished political package. You take this seat, we take that one, and the voters will follow,” he added.

Boga, who came second in the 2022 governor poll, warned that if the Coast is mishandled, the problem will not necessarily be that voters have suddenly embraced another political formation, but the greater danger is that voters may decide that none of the established arrangements speak for them, creating either a rebellion or apathy.

In Kilifi County, the broad-based team publicly worked with Governor Gideon Mung’aro, forcing Ms Jumwa, his main challenger, to quit the government team in protest.

Kilifi Senate aspirant Mr Stephen Kahocho and Ganze parliamentary aspirant Ms Zawadi Kingi have publicly warned that they might be forced to quit UDA and vie as independent candidates or join other political formations.

This is after it emerged that the broad-based arrangement was behind Mung’aro (ODM), Kilifi senator Stewart Madzayo (ODM) and Ganze MP Kenneth Kazungu Tungule of Pamoja African Alliance (PAA), an affiliate of UDA.

World.title: Even LinkedIn is getting tired of your AI-written posts
World.content:
New York — Bland, AI-generated posts have made LinkedIn the butt of many an internet joke this year. The platform has heard its users’ complaints about lengthy, generic missives never touched by human hands loud and clear.

As AI has made it easier than ever to create huge volumes of content cheaply and easily, that “slop” has flooded the internet. YouTube, Pinterest, Spotify and other platforms have all sought to limit the amount of spammy, AI-generated content their users see.

But LinkedIn has been hit especially hard. Scrolling through the professional networking site earlier this year could mean being bombarded by bullet-pointed lists accented by emojis, references to “B2B sales,” and asks for a follow or comment for more.

A report published in July by Pangram, a research firm that tracks AI content online, found that more than 40 percent of long-form posts on the platform were AI-generated, compared to around 30 percent on X and Medium and a smaller percentage on Reddit and Substack.

So now, LinkedIn is upping its fight against slop.

“I know you think you’re doing the right thing with your perfectly bulleted list and your hook at the top, and you followed all the advice from LinkedIn advisors across the internet,” LinkedIn Editor-in-Chief Dan Roth, who leads the platform’s content strategy, told CNN in an interview. “But what works is being human.”

There is some irony in this, given that LinkedIn is owned by Microsoft. The tech giant has pushed for people to adopt its AI tools for everything from writing to coding, and it is up against steep competition from the likes of OpenAI and Anthropic. LinkedIn previously offered AI tools to edit or rewrite posts, although it recently scaled the offerings back.

But low-quality AI posts are a business problem for LinkedIn. They all start to sound the same, Roth said.

If users see too many generic AI posts, instead of content that really teaches them something or gives them a deeper understanding of a professional connection, LinkedIn risks losing them to other platforms.

Fighting AI slop

In August, LinkedIn rolled out a button letting users flag when a post “seems like AI slop,” which was clicked more than 1 million times within its first two weeks. Now, the company is trying to use its own AI systems to help weed out AI slop on the platform and to remind LinkedIn users how to post like humans.

The company built a team largely made up of former journalists and social media experts who have an eye for recognizing generic, sloppy content. These experts help train LinkedIn’s AI model on what authentic, useful posts look like. If the model flags a post as low-quality, AI-generated content, it’ll be less likely to be distributed beyond that user’s direct connections.

The LinkedIn office on July 26, 2023, in San Francisco, California. Justin Sullivan/Getty Images

Also key to the strategy is a creator management team that acts as “content therapists” for executives, subject matter experts and other LinkedIn users, many of whom have gotten accustomed to the convenience of using AI to write what, on the surface, appear to be polished posts, Roth said.

“A lot of times now today, they’ll run it through Claude or Gemini or wherever, they’ll post it on LinkedIn and it will perform poorly. And then they come to the team and they’re like, ‘Why did this do badly?’” Roth said. “And the best thing you can do is give it back to them and be like, ‘Did you enjoy reading this? Do you see yourself in this?”

Instead, the team encourages users to embrace imperfection in their posts — to make videos by leaning a phone up against a coffee mug, rather than shooting in an expensive studio, or to dash off a post to start a conversation, even if it isn’t a complete thought.

The efforts are showing early signs of success. Improvements to LinkedIn’s detection systems have resulted in a 40 percent decline in views of content classified as AI slop, the platform said last month.

That’s not to say LinkedIn is entirely opposed to AI, Roth said, adding that “not everyone is a born communicator.” But failing to edit or personalize content means it’s less likely to reach a wide audience on the platform.

“We just try to push people to be more human,” he said. “That is what is required to be able to cut through the noise.”

World.title: Zelensky praises ‘real leaders’ in Europe as his relationship with Trump deteriorates
World.content:
Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky praised “real leaders” in Europe at a summit in Belgium on Friday, taking a veiled swipe at US President Donald Trump amid testy relations between Kyiv and Washington.

European leaders are rallying around Zelensky after the White House heaped pressure on Ukraine to halt strikes on Russian oil facilities, even as Russia’s attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure continue unabated.

Ukraine halted strikes on Russian oil refineries for three days after Trump’s surprise announcement on Sunday of an “energy ceasefire” between the two countries, but has since resumed attacks given Russia did not reciprocate.

Trump, who is desperate for soaring global diesel prices to ease ahead of next month’s midterm elections, blindsided European leaders last week when he struck a deal allowing Russian diesel exports – a move Zelensky said had left him feeling betrayed.

The US president has blamed the rise in fuel prices on the Ukraine-Russia war, eager to deflect attention from his war in Iran which remains deeply unpopular with voters.

On Thursday, Trump once again lashed out at Zelensky in an interview with Newsmax, saying he found him “more difficult to deal with than Putin.” The following day, he walked back on his comments, saying said he had a “good” relationship with his Ukrainian counterpart. “I want him to do one thing,” Trump told reporters at the White House. “Settle the war,” he said.

As Zelensky arrived at Friday’s summit in Brussels, flanked by the European Union’s top leaders, he didn’t mention the deterioration in US relations, but was keen to emphasize the strength of his relationship with the EU.

“I’m so thankful that we have such huge support from (the) EU Council, Commission and leaders – real leaders – so that they stay with us from the very beginning of this war,” Zelensky said as he walked into the summit.

Starlink services not fully restored

Difficulties for Kyiv have mounted this week, with the country reporting restrictions on Starshield, the military-grade version of Elon Musk’s Starlink internet service.

Zelensky said on Friday that the Starlink operations had improved but had not yet been fully restored.

“They disrupted logistics and compromised the protection of the civilian population. That’s why this is very troubling,” Zelensky said, noting the military relied on Starlink-equipped drones, which need to move at a high speed, to deliver food and water to troops on the frontline.

“Have we fully restored the speed we had before? No. Is the speed coming back? Yes,” he added.

Trump on Friday said he was not behind the Starlink disruption, telling reporters at the White House, “I didn’t do that. No, we didn’t do that at all.

“It wasn’t me, and I don’t think it was Elon (Musk). And from what I understand, it’s the same as it’s always been,” he said.

Trump added that he wasn’t sure there were any speed restrictions on Ukraine’s use of Starshield.“I don’t even think it was slowed down. But from what I understand… We didn’t slow it down at all. And I think it’s probably functioning,” Trump said.

Musk said earlier this week that any decision to limit Starshield was up to the US president. A senior US official told CNN that Trump had made no such request.

The Ukrainian government said on Tuesday that it had not received its usual early warning from the US before a Russian ballistic missile struck a major power plant in Kyiv and damaged a residential building.

But Trump insisted that the United States had not stopped sharing intelligence with Ukraine.

Amid a challenging week diplomatically, Ukraine has also run out of missiles for the US-made Patriot air defense system, a source familiar with the situation told CNN on Thursday.

“It’s an open secret that we are not a priority destination for these missiles now,” Zelensky told Friday’s news conference, noting that most Patriot interceptors were now being sent to the Middle East. But he added that Ukraine was grateful to the Europeans “who are financing all of this,” as well as to NATO and to the White House.

Silence speaks volumes

When a reporter asked whether he thought Trump was treating Ukraine as a scapegoat for his own problems given high fuel prices and the ongoing Iran war, Zelensky paused for a full 15 seconds. With a smile, he told the silent room: “This is my answer.”

Earlier the Ukrainian president said his team was in constant contact with US negotiators and would arrange a meeting in the coming days.

“We will keep living, fighting, and most importantly, living with dignity,” he added. “When the quality of life is so terrible during wartime, maintaining dignity is a very important thing.”

EU leaders said they were preparing a new package of sanctions against Russia – the 22nd package since its full-scale invasion of Ukraine. In contrast with the Trump administration, they were keen to stress that sanctions against Moscow would be strengthened unless Putin stops the war.

“We supported President Trump’s energy ceasefire, but we’ve seen that Russia did not respect it – not a single minute. Instead, Russia escalated, and therefore we have to increase the pressure on Russia,” European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said.

Trump said on Friday that he is waiving a number of sanctions related to Russia, days before they were to take effect under a bill he signed into law last month.

The legislation would have imposed tariffs of up to 100% on – among other things – all goods brought into the US from the five largest importers of Russian crude oil or gas, the sale of which is crucial to funding the Kremlin’s war machine.

They were included in the Graham Act, legislation named after former Senator Lindsey Graham, a noted Russia hawk who died in July.

Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said earlier Friday that Zelensky has “no desire” for a peaceful resolution, adding “on that point, we are in complete agreement with President Trump.”

In a visit to a military command post in an undisclosed location, Putin vowed to continue the war.

“In response to strikes by the Kyiv authorities against our industrial and fuel-and-energy sector facilities, the Russian Armed Forces continue to carry out strikes against Ukraine’s military-industrial complex and infrastructure facilities,” Putin said, according to a video released by the Kremlin on Friday.

The video shows Putin wearing military uniform and greeting senior Russian commanders.

CNN’s Victoria Butenko, Anna Chernova and Kit Maher contributed to this report.

World.title: Pope Leo leads Sunday prayers in first major public appearance since lung cancer surgery
World.content:
Rome — XIV has made his first major public appearance since his lung cancer surgery, saying the experience brought him closer to all those who suffer, from the same spot in the Vatican he announced a week ago he needed an operation. Pope Leo XIV has made his first major public appearance since his lung cancer surgery, saying the experience brought him closer to all those who sufferfrom the same spot in the Vatican he announced a week ago he needed an operation.

The 71-year-old pontiff lead the Sunday Angelus from the balcony of the Apostolic Palace overlooking St. Peter’s Square, where thousands gathered to clap, sing and hear his message.

Leo thanked doctors for his treatment and for all those who prayed for him, adding that he is gradually returning to his duties as pope.

“This experience has given me a profound sense of closeness to all those who are going through illness or a state of infirmity,” he told crowds.

“Now that this delicate phase has passed, I will gradually resume my activities – always with the help of God and your prayers. Thank you once again,” he added.

The pope’s remarks came as thousands of runners taking part in the Rome marathon had been jogging up the main walkway leading into St. Peter’s Square taking a right past the papal residence of the Apostolic palace.

At midday, however, all eyes were on Leo XIV when he appeared at the window of his home to address the crowd, wishing them a happy Sunday in a firm and strong voice.

Nuns wait in St Peter’s Square before the Angelus prayer, a day after Pope Leo XIV returns to the Vatican following surgery to remove a cancerous tumour from his right lung, on October 18, 2026. Andreas Solaro/AFP/Getty Images

The pope was released on Saturday from the Gemelli hospital following lung surgery to remove a growth which was later diagnosed as an adenocarcinoma, the most common form of lung cancer.

Doctors say he has made a good recovery following his surgery, even saying he can make trip to Latin America due to take place 6-17 November.

“I would say there are no clinical reasons why it should not take place,” Professor Stefano Margaritora, who operated on the pontiff, told Vatican news.

Last Sunday the pope made his surprise announcement that a “nodule” had been found on his lung, and he was going to have surgery. The news of the cancer diagnosis on Tuesday shocked people inside the Vatican and across the Catholic world, given the pope was known for being in good physical shape.

The pope’s visit to Latin America includes Uruguay, Argentina and Peru. Leo served as a missionary and bishop in Peru for a number of years. His itinerary includes a stop in Cusco, which is around 3,350 meters above sea level, where there is roughly one-third less oxygen available per breath compared to sea-level.

Sharon Braithwaite and Barbie Latza Nadeau contributed reporting.

World.title: Trump and Netanyahu’s once blossoming bromance sours at a pivotal moment for both men
World.content:
For years, Israelis driving the country’s highways in the final weeks of an election have seen the same image: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu standing beside President Donald Trump, under the slogan, “A different league.”

Less than two weeks before the October 27 vote, the billboards of Netanyahu are back.

This time, Trump is not on them.

The president still appears in some videos for Netanyahu’s Likud party, but his absence may signal something beyond advertising.

Trump has so far declined to endorse Netanyahu and has sidestepped questions on whether he should be reelected.

“I’m not involved in [Israeli] politics anymore,” he told Time earlier this month. On Thursday, Trump told Newsmax Netanyahu would like him to be involved in the election. “I’ve had a very good relationship with him,” he said, but avoided endorsing him again. When asked directly whether he trusts Netanyahu, he said bluntly, “I don’t trust anybody in the world of politics.”

For a campaign that has traditionally treated Netanyahu’s intimacy with the White House as a major electoral asset, the restraint is notable.

Trump has starred in Netanyahu’s campaigns since 2013, when still a businessman and TV personality, he released a video urging Israelis to “vote for Benjamin.”

When Trump entered the White House in 2017, he showered Netanyahu with political gifts.

About two weeks before Israel’s April 2019 election, Netanyahu was in Washington to watch Trump sign a historic proclamation recognizing Israeli sovereignty over the occupied Golan Heights. In January 2020, five weeks before Israelis went again to the polls, Trump unveiled the Israeli-Palestinian “Deal of the Century” plan. Netanyahu stood smiling by his side.

Ahead of this election, there has been no red carpet. The last time Netanyahu and Trump met at the White House in August, there were no cameras. The two did not meet at all when Netanyahu traveled to New York for the UN General Assembly in September.

Demonstrators protest against Netanyahu’s address to the UN General Assembly in New York in September. His efforts to undercut peace talks have drawn bipartisan ire. David Dee Delgado/Reuters A protesters against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s policies is arrested after blocking a street next to the United Nations. Spencer Platt/Getty Images

Over the course of the last year, Netanyahu has taken steps that have drawn fury from Trump, including undermining Trump-led peace efforts by striking inside Lebanon and Gaza.

Trump has cursed the prime minister out in phone calls and warned him he’s losing support among Americans, according to people familiar with the conversations. He’s asked why Israel was blowing up apartment buildings in Lebanon and warned about the risk of a global economic downturn as a result of the Iran war.

Inside the White House, many of the moves were interpreted as election-year posturing by Netanyahu, whose internal politics are well known by Trump and his advisers. Over the summer, many Trump advisers came to the conclusion that Netanyahu was trying to prolong the Iran war to bolster his own political standing.

Trump has given Netanyahu a degree of leeway because of those political concerns, people familiar with the matter said. But he’s still grown frustrated at some of Israel’s actions, many of which he believes run counter to American interests.

Another person close to Trump suggested his lack of endorsement is tied to Netanyahu’s weakness in the polls. Trump has long been careful to avoid endorsing candidates who seem likely to lose.

In conversations over the past several months, Trump has quizzed Netanyahu about the election and his prospects, according to people familiar with the matter. While Netanyahu has sought to project confidence, Trump is well aware of the prime minister’s difficult political position.

As Netanyahu’s standing fell in the Trump administration, so did Trump’s standing in Israel.

According to Israeli sources close to Netanyahu, Trump was originally meant to be a centerpiece of Netanyahu’s campaign. Last December, at Mar-a-Lago, the prime minister announced that Trump would become the first non-Israeli to receive the prestigious Israel Prize. Netanyahu aides hoped Trump would accept the prize in person at Israel’s Independence Day ceremony in April, giving jumpstarting the campaign.

Then came the war with Iran.

A smoke plume rises following a missile strike on a building in Tehran on March 1, 2026. Atta Kenare/AFP/Getty Images

The joint US-Israeli attack began on February 28 with the two leaders projecting strategic harmony. Netanyahu thanked “my friend, President Donald Trump,” calling him “a leader who stands by his word.” Trump described the two of them as “war heroes” and publicly demanded that Israel’s president grant Netanyahu a pardon in his ongoing corruption trials.

But Trump never showed interest in attending the Israel Prize ceremony. By then, the fighting in Iran had ended and ceasefire talks were underway.

The Iran ceasefire and subsequent memorandum of understanding were deeply unpopular in Israel, particularly on the right. Yinon Magal, a pro-Netanyahu TV anchor, called Trump a “loser” after the deal was signed.

A July survey by the Jewish People Policy Institute found that only 7% of Israelis had “a great deal of trust” that Trump “will do the right thing” on US-Israel relations, and 45% had none.

“Trump’s stock in Israel, especially among right wing-voters, has weakened,” a Likud source said. “An endorsement would not necessarily have helped Netanyahu so much, so he did not invest much in it.” Another Likud source said, “It’s not as if Trump will endorse any other opponent, so it’s nice to have, but not a must.”

US President Donald Trump leaves the stage after speaking during a campaign rally at the Freeman Coliseum on October 07, in San Antonio, Texas. Win McNamee/Getty Images

Netanyahu’s opponents are watching, but with less alarm than before. “A year ago, our camp was calling anyone close to Trump to prevent an endorsement,” one senior opposition figure said. “Now it doesn’t really matter, the charm is not there.” Another opposition source said they had conveyed messages urging the White House to stay out of the race and appreciated that Trump has so far done so.

When Trump was asked specifically about who is currently polling as Netanyahu’s leading challenger, he said, “Well, I don’t know, I don’t hear bad things about him.” He then said, “They’ve written Bibi off many, many times, just like they’ve written me off many, many times. I wouldn’t underestimate Bibi.”

Trump has his own reasons for distance. American public opinion of Israel has fallen sharply, declining even more against the backdrop of the Iran war. Israel’s average net favorability fell from +51 points in July 2018 to -16 in July 2026, according to multiple polls, a 67-point drop over eight years.

As America quickly soured on the Iran war, a source familiar with the relationship said, Trump has been “trying to shed the image that Netanyahu pulled him into it.”

Still, the apparent distance may be misleading. Israeli sources say the two leaders have recently discussed renewed strikes on Iran. Israeli security sources told CNN preparations are underway – pending Trump’s decision – with timing unclear because of the US midterm elections.

Netanyahu rejected suggestions he was seeking escalation before the vote.

“It is not convenient for us, it’s no good,” he told Army Radio this week. He complained that if Iran fired missiles at Israel, his opponents “will blame me.”

World.title: Grand Egyptian Museum ticket prices to increase starting November 1
World.content:
Ticket prices for the Grand Egyptian Museum (GEM) will increase starting Sunday, November 1.

This adjustment applies to all visitor categories—including Egyptians, Arabs, and foreign nationals—as well as students, children, and senior citizens, depending on the specific ticket type.

Visitors are advised to check the specific rates applicable to their category before completing their booking.

New Ticket Prices

Egyptian visitors: The ticket price increases from LE 200 to LE 220.

Online Booking

Those wishing to visit GEM can book their tickets online through the official website.

It is recommended to consult the official website prior to your visit to confirm the current prices and booking details.

Visiting Hours
