What Novo Argued About the Concerts

Novo said the concerts amounted to “showmícios,” a Brazilian term for music shows used as campaign rallies, which the electoral law (Law 9,504 of 1997) prohibits. Revista Fórum reported the party called them “disguised” rallies.

Brazilian outlets named Caetano Veloso, Djavan and Daniela Mercury among the artists, Jovem Pan reported. The events belong to a movement called “Brasil nas Ruas” (Brazil in the Streets), organised with the 342 Artes collective.

What the Organisers Told the Court

The organiser, UNS Produções Artísticas, told the court the events would defend democracy and avoid vote requests and campaign jingles, according to Plantão Brasil. The 342 Artes collective says electoral law does not stop artists from stating political opinions, Imirante reported.

Cueva stressed that the ruling is not advance approval of the events. The court can still act if actual violations occur on the day, according to Plantão Brasil.

A Second Challenge Failed This Week

A separate challenge to the Copacabana event had already failed. TSE minister André Mendonça closed a case brought by Rio state deputy candidate Leonardo Aragão and an institute, ruling they had no standing to challenge a presidential matter, Metrópoles reported.

Mendonça did not decide whether the event was irregular campaigning, and sent the content of the complaint to the Electoral Prosecutor-General’s Office, according to Perfil Brasil. The Copacabana act was due to start at 4 p.m. in Brasília time, which is 3 p.m. ET.

What It Means for US Readers

For anyone tracking the Brazil election, the rulings show Brazil’s courts reluctant to restrict artists before an event takes place. Expect more complaints about campaign conduct as the 25 October vote nears, and watch the Brazil election polls for new surveys.

For investors in Brazilian stocks, the real or US-listed Brazilian shares, legal disputes like this rarely move prices alone. They add to headline noise in the final week, when the vote result is the main driver.

What Prediction Markets Say

On Polymarket, an online prediction market, bettors give Flávio Bolsonaro an 80.8% chance of winning the 25 October runoff and Lula 19.5% (18 October, 9:10 a.m. ET). The “Brazil Presidential Election” market has about US$187 million in total bets.

Kalshi, a US exchange regulated by the CFTC (the federal derivatives regulator), also lists runoff markets. These prices are bets, not polls, and they can move fast on news.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

Polymarket Flávio Bolsonaro 80.8% · Lula 19.5% (US$187 million traded) Kalshi (regulated in the US by the CFTC) Flávio Bolsonaro 80% · Lula 22% As of 18 October, 9:00 am ET (14:00 Lisbon), updated every 20 minutes. Prices are bets, not polls, and can move fast. Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What Is Not Known

The court has not ruled on whether any event broke electoral law, and the Prosecutor-General’s Office has not said whether it will act on the earlier complaint. Whether Novo will appeal Cueva’s decision is also not known.

It is not known whether anything said on stage on Sunday will draw new complaints. Any such case would be decided after the events, with the runoff days away.

More: Brazil news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did Brazil’s electoral court decide about the Novo party request?

Minister Ricardo Villas Bôas Cueva rejected Novo’s request to suspend pro-democracy concerts planned for Sunday 18 October. He found no proof at this stage that they were campaign rallies.

What is a showmício?

It is a concert or show used as a campaign rally, which Brazilian electoral law prohibits. Novo claimed the artist events were showmícios for Lula.

Which cities did Novo target?

Novo named Copacabana in Rio de Janeiro, Salvador and Porto Alegre. Artists such as Caetano Veloso, Djavan and Daniela Mercury were named in Brazilian reports.

Can the court still punish violations?

Yes, the ruling is not advance approval of the events. The court can act if concrete violations occur.

When is Brazil’s runoff?

Brazilians vote on Sunday 25 October, one week after these events. The runoff is between President Lula and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro.

World.title: What to Do in São Paulo in October 2026: BTS, Iron Maiden and the Berliner Philharmoniker
World.content:
Culture

Key Facts —K-pop takeover. BTS close the month with three stadium nights at MorumBIS on 28, 30 and 31 October. —Metal and pop. Iron Maiden play Nubank Parque twice, and the Pussycat Dolls follow at the same arena on 30 October. —Classical coup. The Berliner Philharmoniker under Kirill Petrenko play Sala São Paulo on 18 and 19 October. —Film and fashion. The Mostra film festival turns fifty across the city’s cinemas, and São Paulo Fashion Week returns to Ibirapuera. —Fashion week. São Paulo Fashion Week N61 runs at Parque Ibirapuera until Sunday 18 October.

If you are wondering what to do in São Paulo this October, pace yourself: São Paulo in October 2026 is shaping up as the city’s biggest live-music month in years, crowned by three BTS stadium nights and a rare visit from the Berliner Philharmoniker.

The concert calendar alone would fill the month: international acts through 31 October, from club stages in Barra Funda to the city’s two biggest open-air venues. Several shows are already close to sold out, so book early.

Around them, October stacks a national holiday, Latin America’s answer to fashion week, the fiftieth edition of the Mostra film festival and one of the strongest classical line-ups Sala São Paulo has ever hosted. Here is the month in order.

São Paulo in October: The Concert Month

Sunday 18 October Dionne Warwick — Over and Out farewell tour Vibra São Paulo, Av. das Nações Unidas 17955, Santo Amaro · 8 p.m. (doors 6 p.m.), from R$190 (about US$38), via Ticket360 A last chance to see a six-Grammy legend who has loved Brazil back for decades.

Friday 23 October Kneecap Cine Joia, Barra Funda · Tickets via Ingresse The Belfast trio behind the BAFTA-winning film, rapping in Irish in a 700-capacity room. Details.

Sunday 25 and Tuesday 27 October Iron Maiden — Run For Your Lives Nubank Parque · Tickets via Livepass Fifty years of Eddie across two São Paulo nights — the metal event of the year in the band’s most loyal market. Details.

Wednesday 28, Friday 30 and Saturday 31 October BTS — Arirang World Tour MorumBIS stadium · Tickets via Ticketmaster Brasil Three stadium nights, seven years in the waiting. Details.

Friday 30 October Pussycat Dolls — PCD Forever Tour Nubank Parque · Tickets via Eventim The reunited group’s only announced Brazilian show — 2000s pop nostalgia at open-air scale. Details.

Friday 30 October Jorja Smith Espaço Unimed, Barra Funda · Tickets via Tickets For Fun One of Britain’s finest modern soul voices in a mid-size room. Details.

Saturday 31 October The Rasmus Carioca Club, Pinheiros · Tickets via Uhuu “In the Shadows” on Halloween night, in one of the city’s classic rock clubs. Details.

São Paulo in October: Classical, Film and Fashion

Until Sunday 18 October “Os Últimos 5 Anos”, a two-hander musical Teatro Nair Bello, São Paulo · Price from the venue The two-person musical about a couple whose love story is told in opposite directions, billed as a 25th-anniversary run. In Portuguese.

Tuesday 13 – Sunday 18 October São Paulo Fashion Week, N61 Pavilhão das Culturas Brasileiras, Parque Ibirapuera (Tuesday 13 shows are held at other venues) · Tickets via Eventim — details at spfw.com.br Latin America’s leading fashion week returns to its Ibirapuera pavilion with 26 shows over six days — the industry’s twice-yearly takeover of the park.

Thursday 15 – Thursday 29 October 50th Mostra Internacional de Cinema Cinemas across São Paulo · 2026 prices pending; single tickets were R$26–32 (US$5–6) last year The city’s main annual window on world cinema turns fifty — opening with James Gray’s “Paper Tiger”, passes traditionally sell out fast. Details.

Sunday 18 and Monday 19 October Berliner Philharmoniker, conducted by Kirill Petrenko Sala São Paulo · R$1,600–5,000 (about US$300–940); benefit concerts for the TUCCA children’s cancer charity, via salasaopaulo.art.br The classical event of the decade for São Paulo: the world’s most famous orchestra and its chief conductor in two benefit nights — expensive, historic and unlikely to return soon.

Thursday 22 October Theatro Municipal String Quartet: Mayer, Mendelssohn, Schumann Theatro Municipal, Praça Ramos de Azevedo, Centro · Price from the theatre A chamber evening inside the city’s 1911 opera house — the room alone is worth the ticket.

Thursday 22 and Saturday 24 October OSESP: Mendelssohn’s “Scottish” Symphony Sala São Paulo · R$50–330 (about US$9–62), via salasaopaulo.art.br Swiss conductor Thierry Fischer leads Mendelssohn’s Third — a mid-season highlight at standard OSESP prices.

Wednesday 28 October, then Wednesdays and Thursdays to 17 December “Epifania – Uma Fábula Moderna” premieres Teatro Estúdio, São Paulo · Tickets via Sympla, price from the venue A new musical by Vitor Rocha opens its run on 28 October. In Portuguese.

Friday 30 and Saturday 31 October (further dates to 7 November) Theatro Municipal double bill: new Jocy de Oliveira opera and Stravinsky’s “Oedipus Rex” Theatro Municipal, Centro · Price from the theatre The opera season’s boldest pairing: a world premiere by Brazilian pioneer Jocy de Oliveira alongside Stravinsky’s stark opera-oratorio. Opera needs no Portuguese.

Still Running: The Big Exhibitions and Family Picks

Mondays and Tuesdays in October, 8 p.m. “A Igreja do Diabo” — musical with Edyelle Brandão Teatro Estúdio · Price from the venue Companhia A Casa que Fala’s new musical runs through the month on Mondays and Tuesdays — in Portuguese, staged for the music.

3 October – 1 November “Miraculous Ladybug: O Show Musical” Teatro VillaLobos, Shopping VillaLobos · Tickets via Sympla The animated hit’s official stage musical stays for the whole month — the family option of the season, built on spectacle rather than dialogue.

Through 31 January 2027 MASP: “Histórias latino-americanas” MASP, Avenida Paulista 1578 · Paid entry; free days midweek — check masp.org.br The museum’s most ambitious show of the decade fills five floors with Latin American art from Mexico to Argentina. Our full story.

Through 24 January 2027 MAM: 39th Panorama of Brazilian Art Museu de Arte Moderna, Parque Ibirapuera · Regular museum ticket Brazil’s most traditional survey of contemporary art asks what art can still do “after everything has been said”. Pairs naturally with a park walk. Our full story.

Through 7 February 2027 IMS Paulista: Fernando Lemos retrospective Instituto Moreira Salles, Avenida Paulista 2424 · Free Some 400 works mark the centenary of the Portuguese-Brazilian surrealist photographer — and the building adds a library, café and rooftop view over Paulista.

Now showing Pinacoteca: Beatriz Milhazes Pinacoteca, Luz district · Price from the venue — check pinacoteca.org.br for the current building and tickets A solo show for one of Brazil’s central contemporary painters, all colour, rhythm and ornament — combine it with the Museu da Língua Portuguesa next door.

Further Ahead: November and December

November opens with the Formula 1 São Paulo Grand Prix at Interlagos on 6–8 November, then the city’s biggest goodbye: Sepultura play the final concert of their 42-year career on 7 November at the Suhai Music Hall, after the show moved from the Pacaembu stadium; existing tickets remain valid. Ty Segall finally makes his Brazil debut at Audio Club on 15 November, Best of Blues and Rock takes Ibirapuera on 20–22 November, and the month closes with Of Monsters and Men and Babymetal. December then stacks CCXP (3–6 December) and Primavera Sound with Gorillaz and The Strokes (5–6 December) into one week.

What are the biggest concerts in São Paulo in October 2026?

Three BTS stadium nights at MorumBIS (28–31 October) and two Iron Maiden shows at Nubank Parque (25 and 27 October) top the bill, followed by the Pussycat Dolls at Nubank Parque, and club shows by Kneecap, Jorja Smith and The Rasmus.

Is 2 November 2026 a public holiday in São Paulo?

Yes. Monday 2 November is Finados (All Souls’ Day), a national holiday under Law 10,607 of 2002, which gives a long weekend from 31 October to 2 November. Expect cemeteries to be busy.

What can I do in São Paulo in October for free?

Free options include the Fernando Lemos retrospective at IMS Paulista, MASP’s free midweek days for “Histórias latino-americanas”, and a car-free Avenida Paulista every Sunday, with the Feirinha da Liberdade street market a short metro ride away.

World.title: What to Do in Rio in October 2026
World.content:
Rio de Janeiro · Culture

A Leblon theatre keeps up its bossa nova weekends until 8 November, The Color Purple plays as a musical in Barra until the 25th, and the CCBB’s October programme is free. The rest of the month, day by day.

The rotunda of the Centro Cultural Banco do Brasil in Centro, where the October programme is free. (Photo: Bruna Prado)

RIO DE JANEIRO — There is a great deal to do in Rio in October, and very little of it is written down anywhere in English. This guide is the monthly selection for people who live here rather than visit: what is on, where, when, what it costs, and why it might be worth crossing the city for.

Until 8 November the Teatro Café Pequeno in Leblon keeps up its eighteen-concert bossa nova season, and until 25 October the musical A Cor Púrpura plays a short run in Barra. Here is the rest of the month.

Until 8 November: Bossa Nova Weekends in Leblon

Fridays and Saturdays 8pm, Sundays 7pm Bossa Nova Sessions at the Teatro Café Pequeno Teatro Café Pequeno, Av. Ataulfo de Paiva 269, Leblon · From R$50 (about US$10) Eighteen concerts over five weekends in the neighbourhood where the genre was born. The line-up runs from harmonica player Maurício Einhorn and singer Ithamara Koorax to guitarist Victor Biglione, who marks fifty years on stage this year — his 1995 Montreux live album, co-produced by Quincy Jones, has just been reissued. Small room, reserved tables, the most accessible October programme in the city for a listener without Portuguese.

Mid-October

Wednesdays and Thursdays, until 22 October, 7pm “Pra Quem Não Me Conhece” returns to the Laura Alvim Casa de Cultura Laura Alvim, Ipanema · Price from the venue Nicole Musafir’s comedy about her own life, extended after sold-out shows at its premiere. In the first run her grandmother, the pianist Lydia Musafir, played in public for the first time at 91. In Portuguese.

Until Sunday 25 October A Cor Púrpura — The Color Purple, the musical, fifth Rio season Teatro Multiplan, Shopping VillageMall, Av. das Américas 3900, Barra da Tijuca · From R$60 (about US$11) · Wednesday to Friday 8pm, Saturday 4pm and 8pm, Sunday 3.30pm and 7.30pm Fourteen performances only of the Brazilian production of the Alice Walker musical, with Suzana Santana again as Celie and Tadeu Aguiar directing. English-speaking audiences know the story from the novel and the films, which makes this the easiest musical in town to follow in Portuguese. Tickets through Sympla and the box office; every section also has a solidarity ticket at a special price against one kilo of food.

Thursdays through November, 8pm “Jazz dos Muertos” on Thursdays at La Esquina in Lapa La Esquina, Lapa · Price from the venue A new weekly jazz night in the heart of Rio’s bohemian district, built around jazz, Latin jazz, bossa nova, samba jazz and soul. It opened on 15 October with “Aura Jazz” by the Giovana Adoracion Quinteto, and the name is a playful nod to the idea that the old masters are gone but their music is still on stage. Simple to enjoy without Portuguese.

Sunday 18 October Vanessa da Mata at Vivo Rio Vivo Rio, Av. Infante Dom Henrique 85, Parque do Flamengo · Price from the venue One of the defining voices of Brazilian pop of the last two decades, in the big auditorium inside the Flamengo park. Her catalogue crosses MPB, pop and reggae, and most of the room will know every word.

Its Banking segment offers various products and services, including…

Late October

Tuesday 20 October to Sunday 1 November Cine Uruguai: Novos Horizontes at CAIXA Cultural CAIXA Cultural Rio de Janeiro · Free Twenty-one Uruguayan films, sixteen features and five shorts from the last ten years, with talks and a masterclass. It opens with “Agarra-me Forte”, a Goya nominee for best Ibero-American film, and 23 October is a tribute day to the former president José “Pepe” Mujica with “Uma Noite de 12 Anos” at 2.30pm and the documentary “Os Sonhos de Pepe” at 5pm.

Thursday 22 October, 8pm Naiara Martins launches “Terras do Sem-Fim” at Acaso Cultural Acaso Cultural, Rua Vicente de Sousa 16, Botafogo · Price from the venue The singer, songwriter and literary critic, nominated for a 2024 Jabuti Prize in philosophy, presents the show built on her first album. It runs from bossa and samba to songs with words in Yoruba and Kayapó, under the musical direction of Pedro Braga.

Thursday 22 October, 8.30pm Suzy Mac presents her EP “Amor e Atitude” at the Dolores Club Dolores Club, Rua do Lavradio 10, Lapa · R\$60 (about US\$12), half-price R\$30 (about US\$6) The Brazilian-American singer released the EP on 16 October and brings it to Lapa on 22 October. Her sound mixes samba, bossa nova, soul and jazz, so the language is no barrier.

Friday 23 October John Pizzarelli at Vivo Rio Vivo Rio, Av. Infante Dom Henrique 85, Parque do Flamengo · Price from the venue The American jazz guitarist and singer, a regular visitor to Brazil, with the songbook between Nat King Cole and bossa nova. The month’s most expat-friendly evening in a big room.

Saturday 24 October, 8pm Black Pantera open their Brazil tour at the Circo Voador Circo Voador, Lapa · Price from the venue The trio from Uberaba, Rock Artist of the Year 2025, starts its Continental tour in Rio. Hard, political rock from the interior of Minas Gerais. Details here.

Saturday 24 October, 9.30pm Oswaldo Montenegro at the Qualistage Qualistage, Av. Ayrton Senna 3000, Barra da Tijuca · Price from the venue The songwriter and filmmaker with the melodic catalogue that half of Brazil grew up on. Melodic, unhurried, and a good introduction to mainstream Brazilian songwriting.

Sunday 25 October, 11am Quarteto Atlas plays Villa-Lobos string quartets in Tijuca Centro da Música Carioca Artur da Távola, Rua Conde de Bonfim 824, Tijuca · Free, tickets at the box office from one hour before Leading players from the Theatro Municipal orchestra, the Orquestra Sinfônica Brasileira and the Petrobras Symphony take Heitor Villa-Lobos’s string quartets from the French-tinged No. 1 of 1915 through the folk-song No. 5 to No. 17, written two years before his death. The musicians introduce each piece in Portuguese, but the music needs no translation; the tour opens on Tuesday 20 October at 7pm at the Teatro da UFF in Icaraí, Niterói, also free.

Free at the CCBB Through October

Until Monday 19 October Soy Loco por Ti, Centroamérica — Central American cinema Centro Cultural Banco do Brasil, Rua Primeiro de Março 66, Centro · Free Twenty-one features and shorts from Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador, Nicaragua, Costa Rica and Panama, most of them never before screened in Brazil, in their original languages with Portuguese subtitles. It runs three weeks into October and costs nothing.

Until 16 November Amazônicas — Poéticas Femininas Centro Cultural Banco do Brasil, Rua Primeiro de Março 66, Centro · Free Women artists from the North of Brazil, curated by Sissa Aneleh, with Afro-indigenous ancestry at the centre and virtual- and augmented-reality elements. It runs well past the end of the month, so there is no rush.

Running All Month

Until Sunday 1 November, Fridays 8pm, Saturdays and Sundays 7pm “Heathers – O Musical” in a new Rio staging Teatro Nathalia Timberg, Barra da Tijuca · Price from the venue A new Brazilian staging of the Broadway musical, directed by Rafaela Amado with musical direction by Anna Hannickel. It runs on weekends from 9 October, in Portuguese.

Until Sunday 25 October, Fridays and Saturdays 7pm, Sundays 6pm “Café, Almoço, Jantar” at the Casa de Cultura Laura Alvim Casa de Cultura Laura Alvim, Ipanema · Price from the venue A comedy of manners that follows one family through 1987, 1994 and 2018, three breakfast, lunch and dinner scenes in a boarding house, to show how Brazil’s politics and economy reach private life. Written by Ivan Fernandes, back for a short run after a September premiere at the CCJF.

Every Saturday, from midnight Rock-blues at the Bukowski, the oldest rock bar in the city Bar Bukowski, Rua Álvaro Ramos 270, Botafogo · R$39.90 (about US$8) at the door, free from 1am on the guest list The Saturday-night residency continues through October: the Charles Zanol Trio from midnight, with Pedro Leão on guitar and Dawton Mendes on drums and cajón. R$39.90 (about US$8) at the door includes a drink if you arrive before 10pm; R$99.90 (about US$19) gives you R$80 (about US$15) back in food and drink. Names on the guest list through @barbukowski enter free from 1am. The bar runs from 7pm to 5am.

Until 4 December The Jazz Room: a Sinatra and Armstrong tribute Teatro Rival Petrobras, Rua Álvaro Alvim 33, Cinelândia · From R$100 (about US$19) The Rival’s long-running tribute evening — the American songbook with a live band in the Art Deco theatre off Cinelândia. The reliable option when nothing else on this list fits the night.

Through October October season at the CCJF: four new exhibitions, film festivals and concerts Centro Cultural Justiça Federal, Av. Rio Branco 241, Centro · Price from the venue The federal-justice cultural center opens four exhibitions this month (word-and-image rooms, an eleven-artist audiovisual collective, a show on native bees and an artist working with state-school children), alongside theater, two film festivals with retrospectives, open-air cinema and concerts ranging from a flute orchestra to MPB choirs, opera and jazz. The full day-by-day program is on the CCJF site.

22 and 31 October, two stops “Um Rio Dentro de Mim” — the award-nominated musical tours greater Rio São João de Meriti (22 Oct) · Nova Iguaçu (31 Oct) · Price from the venue Carol Botelho and Deborah Marins sing Vinicius de Moraes and Aldir Blanc in a musical that reads as a mother’s love letter to Rio — twice nominated for the Prêmio Musical Rio and on the road through the Sesc network until the end of the month.

Football in Rio in October: The Last Clássico

Thursday 29 October, 8pm One derby left in October: Vasco against Flamengo Vasco home fixture, stadium to be confirmed · Tickets from the clubs Vasco host Flamengo on Thursday 29 October, which the Brazilian football confederation (CBF) has set for 8pm; confirm the stadium before you go. It is the last clássico of the month, so buy only through the clubs’ own sites, and go early.

Planning Your Rio in October

Sunday 25 October is the second round of the general election: the presidential race and the contest for Rio de Janeiro governor both go to a runoff, with voting from 8am to 5pm. Rio de Janeiro state did not restrict alcohol sales in the first round; check nearer the date whether that holds for the runoff.

Where we have not printed a ticket price, the organisers had not published one at the time of writing — check with the venue before you travel. Programmes at the CCBB and the theatres change during the month, so confirm on the day.

Dollar values use the RT rate of about R$5.22 to US$1 on 5 October 2026.

This guide to Rio in October runs monthly, and returns in November. If you run a venue, a gallery or a production in Rio and would like to be considered, write to the newsroom with the date, the time, the address and the ticket price.

Those four things are what get an event into the list.

More on living here: our Rio de Janeiro coverage and Expats in Brazil.

World.title: Best Places to Live in Ghana for Expats 2026
World.content:
Expats · Ghana

For most American expats, the best place to live in Ghana is Accra, and above all its gated eastern and airport-side districts of East Legon, Airport Residential and Cantonments. Kumasi ranks third for culture and a slower pace. Ghana is rated Level 2, “exercise increased caution”, by the US State Department, with the north rated higher.

Key Facts —Who. American retirees, remote workers and families weighing West Africa’s English-speaking democracy, which is a popular destination for the African diaspora. —What. Four areas ranked on safety warnings, services, medical access and entry rules: Accra’s eastern districts, Osu and Labone, Kumasi, and Cape Coast. —Why it matters. The US State Department says emergency medical services outside Accra are limited and advises Americans to reconsider travel to the northern border regions, so the capital region is the practical base for newcomers. —Entry. Americans need an electronic visa from the Ghana Immigration Service portal, launched on 25 May 2026, at a reported fee of US$260 for tourism or business. —Safety. Advisory level 2 of 4, “exercise increased caution”, issued on 7 July 2026; violent crime, including carjacking and street mugging, occurs, often after dark.

The Short Answer: Accra First, and Stay Near It

East Legon, Airport Residential and Cantonments rank first because they combine gated compounds, access to Kotoka International Airport and the largest choice of international schools and clinics. Osu and Labone rank second for restaurants, nightlife and the beach at Labadi.

This ranking is our editorial judgement, not a statistical index. We found no dated, official crime rate for individual Accra districts, so the order rests on the State Department advisory, on where services are located and on how Ghanaian property portals describe each area.

Rank Area Best for Main drawback 1 East Legon, Airport Residential and Cantonments (Accra) Gated housing, schools, airport access, diplomatic community Traffic; higher prices than the rest of the city 2 Osu and Labone (Accra) Restaurants, nightlife, short trips to the beach Noise and crowds; petty crime after dark 3 Kumasi (Ashanti Region) Culture, university life, a slower pace Fewer expat services; limited emergency care 4 Cape Coast (Central Region) History, coastal setting, lower profile Small expat community; long trip to Accra for specialist care

How We Ranked, and What Washington Says About Ghana

The US State Department rates Ghana Level 2, “exercise increased caution”, in an advisory issued on 7 July 2026. It cites crime, limited health infrastructure and violence against women, and says violent crime such as carjacking, street mugging and assault occurs, often at night and in remote places.

The advisory tells Americans to reconsider travel to the northern border in the Upper East Region, the Northeast Region, the Upper West Region and the areas of the Savannah Region west of the N12 highway. The advisory cites crime in these areas.

Africa Intelligence One email, every weekday morning. African markets, politics and business — filed from our newsroom in Rio. Yesterday’s subject line: “Is Morocco safe? Washington says use increased caution” Get the brief Free. We send a confirmation link first — nothing arrives until you click it. Unsubscribe with one click in any edition. If you stop opening us for 30 days we stop sending by ourselves, as we assume the interest is no longer there. See our privacy policy. We never share your email.

Advisories change, so read the full text on the State Department site before you travel.

1. East Legon, Airport Residential and Cantonments

These districts sit in the eastern and central parts of Accra and hold much of the capital’s expat housing, with gated compounds, backup generators and water tanks among the typical features. East Legon is about an 11-minute drive from Kotoka International Airport, according to a Ghanaian property portal.

Rice and other staples on sale at a market in Accra. File photo, 2011. Photo: Susan Quinn / USAID Africa, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

Cantonments is home to many diplomats, which adds services but also traffic around embassies. The State Department says emergency medical services outside Accra are limited, which is the strongest reason we place the capital region first. Our healthcare guide lists the main private hospitals.

2. Osu and Labone

Osu is the entertainment heart of Accra, and Labone is a quieter residential neighbour with easy access to Labadi Beach. They suit younger professionals who want restaurants and bars within a short ride.

Crowds and late-night noise come with the location, and petty theft is a recognised problem across Ghana. Use a ride-hailing app after dark and avoid carrying valuables. Our Is Ghana safe for expats guide covers the precautions.

3. Kumasi

Kumasi is Ghana’s second city and the capital of the Ashanti Region, home to the Manhyia Palace Museum and the KNUST university. It has a slower rhythm than Accra and a smaller foreign community.

A gold-decorated helmet at the Manhyia Palace Museum in Kumasi. Photo: Ebbsonline, CC0 via Wikimedia Commons.

Because emergency services outside Accra are limited, Kumasi suits healthy newcomers with good insurance. Confirm that your policy covers evacuation to Accra or abroad.

4. Cape Coast

Cape Coast is a historic coastal town in the Central Region, known for its colonial-era castle and its place in the story of the Atlantic slave trade. It draws heritage visitors and a small number of long-stay residents.

We rank it last for newcomers because the expat community and services are smaller, and specialist care is far away. It can work as a base for people who already know Ghana well.

Entry and Residency: What the Rules Say

Americans must apply for an electronic visa before they travel. The Ghana Immigration Service launched its new e-visa portal on 25 May 2026, and a law firm’s summary reports a fee of US$260 for a tourism or business e-visa, with faster processing costing more.

Living or working in Ghana needs a separate permit, so a visit is not permission to settle. Our Ghana residency guide and retirement guide set out the options.

What It Means for You

If you are scouting Ghana, rent in Accra first and visit Kumasi or Cape Coast as day or weekend trips. Check your insurance for medical evacuation before you sign a lease.

Ghana’s statistics service publishes inflation data every month, and our Accra cost of living guide and Ghana hub carry the latest prices and news. We will update this guide when the advisory changes.

What Is Not Known

We could not confirm current rents by district or a crime rate for any Accra neighbourhood, and we took the advisory’s wording from reports of it as well as its summary. The ranking is therefore a judgement about services and published warnings, not a measured safety index.

Visa fees and advisories change often. Check the official sources listed below before you travel or sign a lease.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the best place to live in Ghana for expats?

For most American expats, Accra is the best base, and within it East Legon, Airport Residential and Cantonments rank first for gated housing, schools and access to the airport. Osu and Labone rank second for restaurants and nightlife.

Is Ghana safe for American expats?

The US State Department rates Ghana Level 2, exercise increased caution, and warns that violent crime such as carjacking, street mugging and assault occurs, often at night or in isolated places. It tells Americans to reconsider travel to the northern border regions and parts of the Savannah Region, not to Accra.

Do Americans need a visa for Ghana?

Yes. Americans apply for an electronic visa through the Ghana Immigration Service portal, which launched on 25 May 2026, and the reported fee for a tourism or business e-visa is US$260.

Is medical care good outside Accra?

The State Department says emergency medical services outside Accra are limited and advises travellers to check that insurance covers medical evacuation. That is a strong reason to live in or near Accra.

Is Kumasi a good alternative to Accra?

Kumasi is Ghana’s second city and the seat of the Asante kingdom, with a university and a lower profile for foreigners. It suits people who want culture and a quieter pace and who accept fewer expat services.

What should same-sex couples know before moving to Ghana?

The US advisory says same-sex activity is illegal in Ghana and can bring a fine or up to three years in jail, and it notes violence against lesbian and gay travellers. Couples should read the full advisory and take legal advice before they decide.

World.title: Best Places to Live in Kenya for Expats 2026
World.content:
Expats · Kenya

For most American expats, Nairobi’s western suburbs of Karen and Gigiri are the best place to live in Kenya: green, close to international schools and the United Nations, and far from the districts Washington warns against. The coast around Diani ranks third because the beach life is real but security needs more homework. Kenya is rated Level 2, “exercise increased caution”, by the US State Department.

Key Facts —Who. American retirees, remote workers, aid staff and families weighing Kenya, a country that hosts the United Nations’ Nairobi headquarters. —What. Four areas ranked on safety warnings, services, schools and transport: Karen and Gigiri, Kilimani and Westlands, Diani, and Mombasa. —Why it matters. The US State Department warns against travel to Nairobi’s Eastleigh and Kibera, to the Somalia border counties and to parts of the north coast, so the choice of neighbourhood matters more than the choice of city. —Getting around. The Madaraka Express train links Nairobi and Mombasa in about 4 hours 30 minutes, with Economy fares of KSh 1,500 (about US$12) at KSh 129.65 per US dollar. —Entry. Most visitors, including US citizens, need an electronic travel authorisation (eTA), applied for online and usually processed in about three days.

Free download · Expat checklist Get the free checklist as PDF Moving to Kenya 2026: the step-by-step checklist. This guide condensed into 3 printable pages with tick boxes and the key official links. The Short Answer: Nairobi’s Gated Suburbs First, Mombasa Last

Karen and Gigiri rank first because they combine quiet, tree-lined streets with the highest concentration of foreign schools, clinics and embassy staff. Kilimani and Westlands rank second for apartments, restaurants and short commutes, though traffic is heavy.

This ranking is our editorial judgement, not a statistical index. We found no dated, official crime rate for individual Nairobi suburbs, so the order rests on published safety warnings, where services are located and how foreigners describe each area.

Rank Area Best for Main drawback 1 Karen, Gigiri and Runda (Nairobi) Space, gardens, schools, UN and embassy community Long drives; traffic to the centre 2 Kilimani and Westlands (Nairobi) Apartments, restaurants, offices within reach Congestion and noise; pick the street with care 3 Diani Beach (Kwale County) Beach life and a slower pace Security needs local advice; fewer services 4 Mombasa Port city, railway terminus, history Heat and humidity; fewer foreign-friendly services than Nairobi

How We Ranked, and What Washington Says About Kenya

The US State Department rates Kenya Level 2, “exercise increased caution”, citing crime, terrorism, kidnapping and unrest. Its advisory tells Americans to reconsider travel to the Nairobi neighbourhoods of Eastleigh and Kibera because of armed carjacking, mugging, home invasion and kidnapping.

The advisory also says Americans should not travel to the Somalia border counties of Garissa, Wajir and Mandera, to Tana River County or to coastal areas north of Malindi. It lists other remote border areas too.

Advisories change, so read the full text on the State Department site before you travel.

1. Karen, Gigiri and Runda: The Expat Heartland

Karen, in the south-west of Nairobi, is a garden suburb of large plots and mature trees with a long-standing foreign community. Gigiri, in the north, is the diplomatic district around the United Nations Office at Nairobi, which hosts the headquarters of the UN Environment Programme and UN-Habitat.

Nairobi’s central business district. Most expats live in suburbs outside the centre and commute in. Photo: Tall Black, CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons.

Nairobi sits at about 1,800 metres, so days are mild and nights are cool all year. That altitude is a draw for people who dislike tropical heat, and it spares the city much of the coast’s humidity.

The trade-off is distance and traffic. A school run or a hospital visit can take an hour each way at peak times, so many families choose a home by where the school is. Our healthcare guide explains where the private hospitals are.

2. Kilimani and Westlands: Apartments Near the Action

Kilimani and Westlands are apartment districts close to offices, shops and restaurants. They suit single professionals and couples who want to walk to dinner and keep a short commute.

Street-level crime is the main concern in dense parts of the city, and the State Department lists armed carjacking and mugging among the risks across Kenya. Choose a building with a guarded entrance, avoid walking at night and use a ride-hailing app rather than hailing a street taxi. Our Is Kenya safe for expats guide covers the precautions in detail.

3. Diani Beach: The Coast Lifestyle

Diani is a long stretch of white-sand beach in Kwale County, south of Mombasa, and the favourite coastal base for foreign residents. We did not find Kwale County among the areas the US advisory tells Americans not to visit, but the advisory does single out stretches of the coast for terrorism and kidnapping risk.

A Kenya Airways Boeing 737 at Moi International Airport, Mombasa, in August 2025. Many coastal visitors fly into Mombasa and travel on by road. Photo: Bahnfrend, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

Residents and tourists in Diani have long raised concerns about insecurity, and Kenyan press reports describe new street lighting and extra patrols meant to restore night-time activity. Ask neighbours and your landlord about specific roads and the hours when they feel safe before you commit to a lease.

4. Mombasa: Port, Railway and Heat

Mombasa is Kenya’s main port and the coastal end of the Madaraka Express railway. The train takes about 4 hours 30 minutes to Nairobi, with three daily departures at 08:00, 15:00 and 22:00, and Economy fares of KSh 1,500 (about US$12) one way.

We rank Mombasa last for newcomers because of heat, humidity and fewer foreign-friendly services than Nairobi. It still suits people who work in shipping or trade, or who want a historic coastal city.

Entry and Residency: What the Rules Say

Most foreign visitors, including US citizens, must apply online for an electronic travel authorisation, known as an eTA, before they travel. Citizens of some countries and East African Community members are exempt. The official eTA portal says applications are usually processed in about three days and advises applying at least two weeks ahead.

Living or working in Kenya needs a separate permit, and landing without a visa is not permission to work. Our residency visa guide sets out the classes, and our guide to the eTA and travel insurance rule covers what visitors must buy.

What It Means for You

If you are scouting Kenya, rent for a few months in two areas before you commit to either. Visit in the dry and the rainy season, and confirm travel advice with your embassy before booking.

Kenya observes Mashujaa Day, a national holiday, on Tuesday 20 October 2026, and September inflation was 6.8%, according to the national statistics bureau. Our retirement guide, Nairobi cost of living guide and Kenya hub carry the rest.

What Is Not Known

We could not confirm current rents by suburb or a crime rate for any Nairobi district, and we could not read the current State Department advisory line by line, so its wording is taken from reports of it. The ranking is therefore a judgement about services and published warnings, not a measured safety index.

Fares, entry rules and advisories change often. Check the official sources listed below before you travel or sign a lease.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the best place to live in Kenya for expats?

For most American expats, Nairobi’s Karen and Gigiri area is the best base because it has the greatest concentration of international schools, embassies and UN staff. Kilimani and Westlands rank second for apartments and walkability.

Is Kenya safe for American expats?

The US State Department rates Kenya Level 2, exercise increased caution, and warns against travel to Nairobi’s Eastleigh and Kibera and to several border and north-coast areas. Most expats live in a few gated suburbs and take the precautions the embassy lists, such as avoiding night driving and sharing less about travel plans.

Do Americans need a visa to live in Kenya?

Visitors, including US citizens, apply online for an electronic travel authorisation (eTA), which the official portal says is usually processed in about three days. Living or working in Kenya needs a separate permit or residency class, covered in our Kenya residency guide.

Is Diani Beach a good place to live?

It suits people who want a beach lifestyle, and it sits in Kwale County, which we did not find among the areas the US warning tells Americans not to visit. Security has needed attention, so ask local residents and your landlord about specific roads before you sign a lease.

How do you get from Nairobi to Mombasa?

The Madaraka Express train takes about four and a half hours and runs three times a day. Reported one-way fares are KSh 1,500 (about US$12) in Economy and KSh 4,500 (about US$35) in First Class.

Why is Nairobi popular with international organisations?

The United Nations Office at Nairobi in Gigiri hosts the headquarters of the UN Environment Programme and UN-Habitat. That draws diplomats, aid workers and consultants, and it supports a large market for expat housing and schools.

World.title: Vida Loca Drug Suspect Sent to Madagascar
World.content:
A man known as “Vida Loca”, wanted over an alleged cocaine network linking Madagascar, Mauritius and Southeast Asia, was extradited from Spain to Madagascar on Friday 16 October 2026. The case matters to US readers because it touches Indian Ocean drug routes, money laundering through Asian hubs and Interpol cooperation.

Key Facts —Who. The suspect known as “Vida Loca”, a Franco-Mauritian man and naturalised French citizen, reportedly named as Maurice Vitto Laurent Jeevanji, aged 57. —What. Extradited on charges of high-risk drug trafficking, money laundering and criminal association; he is a suspect and is presumed innocent until a court rules. —Where. From Spain to Madagascar; the alleged network ran between Madagascar, Mauritius and Southeast Asia. —When. Friday 16 October 2026. —Why it matters. The case involves Indian Ocean cocaine routes, money laundering through Asian hubs and cooperation with Interpol. —Status. As of 18 October 2026, 11:00 GMT

What We Know

Spain extradited the suspect known as “Vida Loca” to Madagascar on Friday 16 October 2026, according to Newsmada and Défi Media. Spanish authorities had detained him on an international arrest warrant from Madagascar’s Pôle Anti-Corruption (PAC), the country’s anti-corruption unit, and on an Interpol Red Notice.

Défi Media has named him as Maurice Vitto Laurent Jeevanji, aged 57, in a January 2026 profile. He is a Franco-Mauritian man and a naturalised French citizen, while other outlets call him Laurent Vitto.

According to Newsmada, the charges are high-risk drug trafficking, money laundering and criminal association (“association de malfaiteurs” in French). These are accusations at this stage, and he is presumed innocent until a court rules.

Newsmada reported that the extradition followed judicial cooperation between Madagascar and Spain. The ministries of Justice, Foreign Affairs and Public Security, Interpol and Spanish authorities all took part.

An Interpol Red Notice asks police in member countries to locate a wanted person and hold them provisionally pending extradition. Spain acted on both that notice and the Madagascan warrant.

Antananarivo, Madagascar. (Photo: Rod Waddington, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

The Network Investigators Describe

Défi Media reported in January 2026 that investigators suspect “Vida Loca” of being the central figure and financier of an international cocaine network. The network allegedly ran between Madagascar, Mauritius and Southeast Asia, touching Bangkok, Pattaya, Antananarivo and Port Louis.

The same reporting says he allegedly financed the Appaya clan, a group named in the reporting. It also says Spain had opened its own drug investigation.

Défi Media reported that 16 kg of cocaine was seized in Madagascar in February 2025. It also says three Mauritians and five Malagasies were arrested in early 2025.

Défi Media reported that a confidential PAC report on the matter went to Mauritius’ Financial Crimes Commission (FCC). The FCC is among the Mauritian bodies investigating the case.

Défi Media further reported that an intercepted phone call in January 2025 reportedly contained instructions on transporting drugs and threats. We have not independently verified this, and none of it has been tested in court.

What Is Not Known

The date of his arrest in Spain has not been made public in the reports we reviewed. Nor is it known where he is being held in Madagascar or when he will appear in court.

No plea has been reported, and no statement from his lawyers has appeared in the coverage we saw. No official figure for the money involved has been published in those reports either.

Motives, roles and guilt are matters for the court, and we do not speculate on them. Défi Media’s account of the network rests on investigators’ suspicions, not on a verdict.

What It Means for Readers in the United States

This is a story about transit routes and money, not about a single country. Défi Media describes a network spanning the Indian Ocean and Southeast Asia, touching hubs such as Bangkok and Pattaya.

The case also shows Interpol cooperation at work, with Spain acting on a Red Notice and a warrant issued in Madagascar. For compliance teams, it is a reminder that cross-border money laundering cases can involve several jurisdictions at once.

Mauritius’ Financial Crimes Commission is named in the reporting as one of the bodies investigating. Madagascar’s anti-corruption unit issued the arrest warrant that led to his detention in Spain.

For related coverage, see our reports on Madagascar Seeks 11 Chinese Convicts and Mauritius Sergeant Charged After Woman Shot. Our country pages for Mauritius and Madagascar carry further reporting.

The suspect is now in Madagascar and the charges are yet to be tested in court. Further official detail on his detention, hearing and plea would show how the case proceeds.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is “Vida Loca”?

“Vida Loca” is an alias used for a Franco-Mauritian man and naturalised French citizen. Défi Media has named him as Maurice Vitto Laurent Jeevanji, aged 57, while other outlets call him Laurent Vitto.

What is he accused of?

Newsmada reports the charges as high-risk drug trafficking, money laundering and criminal association. He is a suspect and is presumed innocent until a court rules.

When and how was he extradited?

He was extradited from Spain to Madagascar on Friday 16 October 2026. Spain had arrested him on a warrant from Madagascar’s anti-corruption unit and on an Interpol Red Notice.

What is still unknown?

The date of his arrest in Spain, his place of detention, a court date and his plea have not been reported. No statement from his lawyers has been published in the coverage we reviewed.

World.title: Brazil Court Sets Rules on Campaign Channels
World.content:
The Supreme Federal Court in Brasília, which set new liability rules for social media platforms in June 2025 (Photo: Agência Senado, CC BY 2.0 via Wikimedia Commons)

BRAZIL · ELECTIONS

Published Sunday, 18 October, 5:58 a.m. ET · Source: Brazil’s Superior Electoral Court (TSE)

Key Facts The country Brazil, Latin America’s largest country, elects its president in a runoff on Sunday 25 October between President Lula and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro.

What happened On Friday 16 October, the electoral court (TSE) unanimously approved rules on when a supporters’ messaging channel counts as part of a campaign.

The trigger Conflicting rulings on “Exército do Lula”, a WhatsApp channel run by federal deputy André Janones, pushed the court to set clear criteria.

Meta order On Thursday 15 October, Judge Marco Aurélio Bellizze ordered Meta to treat both candidates equally, under a fine of R$500,000 (about US$99,000) a day.

Power Index Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 75.0 points (October 2026 edition).

Prediction markets Polymarket gives Flávio Bolsonaro an 81% chance of winning the 25 October runoff and Lula 19.5% (18 October, 5:54 a.m. ET). Polymarket puts Flávio Bolsonaro’s chance of winning at 81% and Kalshi at 80% (Lula: 20% and 20% ), as of 18 October, 7:40 am ET ; prices are bets, not polls.

Still open The court has not said how it will treat other supporter channels, and campaigns can still challenge individual cases.

Brazil’s electoral court entered the last week before the Brazil election 2026 runoff with new rules for online campaigning. On Friday 16 October, the Superior Electoral Court (TSE) unanimously approved a resolution on when a supporters’ channel is legally linked to a campaign.

The vote on Sunday 25 October decides who runs Latin America’s largest economy, so online disputes between the two campaigns matter beyond Brazil. The court is the body that supervises the election and rules on campaign conduct, including on social media and messaging apps.

What the New Campaign Channel Rules Say

The resolution was drafted by Judge André Mendonça and sets out objective signs that a channel is tied to a candidacy, CNN Brasil reported. They include the use of campaign money or material resources, technical support from the campaign, official promotion of the channel and campaign guidance on what it publishes.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Brazil ranks 1st of 14 with 75.0 points. Strongest pillar: military means (100); weakest: state capacity & security (56). Alignment group: Hedging. WatchRating below investment grade (BB); public debt at 93% of GDP. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

The signs are not cumulative, and one objectively verifiable element can be enough, CNN Brasil said. A channel linked to a campaign must be registered with the electoral authorities and follow the propaganda rules for its platform.

Spontaneous support from individual voters is not enough on its own to show a link, according to ICL Notícias. The aim is to separate organised campaign operations from ordinary political speech.

Why the Court Acted After Conflicting Rulings

The resolution followed a dispute over “Exército do Lula”, a WhatsApp channel administered by federal deputy André Janones of the Rede party, Gazeta do Paraná reported. Flávio Bolsonaro’s campaign had complained to the court that the channel spread disinformation.

Two TSE judges then issued opposite decisions on whether the channel could stay online, the same outlet said. On Sunday 11 October, the court’s president, Kassio Nunes Marques, suspended it, and the electoral ombudsman, Ricardo Villas Bôas Cueva, reversed that the same day for lack of evidence.

Nunes Marques suspended it again on Tuesday 13 October unless it was registered, and the channel was back online around 14 October, according to Folha de Pernambuco.

Meta Ordered to Treat Both Candidates Equally

A day earlier, on Thursday 15 October, Judge Marco Aurélio Bellizze ordered Meta, the owner of Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, not to restrict the reach of presidential candidates unequally, Bahia Notícias reported. The order carries a fine of R$500,000 (about US$99,000 at 5.07 reais per dollar) for each day of non-compliance.

Lula’s campaign had told the court that Meta’s artificial intelligence tool refused to generate images of the president while accepting requests about Flávio Bolsonaro, according to the same report. The judge found signs of a failure in Meta’s control system but said the evidence did not show deliberate or systematic misconduct.

What It Means for US Readers

Brazil’s court is now setting the online ground rules for a vote that moves Brazilian stocks, the real and trade ties with Washington. US-listed Brazilian shares can swing on court rulings as much as on polls in the final days.

The Meta order also shows a foreign platform facing daily fines from a Brazilian court during an election. Expect more rulings of this kind before 25 October, and read each as a decision on one case rather than a signal about the outcome.

What Prediction Markets Say

On Polymarket, an online prediction market, bettors give Flávio Bolsonaro an 81.0% chance of winning the 25 October runoff and Lula 19.5% (18 October, 5:54 a.m. ET). The “Brazil Presidential Election” market has drawn about US$187 million in total bets, and our Brazil election odds page tracks them.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

Polymarket Flávio Bolsonaro 80.8% · Lula 19.5% (US$187 million traded) Kalshi (regulated in the US by the CFTC) Flávio Bolsonaro 80% · Lula 20% As of 18 October, 7:40 am ET (12:40 Lisbon), updated every 20 minutes. Prices are bets, not polls, and can move fast. Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What Is Not Known

The court has not said whether other supporter channels will be reviewed or whether the new criteria will be applied to channels already online. It is also not known how Meta will respond to the order or whether the fine will ever be enforced.

Neither ruling measures any effect on voters, and polls remain the guide to the race. Our Brazil election polls tracker lists every survey.

More: Brazil news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

What new rules did Brazil’s electoral court approve?

On Friday 16 October, the TSE unanimously approved criteria for when a supporters’ messaging channel counts as part of a campaign. One objectively verifiable sign, such as campaign funding or guidance, can be enough.

Why did the court act now?

Judges had issued conflicting rulings on the WhatsApp channel “Exército do Lula”. The runoff is on Sunday 25 October, so the court wanted clear rules for the final week.

What did the court order Meta to do?

On 15 October, Judge Marco Aurélio Bellizze ordered Meta not to restrict presidential candidates’ reach unequally. Non-compliance carries a fine of R$500,000 (about US$99,000) a day.

When is Brazil’s runoff?

Brazilians vote on Sunday 25 October. The candidates are President Lula and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro.

World.content:
RT Ask Rio Times This story and the bigger picture. Ask Answers are generated from Rio Times reporting only — every claim links to its source article. BRAZIL · ELECTIONS

Published Sunday, 18 October, 5:34 AM ET · Source: Vox Brasil, registered with the electoral court (TSE) as BR-04332/2026

Key Facts The country Brazil, Latin America’s largest country, elects its president in a runoff on Sunday 25 October between President Lula and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro.

What happened Vox Brasil, a Brazilian polling institute, published a runoff survey that puts Lula narrowly ahead in a technical tie.

The numbers Lula has 51% of valid votes and Flávio Bolsonaro 49%, while raw totals read 46.4% to 44.6%.

Margin of error 2.15 percentage points at 95% confidence, so the 1.8-point raw gap is inside the margin.

Fieldwork 2,100 voters aged 16 or older, interviewed from 15 to 17 October.

Power Index Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 75.0 points (October 2026 edition).

Prediction markets Polymarket gives Flávio Bolsonaro an 80.8% chance of winning the 25 October runoff (18 October, 5:33 a.m. ET). Polymarket puts Flávio Bolsonaro’s chance of winning at 81% and Kalshi at 80% (Lula: 20% and 22% ), as of 18 October, 9:40 am ET ; prices are bets, not polls.

Still open Most other recent surveys, including Datafolha and Quaest, have Flávio ahead by the same 51% to 49% margin.

Vox Brasil, a Brazilian polling institute, put Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, Brazil’s president, at 51% and Flávio Bolsonaro, senator for Rio de Janeiro, at 49% of valid votes in a runoff survey reported from 11:01 p.m. ET on Saturday 17 October. The result keeps the Brazil election 2026 race a technical tie.

The vote on Sunday 25 October decides who runs Latin America’s largest economy, which matters for Brazilian stocks, the real and trade with Washington. Our Brazil election polls tracker lists every survey, our Brazil election odds page follows the betting markets, and the Brazil runoff date page explains how to follow the count.

What the Vox Brasil Poll Found

Vox Brasil Opinião e Pesquisas interviewed 2,100 voters aged 16 or older from 15 to 17 October, with a 2.15-point margin of error and a 95% confidence level, Metrópoles and tmc.com.br reported. The survey is registered with the electoral court under number BR-04332/2026.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Brazil ranks 1st of 14 with 75.0 points. Strongest pillar: military means (100); weakest: state capacity & security (56). Alignment group: Hedging. WatchRating below investment grade (BB); public debt at 93% of GDP. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

Lula has 46.4% and Flávio Bolsonaro 44.6% of all answers, with 5% blank, null or for neither and 3.9% undecided, according to Metrópoles. Once those answers are set aside, the split is 51% to 49% in Lula’s favour.

Voters were also asked whom they would never back, and 45.3% named Lula and 45.3% named Flávio, Metrópoles reported. Rejection is a measure of how many voters a candidate cannot win over.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

How It Compares With Earlier Surveys

The institute’s previous runoff survey, taken from 5 to 7 October, had Lula at 44.2% and Flávio at 42.7% of all answers, Correio da Manhã reported. The raw gap is therefore 1.8 points now against 1.5 points then, a change well inside the margin of error.

Both candidates gained as undecided voters fell from 9.7% to 3.9%, while blank and null answers rose from 3.4% to 5%. The shift shows more voters choosing a side as the vote approaches.

Other pollsters see the race the other way round. Datafolha, linked to the newspaper Folha de S.Paulo, had Flávio at 51% and Lula at 49% of valid votes, Jornal Opção reported, and O Povo reported the same split from Quaest.

Our earlier report on the Datafolha runoff poll explains how valid votes and technical ties work.

What It Means for US Readers

If you hold Brazilian stocks, bonds or US-listed shares of Brazilian companies, polls that disagree on the leader can mean price swings until the result is known. A single survey does not settle the race, and the 2-point gaps in most polls sit inside their margins of error.

If you follow US politics or trade, the winner will set Brazil’s course with Washington for the next four years. Read the average of all polls, not one survey, and treat each result as a snapshot of the days of the interviews.

What Prediction Markets Say

On Polymarket, an online prediction market, bettors give Flávio Bolsonaro an 80.8% chance of winning the 25 October runoff, against 19.5% for Lula (18 October, 5:33 a.m. ET). The “Brazil Presidential Election” market has drawn about US$186.9 million in total bets.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

Prediction markets · who wins the runoff Implied chance of winning Brazil’s presidency on 25 October, from traders’ prices. Polymarket Flávio Bolsonaro 80.8% · Lula 19.5% (US$187 million traded) Kalshi (regulated in the US by the CFTC) Flávio Bolsonaro 80% · Lula 22% As of 18 October, 9:40 am ET (14:40 Lisbon), updated every 20 minutes. Prices are bets, not polls, and can move fast. Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What Is Not Known

The institute’s full questionnaire was not available to us, and Metrópoles does not state the interview method. Neither detail is known to change the headline figures.

It is not known how undecided and swing voters will behave on 25 October, or how many will turn out. Any poll measures opinion on the days of the interviews and does not forecast the result.

More: Brazil news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who leads Brazil’s latest Vox Brasil runoff poll?

Lula leads with 51% of valid votes against 49% for Flávio Bolsonaro. Raw totals are 46.4% to 44.6%, which is a technical tie.

What is the margin of error of the Vox Brasil poll?

It is 2.15 percentage points at a 95% confidence level, with 2,100 voters interviewed from 15 to 17 October. The 1.8-point raw gap between the candidates is inside that margin.

How did the Vox Brasil poll change from the previous one?

On 5 to 7 October the institute had Lula at 44.2% and Flávio at 42.7% of all answers. Undecided voters have since fallen from 9.7% to 3.9%.

Do other polls agree with Vox Brasil?

Not on the leader. Datafolha and Quaest both have Flávio Bolsonaro ahead 51% to 49% in valid votes.

When is Brazil’s runoff?

Brazilians vote on Sunday 25 October 2026, one week after this poll was published. The winner takes office as president for a four-year term.

World.title: Public auction at Belmopan Aggregates and Hardware set for October 28
World.content:
Public auction at Belmopan Aggregates and Hardware set for October 28

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): Belmopan Aggregates and Hardware is hosting a public auction of industrial equipment, commercial tools, generators, office machinery and surplus supplies.

The auction takes place on Wednesday, October 28, starting at 8:00am at Belmopan Aggregates and Hardware in Belmopan. Everything will go to the highest bidder. Terms are cash, and food and drinks will be available on site.

Among the highlights is a wide range of power equipment, including a Katolight 125kW diesel generator, a Cummins 40kW diesel generator, Generac commercial and standby generators from 9kW to 222kW, Generac and Honda portable generators, and ASCO transfer switches.

Heavy equipment and shop tools include a Mitsubishi electric forklift, a John Deere backhoe extender attachment, Delta and Powermatic industrial table saws, a wood lathe, an electric pallet jack and hydraulic cylinders.

Also up for auction are large format printers, commercial food prep equipment, new pressure washers, a new air compressor, a 54 inch walk behind mower, appliances, furniture, electric scooters, solar batteries, building materials and much more.

The auctioneer is Henry B. Dueck, who can be reached at 610 0158. For enquiries, contact Frans Blatz at 615 9646.

World.title: NASA Satellites track warming Pacific waters as El Niño develops
World.content:
NASA Satellites track warming Pacific waters as El Niño develops

By Zoila Palma: NASA satellites are tracking signs of El Niño in the Pacific Ocean, including rising sea surface temperatures and changes in ocean levels and colour.

According to NASA, one of the first indicators appeared in January 2026, when a wave of warm water known as a Kelvin wave was detected near Micronesia in the western Pacific. By early April, the waves had reached the eastern Pacific, contributing to warmer ocean temperatures and rising sea levels in some areas.

Kelvin waves transport heat across the Pacific Ocean, helping trigger a chain reaction that weakens the trade winds and allows warm water to accumulate farther east. NASA reported that sea levels in parts of the eastern Pacific rose by approximately 1 to 1.3 feet, while levels around Indonesia and northern Australia were 6 to 8 inches below normal.

NASA data also show that sea surface temperatures in the eastern Pacific are approximately 3 degrees Fahrenheit, or 1.7 degrees Celsius, above the long-term average, with the possibility of further warming in the coming months. These temperature changes are significant because ocean heat influences atmospheric conditions, affecting rainfall and weather patterns around the world.

Another sign of El Niño is a change in the ocean’s colour as populations of microscopic marine plants known as phytoplankton decline in some equatorial Pacific waters.

NASA says that its scientists will continue monitoring El Niño through its fleet of Earth-observing satellites to better understand the phenomenon and its potential effects.

World.title: Flood alert remains in effect as continued rains affect Belize
World.content:
Flood alert remains in effect as continued rains affect Belize

By Zoila Palma: A flood alert remains in effect across Belize as additional rainfall is expected over the weekend.

The National Meteorological Service (NMS) forecasts between 2 and 4 inches of rain in portions of the country over on Sunday.

Residents in low-lying, flood-prone and riverside communities are urged to remain alert and monitor official weather updates.

The NMS warns that smaller streams and tributaries could rise quickly.

Although several rivers remain at normal or below-normal levels, conditions could change rapidly as rainfall accumulates.

Residents are advised to exercise caution near rivers, streams and low-level crossings and never attempt to cross flooded roads or waterways.

World.title: National Fire Service honors 27 officers for long service
World.content:
National Fire Service honors 27 officers for long service

By Zoila Palma: The National Fire Service (NFS) has recognized 27 officers for their years of dedicated service in protecting lives, safeguarding property and responding to emergencies across Belize.

The awards ceremony was held in Belize City on October 16, 2026, under the Ministry of the Public Service, Disaster Risk Management and Enterprise.

The ceremony celebrated the commitment and contributions of officers who have dedicated years of their careers to public safety and supporting communities during emergencies. Their service reflects the important role the NFS plays in providing emergency response services and protecting Belizeans throughout the country.

Among those recognized were Assistant Divisional Officer Kenneth Mortis and Station Officer Brenton Gentle, who each completed 30 years of service. Retired Station Officer Miguel Medina was also honoured for completing 20 years of service. Their years of experience and dedication highlight the commitment required to serve in the National Fire Service.

Minister of the Public Service, Disaster Risk Management and Enterprise, Henry Charles Usher, emphasized the importance of recognizing officers who have devoted their careers to serving and protecting the people of Belize. “Today, we honour not only the years these officers have given, but also the important contribution they have made to our nation,” Usher said.

World.title: International News: Police and protesters clash across France in major unrest over cost of living
World.content:
International News: Police and protesters clash across France in major unrest over cost of living

By Zoila Palma: Violent clashes erupted between police and protesters across France today as hundreds of thousands of people reportedly took to the streets to demonstrate against rising living costs, inequality and declining public services.

The unrest, described as some of the country’s most destructive in years, resulted in at least 272 arrests, according to France’s Interior Ministry, following incidents in Paris, Marseille, Toulouse, Angers and Lyon, Reuters report.

The CGT union estimated that 800,000 people participated in the demonstrations, although the Interior Ministry did not provide its own estimate.

Protesters said many marches were peaceful and blamed the violence on individuals who joined to cause damage and confront police. In Paris, officers deployed tear gas as clashes intensified, while shops and restaurants were damaged, vehicles and trash cans were set on fire, and several central areas experienced disruption. In Lyon, protesters set fire to the tourist office, while Marseille’s mayor reported vandalism at the town hall.

French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said the government would not be intimidated by the violence, accusing the far-left and criminals of exploiting the demonstrations ahead of next year’s presidential election.

Meanwhile, protests over rising costs also took place in other European countries today.

World.title: Belize celebrates International Day of Living Heritage
World.content:
Belize celebrates International Day of Living Heritage

By Zoila Palma: Belize joined the global observance of the International Day of Living Heritage, celebrating the traditions, knowledge, skills and cultural practices that connect communities and help shape the country’s national identity.

The observance highlights the importance of preserving Belize’s rich intangible cultural heritage, including the customs and practices passed down through generations. These traditions continue to play an important role in strengthening community connections and maintaining Belize’s diverse cultural identity.

Through community-driven initiatives across the country, efforts are being made to place living heritage at the heart of national development, NICH noted.

NICH also expressed gratitude to its national and international partners and collaborators for their continued support in protecting and promoting the country’s living heritage.

World.title: International News: Taiwan promotes Educational exchanges and talent development partnerships in Latin America
World.content:
International News: Taiwan promotes Educational exchanges and talent development partnerships in Latin America

By Zoila Palma: Taiwan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) is strengthening educational exchanges and cooperation with Latin America through initiatives aimed at developing talent, encouraging innovation and expanding economic partnerships.

MOFA Deputy Minister Chen Ming-chi hosted a welcome luncheon for students participating in the Executive Master’s in Asia-Pacific and Latin American Studies at Tamkang University’s Department of Global Politics and Economics.

Chen thanked the university for its longstanding efforts to promote exchanges with Latin America and highlighted Taiwan’s continued investment in education, talent development and emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence.

Chen also pointed to initiatives such as the Taiwan-Paraguay Polytechnic University project and Taiwan’s support for Taiwanese businesses seeking to expand internationally. He noted that these partnerships can help Taiwan’s diplomatic allies develop new industries through mutually beneficial cooperation. He encouraged the visiting students to explore opportunities for collaboration between Taiwan and their respective home countries during their stay.

Student representative Lorena Yael Piedra Cobo of Ecuador thanked MOFA and Tamkang University for organizing the academic courses and activities.

World.title: Belize City Council, IDB explore plans to revitalize historic Downtown
World.content:
Belize City Council, IDB explore plans to revitalize historic Downtown

By Zoila Palma: The Belize City Council is continuing discussions with the Inter-American Development Bank (IDB) on a proposed comprehensive program to revitalize historic downtown Belize City, with plans being explored to improve public spaces, support businesses and preserve the city’s historic character.

The proposed revitalization area includes the Albert and Regent Street corridors, stretching from the Swing Bridge toward the House of Culture and surrounding historic centre.

Ideas under discussion include cleaning and repainting building façades, improving sidewalks and public spaces, updating traffic signs and making sections of downtown more pedestrian-friendly.

A possible pedestrian route could connect the Swing Bridge with the market, courthouse area and City Hall, while a waterfront boardwalk along the southern coast toward the House of Culture has also been discussed.

The Council and IDB have also explored ways to make better use of vacant or underused lots and encourage more people to live in the downtown area. The IDB’s “IDB for Cities and Regions” program was discussed as a potential avenue for supporting future investment. However, the Council emphasized that discussions remain at an early stage and that the scope of any project has not been finalized.

Any future program would require careful assessment of its costs, the City Council’s financial and legal capacity, and coordination with national partners.

The proposed downtown rejuvenation aims to create more inviting public spaces, support local businesses and protect Belize City’s heritage while making the historic centre a more attractive place to visit, work and live.

World.title: INSIDE THE SLIGOVILLE STAND-OFF
World.content:
Police are seen on the road leading to the house off the Sligoville main road in St Catherine where three men were killed in an alleged shoot-out with members of the security forces last Friday morning.

“POLICE, we a go pull the door, just wait nuh. Mi nuh waan dead enuh!”

One of the children inside the ill-fated house in the Five Miles area off the Sligoville main road in St Catherine shouted these words as she and two other occupants of the premises seemingly negotiated with law enforcers to cease their gunfire so they could exit the house last Friday amid a stand-off with alleged gunmen inside the building.

A video recording seen by the Jamaica Observer captured some of what was happening inside the house while law enforcers were outside. The 18-minute 25-second video was captured during a WhatsApp video call with relatives during Friday morning’s daring gun battle. The video cuts out for much of the recording, with an onscreen notification saying “video paused”, but the audio can still be heard.

The child, who the Sunday Observer has been told is the 10-year-old girl who was injured in the incident, is heard appealing to one of the occupants of the house to open the door.
